# Browser Dual-Engine Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make obscura Aleph's default browser engine and Chromium its escape hatch, both driven through one Aleph-owned CDP client, with an Aleph-derived page-state tree (text + geometry) as the model's default observation and a model-decided engine switch that carries cookies and URLs across.

**Architecture:** `crates/aleph-cdp` (zero-Aleph-dependency CDP transport: one websocket, many sessions, per-command timeout) → `src/browser/engine/` (engine enum, `EngineProcess` launch/kill trait with `ChromiumChild` moved in and `ObscuraChild` added, sidecar + orphan sweep lifted from `chromium_launch.rs`, capability table, readiness gate) → `src/browser/cdp_backend/` (ONE `BrowserBackend` impl for both engines, branching on engine only at geometry fetch / JS dialogs / hit-test) → `src/browser/page_state/` (`RawDom` from two fetchers → ONE `PageState::build` → text render + JSON + `RefTable` with generations). Tool faces (26 tools) unchanged except `browser_session{switch_engine}` and `browser_open{engine}`. Both engines are install-time external runtimes managed by the runtime ledger (a new `InstallStrategy::GithubRelease`).

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2021 (MSRV 1.95, toolchain pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`), tokio, `tokio-tungstenite 0.26` (already in tree), serde/serde_json, `async-trait` (already used by `BrowserBackend`), schemars, proptest (already in tree). No new third-party crates.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-design.md` (committed at `0a3e8a48a` on branch `worktree-browser-dual-engine`). Evidence: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-evidence/` — read `aleph-browser-map.md` (file:line anchors at `c049ef1ed`; re-verify at HEAD `7883799e6`, main merged a browser live-view + Windows shell round after the map was made) and `obscura-spike-v022.md` before writing any code.

## Global Constraints

- **Worktree**: all work in `/Volumes/TBU4/Workspace/Aleph/.claude/worktrees/browser-dual-engine` on branch `worktree-browser-dual-engine`. Never `cd` to the main checkout. Submodules `skills/`, `plugins/` are initialised (needed by `include_dir!`).
- **Cargo target dir**: every cargo invocation MUST be prefixed `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Volumes/TBU4/Workspace/aleph-target-dual-engine` (the main checkout's per-machine `.cargo/config.toml` points at an absolute shared target; sharing it with another session's builds is the phantom-binary hazard recorded in memory). Long builds (>3 min) run in the background with output to a log file; never rely on the tool timeout.
- **Verification set** (CLAUDE.md "最小可信验证集"), run at the end of every task that touches Rust, all with the target-dir prefix:
  `cargo test -p alephcore --lib --no-run` · `cargo test -p alephcore --bins` · `cargo test -p alephcore --features test-helpers --test '*' --no-run` · `cargo test -p aleph-panel --lib --no-run` · `cargo check -p aleph-desktop-macos` (and `-windows`/`-linux` for any `cfg` change) · `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` (needs `just _stage-shell-placeholders` first). Plus the named unit tests of the task, run unfiltered for the crate at least once per stage.
- **Redlines**: R1 (no platform API in `src/`), R3 (no new heavy crate — `chromiumoxide` is explicitly rejected), R7/R10 (no deterministic engine routing, no auto-escalation, `src/harness/` untouched — measure `src/harness/tests/budget.rs::CEILING` before and after the branch and record both numbers), R8 (every knob is a tool), R9 (capability prose lives in the owning tool's `DESCRIPTION`, derived from the capability constant).
- **Spec constants**: `cdp_command_timeout_secs` default **30** and must be `< 60` (obscura's `OBSCURA_CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` guillotine); obscura ledger tag **`v0.2.2`** until the upstream PR lands; obscura archive variant `default` (with render) — never `no-render`; `--allow-file-access` is never passed; `--allow-private-network` only when the profile's network policy allows private ranges.
- **Config compatibility**: existing serde names of `BrowserDriver` variants and `BrowserType` are frozen; legacy `driver` values imply `engine=chromium`; `BrowserType` gets NO `Obscura` variant; `[general.browser.runtime]` section name unchanged; missing config = product defaults, corrupt config = error (never conflate).
- **Errors**: fail-closed. `Err`/`None`/empty means "unknown", never "healthy"/"visible"/"allowed". Error texts name the recovery verb (`browser_session{switch_engine}`, `runtime_manage{install}`, "re-run browser_snapshot").
- **Commit format**: `<scope>: <description>` in English (e.g. `browser: add cdp backend tab table`), body explains why; end with the two trailers exactly:
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01S5svp72kD47JA4KDx7zv2G`. Commit after every task's green; never `git stash` bare (shared stash stack).
- **Search**: run `graphify query "<question>"` (from the worktree root) before grepping; use `rg`, not `grep`. Use `cargo test <filter>` with ONE positional filter. `rustfmt <mod.rs>` recurses into declared children — format only the files you touched (`rustfmt path/to/file.rs`), never `cargo fmt -p alephcore` (rewrites ~100 unrelated files).
- **QA scripts** follow `qa/<name>/run.sh <stage>` with `qa/lib/scratch_home.sh` (scratch `$HOME`, fake API key so `tools.invoke` is not in Simulated mode — see `qa/README.md`), assert EFFECTS (URL changed, cookie present, process gone), and every guard must be shown red once by mutation before it counts.
- **Tests**: TDD per task (write failing test → run → implement → run → commit). Census/grep tests use `include_str!`/`std::fs` reads of production sources, strip comment lines before counting, and assert exact counts.
- **Docs**: FEATURE_LOCATOR §3.12 gets ONE new round entry (Task 19); 附录 E gains rows only for NEW shapes; never duplicate spec prose into CLAUDE.md.

## Canonical Interfaces (every writer uses EXACTLY these names/signatures; if HEAD forces a change, write the change into the task's "Interfaces" block and tell the controller)

```rust
// ===== crates/aleph-cdp =====
pub struct SessionId(pub String);
pub struct TargetId(pub String);
#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct ConnectOptions { pub command_timeout: std::time::Duration }
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct CdpConnection { inner: std::sync::Arc<Inner> }
impl CdpConnection {
    pub async fn connect(ws_url: &str, opts: ConnectOptions) -> Result<CdpConnection, CdpError>;
    pub async fn call(&self, session: Option<&SessionId>, method: &str, params: serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, CdpError>;
    pub async fn call_with_timeout(&self, session: Option<&SessionId>, method: &str, params: serde_json::Value, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<serde_json::Value, CdpError>;
    pub fn events(&self) -> EventStream;
    pub async fn attach(&self, target: &TargetId) -> Result<SessionId, CdpError>;
    pub async fn detach(&self, session: &SessionId) -> Result<(), CdpError>;
    pub fn closed(&self) -> tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<Option<CloseReason>>;
    pub async fn close(&self);
    pub fn command_timeout(&self) -> std::time::Duration;
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct CdpEvent { pub session: Option<SessionId>, pub method: String, pub params: serde_json::Value }
pub struct EventStream { rx: tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<std::sync::Arc<CdpEvent>>, lagged: u64 }
impl EventStream { pub async fn next(&mut self) -> Option<std::sync::Arc<CdpEvent>>; pub fn lagged(&self) -> u64; }
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)] pub enum CdpError {
    #[error("cdp {method}: {code} {message}")] Protocol { method: String, code: i64, message: String, data: Option<serde_json::Value> },
    #[error("cdp {method} timed out after {waited:?}")] Timeout { method: String, waited: std::time::Duration },
    #[error("cdp connection closed: {0:?}")] Disconnected(CloseReason),
    #[error("cdp transport: {0}")] Transport(String),
    #[error("cdp decode: {0}")] Decode(String),
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum CloseReason { PeerClosed, TransportError(String), LocalClose }

// methods:: (all `pub async fn name(conn: &CdpConnection, session: Option<&SessionId>, ...) -> Result<T, CdpError>`)
pub mod methods {
  pub mod browser { pub struct BrowserVersion { pub product: String, pub user_agent: String, pub protocol_version: String } pub async fn get_version(conn) -> Result<BrowserVersion>; }
  pub mod target { pub struct TargetInfo { pub target_id: TargetId, pub r#type: String, pub title: String, pub url: String, pub attached: bool }
                   pub async fn create_target(conn, url: &str) -> Result<TargetId>; pub async fn get_targets(conn) -> Result<Vec<TargetInfo>>; pub async fn close_target(conn, &TargetId) -> Result<bool>; pub async fn activate_target(conn, &TargetId) -> Result<()>; pub async fn set_discover_targets(conn, bool) -> Result<()>; }
  pub mod page   { pub struct NavigateResult { pub frame_id: String, pub loader_id: Option<String>, pub error_text: Option<String> }
                   pub struct LayoutMetrics { pub css_visual_viewport: VisualViewport { pub page_x: f64, pub page_y: f64, pub client_width: f64, pub client_height: f64, pub scale: f64 }, pub css_content_size: Size { pub width: f64, pub height: f64 } }
                   pub enum ScreenshotFormat { Png, Jpeg { quality: u8 } }
                   pub struct HistoryEntry { pub id: i64, pub url: String, pub title: String }
                   pub async fn enable(conn, s) ; pub async fn navigate(conn, s, url: &str) -> Result<NavigateResult>; pub async fn reload(conn, s, ignore_cache: bool); pub async fn get_layout_metrics(conn, s) -> Result<LayoutMetrics>;
                   pub async fn capture_screenshot(conn, s, fmt: ScreenshotFormat, capture_beyond_viewport: bool) -> Result<Vec<u8>>; pub async fn print_to_pdf(conn, s) -> Result<Vec<u8>>;
                   pub async fn get_navigation_history(conn, s) -> Result<(usize, Vec<HistoryEntry>)>; pub async fn navigate_to_history_entry(conn, s, entry_id: i64);
                   pub async fn handle_javascript_dialog(conn, s, accept: bool, prompt_text: Option<&str>); pub async fn bring_to_front(conn, s); }
  pub mod dom    { pub struct Node { pub node_id: i64, pub backend_node_id: i64, pub node_type: i64, pub node_name: String, pub node_value: String, pub attributes: Vec<String>, pub children: Vec<Node>, pub shadow_roots: Vec<Node>, pub content_document: Option<Box<Node>>, pub frame_id: Option<String> }
                   pub struct BoxModel { pub content: [f64; 8], pub padding: [f64; 8], pub border: [f64; 8], pub margin: [f64; 8], pub width: i64, pub height: i64 }
                   pub async fn get_document(conn, s, depth: i64, pierce: bool) -> Result<Node>; pub async fn query_selector(conn, s, node_id: i64, selector: &str) -> Result<Option<i64>>; pub async fn query_selector_all(conn, s, node_id: i64, selector: &str) -> Result<Vec<i64>>;
                   pub async fn resolve_node(conn, s, backend_node_id: i64) -> Result<String /*objectId*/>; pub async fn get_box_model(conn, s, backend_node_id: i64) -> Result<Option<BoxModel>> /* Ok(None) on "Could not compute box model" */;
                   pub async fn scroll_into_view_if_needed(conn, s, backend_node_id: i64); pub async fn describe_node(conn, s, backend_node_id: i64) -> Result<Node>; pub async fn set_file_input_files(conn, s, backend_node_id: i64, files: &[String]); pub async fn focus(conn, s, backend_node_id: i64); }
  pub mod runtime{ pub struct EvalResult { pub value: serde_json::Value, pub exception: Option<String> }
                   pub async fn enable(conn, s); pub async fn evaluate(conn, s, expression: &str, await_promise: bool) -> Result<EvalResult> /* returnByValue:true always */; pub async fn call_function_on(conn, s, object_id: &str, declaration: &str, args: Vec<serde_json::Value>) -> Result<EvalResult>; }
  pub mod input  { pub enum MouseType { Pressed, Released, Moved, Wheel } pub enum MouseButton { None, Left, Right, Middle }
                   pub struct MouseEvent { pub r#type: MouseType, pub x: f64, pub y: f64, pub button: MouseButton, pub click_count: u32, pub modifiers: u32, pub delta_x: f64, pub delta_y: f64 }

                   pub async fn dispatch_mouse_event(conn, s, ev: &MouseEvent); pub async fn dispatch_key_event(conn, s, ev: &KeyEvent); pub async fn insert_text(conn, s, text: &str); }
  pub mod network{ pub struct Cookie { pub name: String, pub value: String, pub domain: String, pub path: String, pub expires: Option<f64>, pub http_only: bool, pub secure: bool, pub same_site: Option<String> }

  pub mod emulation { pub async fn set_device_metrics_override(conn, s, width: u32, height: u32, dpr: f64, mobile: bool); pub async fn clear_device_metrics_override(conn, s); pub async fn set_user_agent_override(conn, s, ua: &str); pub async fn set_geolocation_override(conn, s, lat: f64, lon: f64, accuracy: f64); }
  pub mod dom_snapshot { pub struct DomSnapshot { pub raw: serde_json::Value } /* typed accessors: documents(), strings() */ pub async fn capture_snapshot(conn, s, computed_styles: &[&str], include_dom_rects: bool, include_paint_order: bool) -> Result<DomSnapshot>; }
}

// ===== src/browser/engine =====
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] pub enum Engine { Obscura, Chromium }
impl Engine { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Engine>; pub fn data_subdir(self) -> &'static str /* "chromium" | "obscura" */ }

#[async_trait::async_trait] pub trait EngineProcess: Send + Sync {
    fn engine(&self) -> Engine;
    async fn launch(&self, req: LaunchRequest) -> Result<Launched, BrowserError>;
    async fn kill(&self, pid: u32, grace: std::time::Duration) -> Result<bool /*died*/, BrowserError>;
}
pub struct LaunchRequest { pub profile: String, pub session_key: String, pub data_dir: std::path::PathBuf, pub headless: bool, pub proxy: Option<String>, pub allow_private_network: bool, pub stealth: bool, pub extra_args: Vec<String> }
pub struct Launched { pub pid: u32, pub endpoint: CdpEndpoint, pub sidecar_path: std::path::PathBuf }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)] pub struct CdpEndpoint { pub http_url: String, pub ws_url: String, pub pid: u32 }   // moved from chromium_launch.rs, same fields
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)] pub struct EngineSidecar { #[serde(default = "Engine::chromium_default")] pub engine: Engine, pub pid: u32, pub http_url: Option<String>, pub data_dir: std::path::PathBuf, pub build: String }
pub fn sidecar_registry_dir() -> std::path::PathBuf; pub fn sidecar_path(session_key: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf;
pub fn reap_orphans(registry: &std::path::Path, argv_of: &dyn Fn(u32) -> ArgvProbe, kill: &dyn Fn(u32) -> bool) -> ReapOutcome;   // moved, engine-aware match on data_dir flag per engine
pub async fn shutdown_all(handles: Vec<std::sync::Arc<EngineHandle>>);

pub struct EngineHandle { pub engine: Engine, pub profile: String, pub launched: Launched, pub conn: aleph_cdp::CdpConnection, pub tabs: tokio::sync::Mutex<TabTable>, process: std::sync::Arc<dyn EngineProcess> }
pub struct TabTable { pub entries: std::collections::HashMap<String /*TabId=targetId*/, TabEntry>, pub active: Option<String> }
pub struct TabEntry { pub session: aleph_cdp::SessionId, pub refs: crate::browser::page_state::RefTable, pub generation: u64, pub console: std::collections::VecDeque<String>, pub network: std::collections::VecDeque<String>, pub pending_dialog: Option<String> }
impl EngineHandle { pub fn alive(&self) -> bool; pub async fn shutdown(&self); pub async fn ensure_tab(&self, tab_id: &str) -> Result<aleph_cdp::SessionId, BrowserError>; }

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum Cap { Supported, Partial, Unsupported }
pub struct EngineCapabilities { pub js_dialogs: Cap, pub drag: Cap, pub touch: Cap, pub file_upload: Cap, pub pdf: Cap, pub screencast: Cap, pub multi_connection: Cap, pub network_interception: Cap, pub insert_text: Cap, pub measured_on: &'static str }
pub const fn capabilities(engine: Engine) -> &'static EngineCapabilities;
pub fn describe_for_tool() -> String;   // deterministic prose derived from both tables; used in browser_session DESCRIPTION
pub async fn ready_gate(conn: &aleph_cdp::CdpConnection, session: &aleph_cdp::SessionId, budget: std::time::Duration) -> Result<(), BrowserError>;

// ===== src/browser/page_state =====
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct Rect { pub x: i32, pub y: i32, pub w: i32, pub h: i32 }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct Viewport { pub width: u32, pub height: u32, pub scroll_x: i32, pub scroll_y: i32, pub content_width: u32, pub content_height: u32, pub dpr: f64 }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct Computed { pub display_none: bool, pub visibility_hidden: bool, pub opacity_zero: bool, pub cursor_pointer: bool, pub overflow_clip: bool }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub enum RawNodeKind { Document, Element, Text, Other }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct RawNode { pub backend_node_id: u64, pub parent: Option<usize>, pub kind: RawNodeKind, pub tag: Option<String>, pub attrs: Vec<(String, String)>, pub text: Option<String>, pub rect: Option<Rect>, pub computed: Option<Computed>, pub shadow_root: bool, pub clickable_hint: Option<bool> }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct RawFrame { pub frame_id: String, pub loader_id: String, pub offset: (i32, i32), pub nodes: Vec<RawNode> }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct RawDom { pub engine: Engine, pub viewport: Viewport, pub frames: Vec<RawFrame> }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct RefId(pub String);
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)] pub struct RefKey { pub frame_id: String, pub loader_id: String, pub backend_node_id: u64 }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct FrameKey { pub frame_id: String, pub loader_id: String }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum StaleReason { Navigated, NodeGone, Unknown }
pub struct RefEntry { pub key: RefKey, pub minted_generation: u64 }
#[derive(Default)] pub struct RefTable { .. }
impl RefTable { pub fn new() -> Self; pub fn mint(&mut self, key: &RefKey, generation: u64) -> RefId; pub fn resolve(&self, r: &RefId) -> Result<RefEntry, StaleReason>; pub fn reset_for_document(&mut self, main_loader_id: &str); pub fn document(&self) -> Option<&str>; pub fn len(&self) -> usize; }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")] pub enum Role { Link, Button, Textbox, Checkbox, Radio, Combobox, Listbox, Option, Menu, MenuItem, Tab, Heading, Image, Banner, Main, Navigation, Contentinfo, List, ListItem, Table, Row, Cell, Article, Form, Dialog, Generic, Text }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct NodeStates { pub disabled: bool, pub checked: Option<bool>, pub expanded: Option<bool>, pub selected: bool, pub required: bool, pub readonly: bool, pub focused: bool }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct StateNode { pub parent: Option<usize>, pub r#ref: Option<RefId>, pub backend_node_id: u64, pub frame: FrameKey, pub role: Role, pub name: String, pub value: Option<String>, pub states: NodeStates, pub rect: Option<Rect>, pub interactive: bool, pub visible: bool, pub text: Option<String>, pub href: Option<String>, pub placeholder: Option<String> }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct PageState { pub engine: Engine, pub generation: u64, pub url: String, pub title: String, pub viewport: Viewport, pub no_box: (usize, usize), pub waited_secs: u64, pub nodes: Vec<StateNode> }
impl PageState { pub fn build(raw: &RawDom, refs: &mut RefTable, generation: u64, url: &str, title: &str, waited: std::time::Duration) -> PageState; pub fn ref_count(&self) -> usize; }
pub fn render_text(state: &PageState) -> String;   // header line + one line per visible node; never emits "\n" inside a node line
pub fn to_json(state: &PageState) -> serde_json::Value;
pub async fn fetch_chromium(conn: &CdpConnection, session: &SessionId) -> Result<RawDom, BrowserError>;
pub async fn fetch_obscura(conn: &CdpConnection, session: &SessionId, box_concurrency: usize) -> Result<RawDom, BrowserError>;
pub const PAGE_STATE_MIME: &str = "application/vnd.aleph.page-state+json";

BrowserError::EngineBusy { engine: Engine, method: String, waited_secs: u64 }
```

# Tasks

## Part 1 — Stage T0 + S1 — verification probes and the aleph-cdp crate (Tasks 0–4)

### Part 1 deviations (skeleton → HEAD)

1. **skeleton says** `crates/aleph-cdp` depends on `url` → **HEAD/API forces** dropping it, because
   `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async` takes anything implementing `IntoClientRequest` and `&str`
   implements it (`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/tokio-tungstenite-0.26.2/src/connect.rs`); the crate never
   parses a URL itself. An unused dependency in a crate whose whole point is "zero extra weight"
   contradicts R3/P6, so `url` is not declared.
2. **skeleton says** dev-dependency `proptest` → **dropped**. Nothing in Tasks 1–4 is a property:
   id correlation is asserted exactly (a fixed out-of-order script), and the lag counter has one
   exact expected value. `proptest 1.4` stays where the workspace already declares it
   (`Cargo.toml:363`, alephcore's `[dev-dependencies]`) for Task 10's `render_text` line-shape
   property.
3. **skeleton does not list** `base64` → **added** as `base64 = "0.22"`, because the skeleton types
   `methods::page::capture_screenshot` and `print_to_pdf` as `-> Result<Vec<u8>, CdpError>` and CDP
   returns those as base64 strings. `base64 = "0.22"` is already resolved in this workspace
   (`Cargo.toml:79`), so this adds no new third-party surface — it only adds an edge to a crate the
   lockfile already carries.
4. **skeleton puts** `src/events.rs` in Task 3 → **compile order forces** the `CdpEvent` half into
   Task 2: the read loop that Task 2 writes is the only producer of events, so the type it broadcasts
   must exist in the same task. Task 3 keeps everything the skeleton actually gates on it —
   `EventStream`, `CdpConnection::events()`, the lag counter, and `tests/events.rs`. Task 2 therefore
   ships `events.rs` containing only `CdpEvent` + `EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY`, and Task 3's tests are
   genuinely red-first (`no method named events`).
5. **skeleton shows** `#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)] pub enum CdpError` → **also derives**
   `Clone, PartialEq`. `Clone` is load-bearing: when the socket dies, one `CloseReason` has to be
   handed to every pending call at once (`Shared::fail_all`). `PartialEq` lets the tests
   `assert_eq!` on a whole error value instead of matching a shape and then re-reading fields.
6. **skeleton writes** `LayoutMetrics` with anonymous inline structs
   (`pub css_visual_viewport: VisualViewport { pub page_x: f64, … }`) — not valid Rust →
   **named types** `VisualViewport` and `ContentSize` with exactly those fields.
7. **skeleton writes** `methods::*` signatures in shorthand (`conn`, `s`, no argument types) →
   spelled out as `conn: &CdpConnection, session: Option<&SessionId>` everywhere, with the return
   types the skeleton gives.
8. **skeleton says** `FakeCdpServer` lives in `crates/aleph-cdp/tests/support/mod.rs` →
   **controller ruling (2026-09-06) moves it to `crates/aleph-cdp/src/testkit.rs` behind a
   `testkit` cargo feature**, exported as `aleph_cdp::testkit::FakeCdpServer`. A `tests/` module is
   compiled into that crate's own test binaries and is not reachable from any other crate, and
   Tasks 9, 12, 13 and 19 drive `CdpBackend` from `alephcore`'s tests against this same fake. The
   feature keeps it out of production: with `resolver = "2"` (`Cargo.toml:5`) a dev-dependency's
   features are not unified into the normal dependency graph, so `alephcore` taking `aleph-cdp` in
   `[dependencies]` does not pull the fake into `aleph-server`. Task 1 Step 4 verifies that with
   `cargo tree -e features` rather than assuming it. This crate's own tests reach the feature
   through a self dev-dependency (`aleph-cdp = { path = ".", features = ["testkit"] }`) so
   `cargo test -p aleph-cdp` needs no flag; Task 1 Step 3 carries the `required-features` fallback
   and the binary-count check that keeps that fallback from skipping a target silently.
9. **skeleton describes `FakeCdpServer` as `start` + a scripted responder + "records received
   messages"** → **controller ruling (2026-09-06) fixes the API as the union four parts already
   call**, so the fake also serves HTTP on its own port (`GET /json/version`, Chrome-shaped, whose
   `webSocketDebuggerUrl` is its own socket) and gains `http_url`, `host`, `on` (a per-method
   override table consulted *before* the constructor's closure), `shutdown` (stop accepting, close
   every socket, wait for the tasks), `scripted_slow`, `scripted` in both free and associated
   form, and `connect_and_attach`. `ws_url` changes from `-> &str` to `-> String`. Two knock-on
   facts: the accept loop now peeks the request head to tell a websocket handshake from an HTTP
   GET (peek, not read, so tungstenite still sees the handshake whole), and
   `connect_and_attach` cannot exist until `CdpConnection::attach` does, so it is added to the same
   file in **Task 3** rather than Task 1. Everything else in the union ships in Task 1.
10. **skeleton says** `get_box_model` returns `Ok(None)` *on "Could not compute box model"* → the
   constants **stay in production code** (`NO_BOX_CODE` / `NO_BOX_MESSAGE` in `methods::dom`), and a
   Task-4 test asserts they equal the code and message the Task-0 fixture recorded from Chrome, so a
   wrong guess is red rather than silent. The test INPUT also comes from that fixture, replayed
   through the fake server, so neither half is a literal compared with a literal (判据 §1).

**Flagged for the S2 writer (not used by Tasks 0–4):** the skeleton's canonical block says

    **Two fields, because "the wire said ok" and "the page changed" are different facts.** obscura
    answers `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` with `Ok({})` and does nothing at all (source survey,
    `domains/input.rs:413`) — the report-success no-op (判据 §11). A capability row judged on
    `protocol` alone would call that verb supported, ship it in the tool schema, and the model
    would tap a button that is never tapped. `effect` is measured by the page itself: `t0-page.html`
    sets `window.__aleph_touch` / `__aleph_drag` from capture-phase listeners, and the probe reads
    the flag back through `Runtime.evaluate` after dispatching. Measured for the four verbs where a
    silent no-op is plausible — `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`, `Input.dispatchDragEvent`,
    `DOM.setAttributeValue`, `DOM.removeNode` — and `null` everywhere else.
    `effect: false` is written **only** after a flag was successfully read back and was not set. If
    the read itself failed, `effect` stays `null`: "we could not look" is not "nothing happened"
    (判据 §8). The capture report also lists `reportsSuccessButDoesNothing`, the labels where
    `protocol === "ok" && effect === false`, which is the set Task 16 must never mark
    `Cap::Supported`.

    **Keyed by the probe's LABEL, not by the CDP method**, because three
    measurements share `DOM.getBoxModel` and two each share `DOM.querySelector` and
    `Runtime.evaluate`; a method key would let a deliberately provoked refusal overwrite the
    success. Labels are the first argument of `record()` in `t0-capture.mjs`:
    `DOM.getBoxModel`, `DOM.getBoxModel.hidden`, `DOM.getBoxModel.badnode`, `DOM.querySelector`,
    `DOM.querySelector.miss`, `Runtime.evaluate`, `Runtime.evaluate.throws`, and the bare method
    name everywhere else.
    **Consumer (controller ruling, 2026-09-06): Task 16's capability-table test.** It reads this
    file with `include_str!("../../../crates/aleph-cdp/tests/fixtures/t0-support-matrix.json")`
    from a `#[cfg(test)]` module in `src/browser/engine/capability.rs`, and asserts every `Cap` row
    it can check agrees with the measured answer — `Cap::Supported` requires `protocol == "ok"`
    **and** `effect != Some(false)`, `Cap::Unsupported` requires anything else. That is what stops
    the capability table from being prose: a row claiming obscura supports a verb the probe
    recorded a refusal for goes red, and so does a row claiming support for one the probe watched
    do nothing.
    Task 16's writer owns the mapping from `Cap` field to label; Task 0 owns the labels, and any
    label rename is a change both sides see.

**Why the step format below is adapted.** This task produces measurements, not a Rust function, so
"write the failing test" is `t0-check.mjs` — a guard that asserts the fixture set exists, parses,
and carries the keys Tasks 4/11/17 will read. It is red before the probes run and green after, and
it stays in the tree as the thing that catches a fixture someone truncates later.

**Non-negotiables for this task:**
- `--allow-file-access` is never passed to obscura, in the probes or anywhere else (spec §6.2).
- `--allow-private-network` **is** passed here, and only here, because the probe pages are served
  from `127.0.0.1` and obscura's own SSRF floor blocks private ranges by default. The task report
  must say so; production passes it only when the profile's network policy allows private ranges.
- Both engines run against a **local static page** for everything that must be reproducible. Two
  probes touch the network: `t0-hn.mjs` (its output is a frozen snapshot, never re-fetched) and
  the second half of `t0-u9-inline.mjs` (the tie back to the spike's M11 measurement on HN). Both
  are written so an unreachable site is reported as *not measured* and neither takes its local
  half down with it — "the site did not load" must never be recorded as "the element has no box".
- If any single fixture exceeds **4 MB**, stop and report to the controller instead of committing it.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing guard**

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-evidence/probes/t0-check.mjs`:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// T0 guard: the fixture set Tasks 4/11/17 compile against must exist, parse, and carry the keys
// those tasks read. Run from anywhere: `node docs/.../probes/t0-check.mjs`.
// Red before t0-run.sh has been run; green after. Never asserts a *value* an engine produced —
// only that the shape a downstream `include_str!` will index into is present.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const PROBE_DIR = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = path.resolve(PROBE_DIR, "../../../../..");
if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(REPO, "Cargo.toml"))) {
  console.error(`FAIL repo root not found from ${PROBE_DIR} (resolved ${REPO})`);
  process.exit(2);
}
const CDP = path.join(REPO, "crates/aleph-cdp/tests/fixtures");
const PAGE = path.join(REPO, "src/browser/page_state/fixtures");
const MAX_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024;

// key path helper: "model.content" -> value or undefined
const dig = (v, p) => p.split(".").reduce((a, k) => (a == null ? a : a[k]), v);

// [file, [required key paths], optional predicate returning true | "why not"]
//
// R38: a fixture exists only where a NAMED test include_str!s it (判据 §17). Every entry below
// carries the Task-4 test that reads it; a file with no reader is not captured at all, which is
// why there is no obscura-void.json, no chrome-Target.attachToTarget.json and no
// obscura-DOM.getBoxModel.hidden.json — their findings live in t0-support-matrix.json and in
// t0-results.md, which do have readers.
const REQUIRED = [
  // ---- Chrome, under crates/aleph-cdp/tests/fixtures/ ----
  // reader: browser_get_version_parses_what_chrome_sent
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Browser.getVersion.json`, ["product", "userAgent", "protocolVersion"]],
  // reader: target_create_and_close_send_the_id_and_read_the_answer
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Target.createTarget.json`, ["targetId"]],
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Target.closeTarget.json`, ["success"]],
  // reader: target_get_targets_parses_both_engines
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Target.getTargets.json`, ["targetInfos.0.targetId", "targetInfos.0.type", "targetInfos.0.url"]],
  // reader: page_navigate_parses_both_engines_and_keeps_the_loader_id
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Page.navigate.json`, ["frameId"]],
  // reader: page_get_frame_tree_parses_the_chrome_fixture_and_its_child_frames
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Page.getFrameTree.json`, ["frameTree.frame.id", "frameTree.frame.loaderId", "frameTree.frame.url"]],
  // readers: page_get_layout_metrics_reads_only_the_css_pair,
  //          page_get_layout_metrics_refuses_a_reply_that_only_has_the_device_pixel_pair
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Page.getLayoutMetrics.json`, ["cssVisualViewport.clientWidth", "cssContentSize.width"]],
  // reader: page_navigation_history_returns_the_index_and_the_entries
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Page.getNavigationHistory.json`, ["currentIndex", "entries.0.id", "entries.0.url"]],
  // reader: page_screenshot_and_pdf_decode_their_base64_payloads
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Page.captureScreenshot.json`, ["data"]],
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Page.printToPDF.json`, ["data"]],
  // reader: dom_get_document_parses_both_engines_and_asks_for_the_whole_tree
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.getDocument.json`, ["root.nodeId", "root.backendNodeId", "root.nodeName", "root.children"]],
  // reader: dom_query_selector_maps_the_peers_zero_to_none
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.querySelector.json`, ["nodeId"],
    (v) => v.nodeId !== 0 || "querySelector hit must have a non-zero nodeId"],
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.querySelector.miss.json`, ["nodeId"],
    (v) => v.nodeId === 0 || "querySelector miss must be nodeId 0"],
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.querySelectorAll.json`, ["nodeIds"]],
  // reader: dom_resolve_and_describe_and_the_void_dom_verbs_send_their_arguments
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.describeNode.json`, ["node.backendNodeId", "node.nodeName"]],
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.resolveNode.json`, ["object.objectId"]],
  // reader: dom_box_model_parses_both_engines
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.getBoxModel.json`,
    ["model.content", "model.padding", "model.border", "model.margin", "model.width", "model.height"],
    (v) => (v.model.content.length === 8 || "content quad must have 8 numbers")
        && ((Number.isInteger(v.model.width) && Number.isInteger(v.model.height))
            || "width/height must be integers (aleph-cdp types them i64)")],
  // readers: the_no_box_matcher_is_the_code_and_message_chrome_actually_sends,
  //          dom_get_box_model_answers_none_for_the_refusal_chrome_actually_sent
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.getBoxModel.hidden.json`, ["error.code", "error.message"]],
  // reader: dom_get_box_model_propagates_every_other_protocol_error
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOM.getBoxModel.badnode.json`, ["error.code", "error.message"]],
  // reader: runtime_evaluate_returns_the_value_and_always_asks_for_it_by_value
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Runtime.evaluate.json`, ["result.type"]],
  // reader: runtime_evaluate_surfaces_a_thrown_error_instead_of_a_value
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Runtime.evaluate.throws.json`, ["exceptionDetails.text"]],
  // reader: runtime_call_function_on_wraps_its_arguments_the_way_cdp_expects
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Runtime.callFunctionOn.json`, ["result.type"]],
  // readers: network_cookies_parse_from_both_engines_and_survive_a_round_trip,
  //          network_set_cookies_supplies_a_url_only_for_cookies_with_no_domain
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Network.getAllCookies.json`,
    ["cookies.0.name", "cookies.0.value", "cookies.0.domain", "cookies.0.path"]],
  // reader: network_get_and_delete_cookies_send_exactly_their_arguments
  [`${CDP}/chrome-Network.getCookies.json`, ["cookies"]],
  // reader: dom_snapshot_keeps_the_raw_reply_and_exposes_its_two_arrays
  [`${CDP}/chrome-DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot.json`,
    ["documents.0.nodes.backendNodeId", "documents.0.layout.nodeIndex", "documents.0.layout.bounds", "strings"]],
  // readers: every_void_method_the_probe_captured_is_accepted_by_its_wrapper,
  //          target_activate_and_discover_send_exactly_their_arguments,
  //          page_dialog_and_history_and_reload_send_exactly_their_arguments
  [`${CDP}/chrome-void.json`,
    ["Page.enable", "Runtime.enable", "DOM.focus", "Input.dispatchMouseEvent",
     "Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", "Emulation.setEmulatedMedia",
     "Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate", "Network.emulateNetworkConditions",
     "Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders", "Network.clearBrowserCookies"]],
  // ---- obscura: only the seven a Task-4 test parses ----
  // reader: browser_get_version_parses_what_obscura_sent_with_the_same_type
  [`${CDP}/obscura-Browser.getVersion.json`, ["product", "userAgent", "protocolVersion"]],
  // reader: target_get_targets_parses_both_engines
  [`${CDP}/obscura-Target.getTargets.json`, ["targetInfos"]],
  // reader: page_navigate_parses_both_engines_and_keeps_the_loader_id
  [`${CDP}/obscura-Page.navigate.json`, ["frameId"]],
  // reader: dom_get_document_parses_both_engines_and_asks_for_the_whole_tree
  [`${CDP}/obscura-DOM.getDocument.json`, ["root.nodeId", "root.backendNodeId", "root.nodeName"]],
  // reader: dom_box_model_parses_both_engines
  [`${CDP}/obscura-DOM.getBoxModel.json`, ["model.content", "model.width", "model.height"],
    (v) => (v.model.content.length === 8 || "content quad must have 8 numbers")
        && ((Number.isInteger(v.model.width) && Number.isInteger(v.model.height))
            || "width/height must be integers (aleph-cdp types them i64)")],
  // reader: runtime_evaluate_returns_the_value_and_always_asks_for_it_by_value
  [`${CDP}/obscura-Runtime.evaluate.json`, ["result.type"]],
  // reader: network_cookies_parse_from_both_engines_and_survive_a_round_trip
  [`${CDP}/obscura-Network.getAllCookies.json`, ["cookies"]],
  // ---- cross-engine support record ----
  // reader: the_support_matrix_records_both_engines
  [`${CDP}/t0-support-matrix.json`, ["chrome", "obscura"]],
  // ---- page_state fixtures: both read by Part 3's Task 11, neither by any aleph-cdp test ----
  [`${PAGE}/hn-chromium.domsnapshot.json`, ["documents.0.layout.bounds", "strings"]],
  [`${PAGE}/local-oopif.domsnapshot.json`, ["documents.1.documentURL", "documents.1.layout.bounds"]],
];


let failures = 0;
const fail = (msg) => { console.error(`FAIL ${msg}`); failures += 1; };
for (const [file, keys, pred] of REQUIRED) {
  const rel = path.relative(REPO, file);
  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) { fail(`missing ${rel}`); continue; }
  const bytes = fs.statSync(file).size;
  if (bytes === 0) { fail(`${rel}: empty`); continue; }
  if (bytes > MAX_BYTES) {
    fail(`${rel}: ${bytes} bytes > ${MAX_BYTES} cap — report to the controller, do not commit`);
    continue;
  }
  let v;
  try { v = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8")); }
  catch (e) { fail(`${rel}: not JSON (${e.message})`); continue; }
  for (const k of keys) if (dig(v, k) === undefined) fail(`${rel}: missing ${k}`);
  if (pred) {
    const r = pred(v);
    if (r !== true) fail(`${rel}: ${r === false ? "predicate failed" : r}`);
  }
}
// t0-results.md must exist and must not still carry the marker the report writes when a probe
// produced no verdict at all.
const results = path.join(PROBE_DIR, "..", "t0-results.md");
if (!fs.existsSync(results)) fail("missing t0-results.md");
else if (fs.readFileSync(results, "utf8").includes("NO-VERDICT")) {
  fail("t0-results.md still carries a NO-VERDICT row");
}

console.log(failures === 0
  ? `PASS ${REQUIRED.length} fixtures + t0-results.md`
  : `${failures} failure(s)`);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);
```

`probes/t0-page.html` — the deterministic page every reproducible probe loads:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Aleph T0 probe page</title>
<style>
  html,body { margin:0; padding:0; font:16px/1.4 -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; }
  #hidden-none  { display:none; }
  #hidden-vis   { visibility:hidden; }
  #zero-size    { width:0; height:0; overflow:hidden; }
  #offscreen    { position:absolute; left:-9999px; top:0; }
  #opacity-zero { opacity:0; }
  #clip         { width:40px; height:12px; overflow:hidden; }
  #spacer       { height:2000px; }
  #deep-target  { width:120px; height:30px; }
  #frame-host   { position:absolute; left:200px; top:120px; width:400px; height:200px; border:0; }
  a, button     { cursor:pointer; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
  <header id="banner">
    <a id="home" href="/t0-page.html">Aleph T0</a>
    <a id="external" href="https://example.invalid/docs">Docs</a>
  </header>
  <main id="main">
    <h1 id="title">T0 probe page</h1>
    <p id="para">Deterministic page for the dual-engine T0 probes.</p>
    <label for="q">Search</label>
    <input id="q" name="q" type="text" placeholder="type here">
    <button id="go" type="button">Go</button>
    <input id="check" type="checkbox" checked>
    <select id="sel"><option value="a">Alpha</option><option value="b" selected>Beta</option></select>
    <textarea id="notes" rows="2" placeholder="notes"></textarea>
    <input id="file" type="file">
    <div id="hidden-none">display none text</div>
    <div id="hidden-vis">visibility hidden text</div>
    <div id="zero-size">zero</div>
    <div id="offscreen">offscreen text</div>
    <div id="opacity-zero">transparent text</div>
    <div id="clip">a very long clipped string that overflows its box</div>
    <ul id="list"><li>one</li><li>two</li></ul>
    <div id="spacer"></div>
    <button id="deep-target" type="button">Deep target</button>
  </main>
  <iframe id="frame-host" src="about:blank" title="child frame"></iframe>
  <script>
    window.__clicks = [];
    document.getElementById('deep-target').addEventListener('click', function (e) {
      window.__clicks.push({ id: 'deep-target', clientX: e.clientX, clientY: e.clientY,
                             pageX: e.pageX, pageY: e.pageY, scrollY: window.scrollY });
    });
    document.getElementById('go').addEventListener('click', function () {
      window.__clicks.push({ id: 'go' });
    });
    // Effect flags. A CDP method that answers `{}` while doing nothing is indistinguishable from
    // one that worked, unless the page itself reports what reached it. These are the read-back.
    window.__aleph_touch = false;
    window.__aleph_drag = false;
    document.addEventListener('touchstart', function () { window.__aleph_touch = true; }, true);
    document.addEventListener('dragover', function () { window.__aleph_drag = true; }, true);
    document.addEventListener('drop', function () { window.__aleph_drag = true; }, true);
    var child = new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('child');
    if (child) { document.getElementById('frame-host').src = child; }
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

`probes/t0-frame.html` — the cross-site child. `#probe` sits at `(30, 40)` inside the child, and the
iframe sits at `(200, 120)` in the parent with `border:0`, so its page-absolute position in the
parent is `(230, 160)`. That difference is exactly what U4 asks about.
