/// The machine-readable table: `{ "<engine>": { "<cap>": "<state>", …,
/// "measured_on": "…" } }`.
///
/// One author with [`describe_for_tool`] — both walk [`CAP_FIELDS`], which
/// Task 12 declares — so the sentence the model reads and the object the QA
/// fixture diffs cannot say different things.
#[must_use]
pub fn capabilities_json() -> serde_json::Value {
    let mut root = serde_json::Map::new();
    for engine in [Engine::Obscura, Engine::Chromium] {
        let caps = capabilities(engine);
        let mut row = serde_json::Map::new();
        for (name, get) in CAP_FIELDS {
            row.insert(
                (*name).to_string(),
                serde_json::Value::String(get(caps).as_str().to_string()),
            );
        }
        row.insert(
            "measured_on".to_string(),
            serde_json::Value::String(caps.measured_on.to_string()),
        );
        root.insert(engine.as_str().to_string(), serde_json::Value::Object(row));
    }
    serde_json::Value::Object(root)
}

/// The prose form, for the `browser_session{action:"capabilities"}` result.
///
/// Deliberately NOT in any tool's `DESCRIPTION`: that is a `const &'static str`
/// and the builtin catalog is a `const` array fed from it
/// (`src/executor/builtin_registry/definitions.rs:72,690`), so a runtime
/// `String` cannot get there — and a second, hand-written copy of this table
/// living in a description would be the exact defect that file's module doc
/// records (a literal in the catalog replaces the tool's own text and nothing
/// notices). The description names the ACTION; the action serves the table.
///
/// The model that never asks still learns the gap at the only moment it
/// matters: `UnsupportedByEngine` names the verb and the engine that has it,
/// and that engine comes from Task 12's `supported_by` — the same table.
#[must_use]
pub fn describe_for_tool() -> String {
    let mut out = String::from(
        "Browser engines. obscura is the default; chromium is the escape hatch, reached with \
         browser_session{action:\"switch_engine\", engine:\"chromium\"} (cookies and open URLs \
         move across; scroll position and page state do not).\n",
    );
    for engine in [Engine::Obscura, Engine::Chromium] {
        let caps = capabilities(engine);
        let gaps: Vec<&str> = CAP_FIELDS
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, get)| get(caps) != Cap::Supported)
            .map(|(name, _)| *name)
            .collect();
        if gaps.is_empty() {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "{}: every verb in this table. Measured on {}.\n",
                engine.as_str(),
                caps.measured_on
            ));
        } else {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "{}: cannot {}. Measured on {}.\n",
                engine.as_str(),
                gaps.join(", "),
                caps.measured_on
            ));
        }
    }
    out
}

**3b. `src/browser/engine/obscura.rs`** (new):

```rust
//! Launching obscura, and knowing which process owns the port it answers on.
//!
//! # Why Aleph picks the port
//!
//! `obscura serve --port 0` binds an ephemeral port and then reports the
//! *requested* one in both announcements: stdout prints
//! `CDP server: ws://127.0.0.1:0/devtools/browser`, and `/json/version`
//! returns the same string (`server.rs:791` formats the configured port).
//! Measured on v0.2.2. So there is no "read the port back" path — that URL
//! cannot connect. Aleph reserves an ephemeral port itself, passes it, and the
//! announcements then agree with reality.
//!
//! # Why the stdout banner is never waited on
//!
//! It is printed BEFORE the bind is attempted. Launch obscura on a port
//! somebody else holds and you get the banner on stdout, then
//! `Error: bind 127.0.0.1:<p>: Address already in use` on stderr, then exit 1.
//! A wait on that line would be a readiness signal that is true even when the
//! server never came up — a 恒真 predicate (判据 §2). Readiness here is
//! `/json/version` answering AND the child still being alive.
//!
//! # Why the port cannot belong to somebody else
//!
//! TCP bind on `127.0.0.1:<p>` is exclusive, so at most one process holds it.
//! If another process took the port in the window between our reservation and
//! the spawn, obscura fails to bind and exits non-zero with the message above
//! — which is why "the child is still alive after `/json/version` answered" is
//! evidence and not a hope. [`probe_port_owner`] adds the direct OS-level
//! confirmation on top; when the probing tool itself is unavailable that is an
//! absent instrument, not a refutation, and the launch proceeds with a warning
//! (判据 §8, §18).
//!
//! # stdio: a file, not a pipe, and no endpoint line is taken from it
//!
//! stdin null; stdout and stderr to `<storage_dir>/serve.log`, truncated per
//! launch. NOT a pipe: there is no endpoint line worth reading (the banner
//! carries the requested port and is printed before the bind), and an undrained
//! pipe blocks the child once the OS buffer fills — obscura is chatty, logging
//! a warning per page script. NOT `/dev/null` either: the bind-failure text
//! above is the single most useful diagnostic this launcher can hand an
//! operator, and dropping it would leave `LaunchFailed` holding an exit code
//! and nothing else. A file has no backpressure and keeps the text.
//!
//! The cost, stated: one log file per profile per session, unbounded within
//! that session. It is truncated on each launch rather than rotated, which is
//! the cheap answer and the honest one to write down.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use async_trait::async_trait;

use super::process::{
    terminate, write_sidecar_record, ChildHandle, CdpEndpoint, EngineProcess, LaunchRequest,
    Launched,
};
use super::Engine;
use crate::browser::error::BrowserError;
use crate::browser::profile::ObscuraVariant;
use crate::utils::no_window::NoWindow;

/// The per-profile subdirectory obscura persists cookies and storage into.
/// `Engine::data_subdir(Engine::Obscura)` returns the same string; this const
/// exists so the QA fixture and the orphan sweep can name it without importing
/// the enum.
pub const OBSCURA_STORAGE_LEAF: &str = "obscura";

/// obscura's own stdout+stderr, per profile.
pub const OBSCURA_LOG: &str = "serve.log";

/// How long to wait for `/json/version` after the spawn.
const ENDPOINT_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
const ENDPOINT_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);

/// The exact argv, as an ordered token vector.
///
/// Every valued flag uses the `=` form so it is ONE token. That is not style:
/// the orphan sweep matches whole argv elements
/// (`src/browser/chromium_launch.rs:257-275` — a substring scan kills the
/// neighbouring profile's browser, and macOS `sysinfo::cmd()` bleeds
/// environment words into argv), so `--storage-dir=<dir>` as one token is what
/// makes an obscura orphan reapable at all.
///
/// `--host=127.0.0.1` is passed explicitly even though it is already the
/// default. A CDP endpoint reachable off-loopback is remote code execution on
/// this machine, and inheriting a default for a security boundary is how that
/// boundary moves without anyone editing Aleph.
///
/// `--allow-file-access` is never passed, on any path (spec §7.2). There is no
/// parameter for it, so there is nothing to get wrong.
///
/// `req.headless` has no counterpart: obscura has no window and no `--headless`
/// flag. `launch` warns once when a profile asks for `headless = false`.
#[must_use]
pub fn obscura_argv(
    port: u16,
    storage_dir: &Path,
    req: &LaunchRequest,
    variant: ObscuraVariant,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut argv = vec![
        "serve".to_string(),
        "--host=127.0.0.1".to_string(),
        format!("--port={port}"),
        format!("--storage-dir={}", storage_dir.display()),
    ];
    if matches!(variant, ObscuraVariant::Stealth) {
        argv.push("--stealth".to_string());
    }
    if req.allow_private_network {
        argv.push("--allow-private-network".to_string());
    }
    if let Some(proxy) = &req.proxy {
        argv.push(format!("--proxy={proxy}"));
    }
    argv.extend(req.extra_args.iter().cloned());
    argv
}

/// Reserve an ephemeral loopback port by binding it and letting it go.
///
/// The window between the drop and obscura's own bind is real, and it is
/// closed on the far side rather than here: a loser gets `Address already in
/// use` and exits 1, which `launch` reports as `LaunchFailed{stage:
/// "obscura-exit"}` with that text.
pub fn reserve_port() -> Result<u16, BrowserError> {
    let listener =
        std::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)).map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
            stage: "reserve-port",
            detail: format!("cannot reserve a loopback port for obscura: {e}"),
        })?;
    let port = listener
        .local_addr()
        .map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
            stage: "reserve-port",
            detail: format!("cannot read the reserved port: {e}"),
        })?
        .port();
    drop(listener);
    Ok(port)
}

/// What an OS-level listener probe learned. Three states, not two, for the
/// same reason [`super::process::ArgvProbe`] has three: "I could not look" and
/// "nobody is there" authorise opposite actions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PortOwner {
    /// A listener on this port belongs to this pid.
    Pid(u32),
    /// The probe ran and found nothing listening.
    Unbound,
    /// The probe itself could not run. This is an absent instrument, NOT a
    /// statement about the port.
    Unknown(String),
}

/// Ask the OS who holds `port`.
///
/// unix: `lsof -a -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN -Fp`, whose output is `p<pid>`
/// lines — parsed by prefix rather than by column, so a change in lsof's
/// human-readable layout cannot silently produce a wrong pid. Exit 1 with no
/// output and no stderr is lsof's "no matches", i.e. [`PortOwner::Unbound`];
/// exit 1 WITH stderr is the tool complaining, i.e. [`PortOwner::Unknown`].
///
/// windows: `netstat -ano -p TCP`, matching a `LISTENING` row whose local
/// address ends `:<port>`; the last column is the pid.
#[must_use]
pub fn probe_port_owner(port: u16) -> PortOwner {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        let out = std::process::Command::new("lsof")
            .args([
                "-a",
                "-nP",
                &format!("-iTCP:{port}"),
                "-sTCP:LISTEN",
                "-Fp",
            ])
            .output();
        let out = match out {
            Ok(o) => o,
            Err(e) => return PortOwner::Unknown(format!("lsof could not run: {e}")),
        };
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
        if let Some(pid) = stdout
            .lines()
            .find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix('p'))
            .and_then(|p| p.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
        {
            return PortOwner::Pid(pid);
        }
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr);
        if stderr.trim().is_empty() {
            PortOwner::Unbound
        } else {
            PortOwner::Unknown(format!("lsof: {}", stderr.trim()))
        }
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let out = std::process::Command::new("netstat").args(["-ano", "-p", "TCP"]).output();
        let out = match out {
            Ok(o) => o,
            Err(e) => return PortOwner::Unknown(format!("netstat could not run: {e}")),
        };
        if !out.status.success() {
            return PortOwner::Unknown(format!(
                "netstat exited with {}: {}",
                out.status,
                String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim()
            ));
        }
        let needle = format!(":{port}");
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
        for line in text.lines() {
            let cols: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            // proto local foreign state pid
            if cols.len() < 5 || !cols[3].eq_ignore_ascii_case("LISTENING") {
                continue;
            }
            if !cols[1].ends_with(&needle) {
                continue;
            }
            if let Ok(pid) = cols[4].parse::<u32>() {
                return PortOwner::Pid(pid);
            }
        }
        PortOwner::Unbound
    }
    #[cfg(not(any(unix, windows)))]
    {
        let _ = port;
        PortOwner::Unknown("no listener probe on this platform".to_string())
    }
}

/// Turn a probe result into a verdict.
///
/// Split from [`probe_port_owner`] so all three arms are reachable from a test
/// without an OS, and so the *decision* is one function rather than a `match`
/// scattered through `launch`.
pub fn settle_port_ownership(port: u16, pid: u32, probe: PortOwner) -> Result<(), BrowserError> {
    match probe {
        PortOwner::Pid(p) if p == pid => Ok(()),
        PortOwner::Pid(other) => Err(BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
            stage: "port-ownership",
            detail: format!(
                "the CDP endpoint on 127.0.0.1:{port} is held by pid {other}, not by the \
                 obscura we launched (pid {pid}). Refusing to drive somebody else's browser."
            ),
        }),
        PortOwner::Unbound => Err(BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
            stage: "port-ownership",
            detail: format!(
                "nothing is listening on 127.0.0.1:{port}, but it answered /json/version a \
                 moment ago — the endpoint moved out from under us (pid {pid})."
            ),
        }),
        // An instrument we do not have says nothing about the port. Exclusive
        // TCP bind plus a child that did not exit with a bind error already
        // establishes ownership; failing here would make obscura unusable in
        // any container without lsof on the strength of a tool we never ran.
        PortOwner::Unknown(why) => {
            tracing::warn!(
                port,
                pid,
                reason = %why,
                "could not confirm the obscura CDP port's owner at the OS level; \
                 relying on exclusive bind plus a live child"
            );
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}

/// One obscura process this Aleph launched.
pub struct ObscuraLauncher {
    /// The resolved binary: the `[general.browser.obscura] binary_path` pin, or
    /// the ledger's `~/.aleph/runtimes/obscura/<tag>/obscura`.
    pub binary: PathBuf,
    pub variant: ObscuraVariant,
}

#[async_trait]
impl EngineProcess for ObscuraLauncher {
    fn engine(&self) -> Engine {
        Engine::Obscura
    }

    async fn launch(&self, req: LaunchRequest) -> Result<Launched, BrowserError> {
        if !req.headless {
            // obscura has no window and no `--headless`; a profile asking for
            // a headed browser is asking for something this engine cannot do.
            // Warned rather than refused: the useful answer is "you got a
            // headless one", and `browser_session{switch_engine}` is the way
            // to a real window.
            tracing::warn!(
                profile = %req.profile,
                "obscura has no headed mode; headless = false is ignored on this engine \
                 (switch to chromium for a window)"
            );
        }
        let storage_dir = req.data_dir.join(OBSCURA_STORAGE_LEAF);
        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&storage_dir)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
                stage: "spawn",
                detail: format!(
                    "cannot create the obscura storage dir {}: {e}",
                    storage_dir.display()
                ),
            })?;
        // obscura persists cookies here under `--use-mock-keychain`-equivalent
        // conditions (no OS keychain at all), so the same owner-only bit
        // `restrict_udd_to_owner` applies to Chromium applies here.
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            tokio::fs::set_permissions(&storage_dir, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700))
                .await
                .map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
                    stage: "spawn",
                    detail: format!(
                        "cannot restrict the obscura storage dir {} to owner-only: {e}",
                        storage_dir.display()
                    ),
                })?;
        }

        let port = reserve_port()?;
        let fx = ObscuraEffects {
            binary: self.binary.clone(),
            log_path: storage_dir.join(OBSCURA_LOG),
            session_key: req.session_key.clone(),
            data_dir: req.data_dir.clone(),
            sidecar_path: std::sync::Mutex::new(None),
        };
        let launched = launch_with(&req, self.variant, port, &fx).await?;
        tracing::info!(
            pid = launched.pid,
            endpoint = %launched.endpoint.http_url,
            "obscura launched"
        );
        Ok(launched)
    }

    /// Delegated: terminating a child, waiting out a grace period and reaping
    /// it is identical for both engines, and a second copy here is how one of
    /// them ends up without the `wait()` (判据 §16).
    async fn kill(&self, launched: &Launched, grace: Duration) -> Result<bool, BrowserError> {
        terminate(launched, grace).await
    }
}

/// The ordering skeleton, with the three effects injected.
///
/// Exists so the ORDER — sidecar before the endpoint is known, endpoint before
/// the second sidecar write — is testable without a binary. `ChromiumChild::spawn`
/// states the same rule at `src/browser/chromium_launch.rs:355-364`: if this
/// future is dropped at any await below, the first record is the only trace
/// that a process exists and needs reaping (判据 §15).
/// The three effects `launch_with` orders, behind one trait.
///
/// `record` and `wait_ready` are `async` **because they are async in
/// production**: one writes a file, the other polls HTTP. The first draft made
/// them synchronous so a closure could stand in, and that decision propagated
/// backwards into the implementation — the write became a detached
/// `tokio::spawn` and the poll became `reqwest::blocking` on a tokio worker.
/// A seam whose shape forces the production code to block or detach is the
/// defect, not the convenience (判据 §4, arriving through the test door).
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub(crate) trait LaunchEffects: Sync {
    fn spawn(&self, argv: Vec<String>) -> Result<(u32, ChildHandle), BrowserError>;
    /// Must have LANDED when it returns. A caller that detaches this defeats
    /// the ordering the sidecar exists for.
    async fn record(&self, pid: u32, http: Option<String>);
    async fn wait_ready(&self, port: u16, child: &ChildHandle) -> Result<String, BrowserError>;
    /// The path the first `record` wrote. ONE derivation of it (判据 §1).
    fn sidecar_path(&self) -> std::path::PathBuf;
}

pub(crate) async fn launch_with(
    req: &LaunchRequest,
    variant: ObscuraVariant,
    port: u16,
    fx: &dyn LaunchEffects,
) -> Result<Launched, BrowserError> {
    let storage_dir = req.data_dir.join(OBSCURA_STORAGE_LEAF);
    let argv = obscura_argv(port, &storage_dir, req, variant);
    let (pid, child) = fx.spawn(argv)?;
    // Intent stamped BEFORE the endpoint is known, and AWAITED: a detached
    // write returns before anything reaches disk, so a cancelled launch or a
    // runtime shutdown in that window leaves an obscura nothing can find
    // again. `ChromiumChild::spawn` awaits its equivalent for the same reason
    // (`src/browser/chromium_launch.rs:364`).
    fx.record(pid, None).await;
    // On every early return from here on, the child is still owned by
    // `child` — which is dropped, NOT killed (`std::process::Child` has no
    // kill-on-drop). The sidecar written one line above is what makes it
    // reapable, which is the whole reason that write comes first (判据 §15).
    let ws_url = fx.wait_ready(port, &child).await?;
    let http_url = format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}");
    fx.record(pid, Some(http_url.clone())).await;
    Ok(Launched {
        pid,
        endpoint: CdpEndpoint {
            http_url,
            ws_url,
            pid,
        },
        // ONE derivation. `write_sidecar_record` returns the path it wrote, and
        // that is the path this carries — computing it a second time with
        // `sidecar_path` would put a path in `Launched` that nothing wrote if
        // Task 5 ever moved the leaf (判据 §1).
        sidecar_path: fx.sidecar_path(),
        child,
    })
}

/// Spawn the process with the stdio discipline described in the module doc.
/// The production effects. One struct rather than three closures so the
/// `sidecar_path` the first `record` learns can be carried to `launch_with`'s
/// return without a second derivation.
struct ObscuraEffects {
    binary: PathBuf,
    log_path: PathBuf,
    session_key: String,
    data_dir: PathBuf,
    /// Set by the first `record`, read once by `launch_with`.
    sidecar_path: std::sync::Mutex<Option<PathBuf>>,
}

#[async_trait]
impl LaunchEffects for ObscuraEffects {
    fn spawn(&self, argv: Vec<String>) -> Result<(u32, ChildHandle), BrowserError> {
        spawn_obscura(&self.binary, argv, &self.log_path)
    }

    async fn record(&self, pid: u32, http: Option<String>) {
        let path =
            write_sidecar_record(Engine::Obscura, &self.session_key, pid, &self.data_dir, http)
                .await;
        *self.sidecar_path.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(path);
    }

    async fn wait_ready(&self, port: u16, child: &ChildHandle) -> Result<String, BrowserError> {
        wait_for_endpoint(port, child, &self.log_path).await
    }

    fn sidecar_path(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.sidecar_path
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .clone()
            // `record(pid, None)` runs before this is ever read, so the `None`
            // arm is unreachable; it falls back to the deriver rather than
            // panicking, because an unreachable arm that panics is a crash
            // where a stale path would merely be wrong.
            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
                super::process::sidecar_path(&self.session_key).unwrap_or_default()
            })
    }
}

/// stdio per the module doc: a file, never a pipe, never `/dev/null`.
fn spawn_obscura(
    binary: &Path,
    argv: Vec<String>,
    log_path: &Path,
) -> Result<(u32, ChildHandle), BrowserError> {
    let log = std::fs::File::create(log_path).map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
        stage: "spawn",
        detail: format!("cannot open {} for obscura's output: {e}", log_path.display()),
    })?;
    let errlog = log.try_clone().map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
        stage: "spawn",
        detail: format!("cannot duplicate the obscura log handle: {e}"),
    })?;
    // `std::process::Command`, not tokio's: `Launched.child` carries a
    // `std::process::Child` so `kill` can `try_wait`/`wait` it, and that is
    // also the type `ChromiumChild::spawn` uses at HEAD
    // (`src/browser/chromium_launch.rs:355` treats `child.id()` as a bare
    // `u32`, which only the std type gives).
    let mut cmd = Command::new(binary);
    cmd.args(&argv)
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::from(log))
        .stderr(Stdio::from(errlog));
    // Same discipline as `ChromiumChild::spawn` (`chromium_launch.rs:344-348`)
    // and `playwright_cli::spawn`: the browser never needs the parent's
    // credentials, and over-stripping is safe.
    //
    // It inherits that code's hazard as well, and copying it knowingly is the
    // point: `std::env::vars()` iterates while another thread may be inside
    // `std::env::set_var` (the `HomeEnvGuard` / `AlephHomeEnvGuard` pair does
    // exactly that in tests, `bootstrap::prepend_existing_dirs` in production).
    // `env_clear()` is not the fix — the browser needs PATH and DISPLAY — and
    // diverging from the twin here would leave two disciplines where the point
    // was to have one (判据 §16). Named so the next reader does not rediscover
    // it and assume this file introduced it.
    for (name, _) in std::env::vars() {
        if crate::security::secret_env::is_secret_env(&name) {
            cmd.env_remove(&name);
        }
    }
    let child = cmd
        .no_window()
        .spawn()
        .map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
            stage: "spawn",
            detail: format!("{}: {e}", binary.display()),
        })?;
    let pid = child.id();
    Ok((pid, Arc::new(Mutex::new(Some(child)))))
}

/// Poll `/json/version` until it answers, then confirm the port's owner.
///
/// The three exits are deliberately distinct, because they are three different
/// operator problems: the child died (its stderr is in the log and goes into
/// the message), the deadline elapsed, or somebody else owns the port.
/// **`async`, and the async `reqwest::Client`.** The first draft used
/// `reqwest::blocking` and `std::thread::sleep` inside a function called from
/// an `async fn`. `reqwest::blocking` builds its own runtime and **panics when
/// nested inside a tokio worker** — this codebase already wrote that down at
/// `src/extension/runtime/wasm/host_functions.rs:232-234` and goes through
/// `std::thread::scope` to avoid it. Even without the panic, a 30 s
/// `std::thread::sleep` loop parks a worker. `spawn_blocking` is not the fix
/// either: the `&ChildHandle` this borrows is not `'static`. HEAD's equivalent
/// poll loop is fully async for the same reasons
/// (`ChromiumChild::spawn`, `src/browser/chromium_launch.rs:366-406`).
async fn wait_for_endpoint(
    port: u16,
    child: &ChildHandle,
    log_path: &Path,
) -> Result<String, BrowserError> {
    let url = format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/version");
    let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(2))
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
            stage: "cdp-endpoint",
            detail: format!("cannot build an http client for the readiness poll: {e}"),
        })?;
    let started = Instant::now();
    let pid = child
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
        .as_ref()
        .map_or(0, std::process::Child::id);
    loop {
        if let Ok(resp) = client.get(&url).send().await {
            if resp.status().is_success() {
                // Ownership AFTER the endpoint answered: before it, nothing is
                // bound yet and the probe would legitimately say `Unbound`.
                // `probe_port_owner` forks `lsof`/`netstat`, so it goes to a
                // blocking thread rather than onto this worker.
                let probe = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || probe_port_owner(port))
                    .await
                    .unwrap_or_else(|e| PortOwner::Unknown(format!("the probe task failed: {e}")));
                settle_port_ownership(port, pid, probe)?;
                return Ok(format!("ws://127.0.0.1:{port}/devtools/browser"));
            }
        }
        // Liveness from the CHILD HANDLE, not from a pid lookup: `try_wait`
        // reaps the exit status as a side effect, so this loop cannot leave a
        // zombie behind on the failure path, and it cannot be fooled by a
        // recycled pid. `Err` from `try_wait` is answered "still alive", the
        // same reading `ChromiumChild::alive` states
        // (`src/browser/chromium_launch.rs:445-451`): "I could not tell" is
        // not "it is dead".
        let exited = child
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .as_mut()
            .and_then(|c| c.try_wait().ok().flatten());
        if let Some(status) = exited {
            return Err(BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
                stage: "obscura-exit",
                detail: format!(
                    "obscura (pid {pid}) exited with {status} before answering \
                     /json/version: {}",
                    tail_of(log_path, 2000)
                ),
            });
        }
        if started.elapsed() >= ENDPOINT_DEADLINE {
            return Err(BrowserError::LaunchFailed {
                stage: "cdp-endpoint",
                detail: format!(
                    "obscura (pid {pid}) did not answer {url} within {}s: {}",
                    ENDPOINT_DEADLINE.as_secs(),
                    tail_of(log_path, 2000)
                ),
            });
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(ENDPOINT_POLL).await;
    }
}

/// The last `max` bytes of obscura's log, on a char boundary.
///
/// `.get(..n)` rather than `&s[..n]` (P7): the log is arbitrary UTF-8 and a
/// byte slice through a multi-byte character panics — inside an error path,
/// where a panic replaces a diagnosis with a crash.
fn tail_of(path: &Path, max: usize) -> String {
    let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(path) else {
        return format!("(no output captured at {})", path.display());
    };
    if text.len() <= max {
        return text.trim().to_string();
    }
    let start = text.len() - max;
    let boundary = text
        .char_indices()
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .find(|i| *i >= start)
        .unwrap_or(text.len());
    text.get(boundary..).unwrap_or_default().trim().to_string()
}
```

```rust
/// The spawned process, kept so it can be waited rather than merely signalled.
///
/// `Option` because the child is TAKEN by whoever reaps it, and because a
/// `Launched` reconstructed from a sidecar after a crash has no `Child` at
/// all — that case goes to the orphan sweep, which decides on pid + argv.
pub type ChildHandle = std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::process::Child>>>;

/// SIGKILL, bounded reap, no handshake. Returns whether the process is GONE.
pub async fn terminate(launched: &Launched, grace: Duration) -> Result<bool, BrowserError>;
```

### Task 17: `fetch_obscura` — the interim `RawDom` fetcher

**Files:**
- Create: `src/browser/page_state/fetch_obscura.rs`
- Create: `src/browser/page_state/fixtures/boxes-obscura.getdocument.json` — **the only fixture this task creates**, and the only one with a reader: `include_str!` in the test module below. Three others were listed here and are cut (R38, 判据 §17): `hn-obscura.getdocument.json` and `hn-obscura.boxmodels.json` are read by no test in any part, so Task 0 no longer captures them; and the computed rows live inline in `measured_rows()` rather than in a file, because a fixture nobody `include_str!`s is a file that gets regenerated, diffed and reviewed while bounding nothing. **A fixture exists where a NAMED test reads it, and nowhere else.**
- Modify: `src/browser/page_state/mod.rs` (declare + re-export `fetch_obscura`)
- Modify: the root `Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]` (`aleph-cdp = { path = "crates/aleph-cdp", features = ["testkit"] }`). **`crates/aleph-cdp/src/testkit.rs` itself is Task 1's file and is not edited here** — this task uses `start` / `scripted` / `scripted_slow` / `connect_and_attach` exactly as that task defines them (R20).
- Test: inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `fetch_obscura.rs`

**Interfaces:**

Consumes (Task 10's `page_state` types, restated verbatim):
- `pub struct Rect { pub x: i32, pub y: i32, pub w: i32, pub h: i32 }`
- `pub struct Viewport { pub width: u32, pub height: u32, pub scroll_x: i32, pub scroll_y: i32, pub content_width: u32, pub content_height: u32, pub dpr: f64 }`
- `pub struct Computed { pub display_none: bool, pub visibility_hidden: bool, pub opacity_zero: bool, pub cursor_pointer: bool }` — **four flags. R34 cut `overflow_clip`**, so the `evaluate` below requests exactly the four properties the builder reads: a fifth column would be bytes across the wire that nothing consumes, and a `Computed` the builder cannot construct.
- `pub enum RawNodeKind { Document, Element, Text, Other }`
- `pub struct RawNode { pub backend_node_id: u64, pub parent: Option<usize>, pub kind: RawNodeKind, pub tag: Option<String>, pub attrs: Vec<(String, String)>, pub text: Option<String>, pub rect: Option<Rect>, pub computed: Option<Computed>, pub clickable_hint: Option<bool> }` — **no `shadow_root`; R34 cut it.** Shadow roots are still walked, as ordinary children (Part 1's `dom::Node` keeps `pub shadow_roots: Vec<Node>`), they simply carry no flag distinguishing them.
- `pub struct RawFrame { pub frame_id: String, pub loader_id: String, pub offset: (i32, i32), pub nodes: Vec<RawNode> }`
- `pub struct RawDom { pub engine: Engine, pub viewport: Viewport, pub frames: Vec<RawFrame> }`

Consumes (Task 4's `aleph_cdp::methods`, restated):
- `dom::get_document(conn, session, depth: i64, pierce: bool) -> Result<dom::Node, CdpError>` with `pub struct Node { pub node_id: i64, pub backend_node_id: i64, pub node_type: i64, pub node_name: String, pub node_value: String, pub attributes: Vec<String>, pub children: Vec<Node>, pub shadow_roots: Vec<Node>, pub content_document: Option<Box<Node>>, pub frame_id: Option<String> }`
- `dom::get_box_model(conn, session, backend_node_id: i64) -> Result<Option<dom::BoxModel>, CdpError>` with `pub struct BoxModel { pub content: [f64; 8], pub padding: [f64; 8], pub border: [f64; 8], pub margin: [f64; 8], pub width: i64, pub height: i64 }`
- `page::get_layout_metrics(conn, session) -> Result<page::LayoutMetrics, CdpError>`
- `page::get_frame_tree(conn, session) -> Result<page::FrameTree, CdpError>` — **Task 4 owns it (binding ruling R8); this task only consumes it.** The shape is nested, not flat: `pub struct Frame { pub id: String, pub parent_id: Option<String>, pub loader_id: String, pub url: String }` and `pub struct FrameTree { pub frame: Frame, pub child_frames: Vec<FrameTree> }`. The main frame's document identity is `tree.frame.loader_id`. Task 11 (`fetch_chromium`) consumes the same type, so a second flat shape here would break whichever of the two landed second.
- `runtime::evaluate(conn, session, expression: &str, await_promise: bool) -> Result<runtime::EvalResult, CdpError>` with `pub struct EvalResult { pub value: serde_json::Value, pub exception: Option<String> }` (`returnByValue: true` always)

Produces:
- `pub async fn fetch_obscura(conn: &CdpConnection, session: &SessionId, box_concurrency: usize) -> Result<RawDom, BrowserError>`
- `pub const DEFAULT_BOX_CONCURRENCY: usize = 16;`
- `pub const COMPUTED_FLAGS_JS: &str` — the one expression, so the QA fixture and the test use the same string
- `pub fn parse_computed_rows(value: &serde_json::Value, element_count: usize, first_tag: &str, last_tag: &str) -> Option<Vec<Computed>>`

**Measurements this task is built on — taken on the real v0.2.2 binary, 2026-09-06, against a local `python3 -m http.server` fixture. Re-run them before writing code; every design choice below is downstream of one of them.**

Fixture page (`boxes.html`): an `h1`, a `div.hid{display:none}`, a `div.invis{visibility:hidden}`, an `a#lnk[style=cursor:pointer]`, a `span.zero{opacity:0}`, and an `iframe src=/child.html`.

**M-a. `Page.getFrameTree` carries a real `loaderId`, and `Page.navigate` returns one.**
```
FRAMETREE_BEFORE_NAV  frame.loaderId = "loader-blank-page-1"
NAVIGATE_RESULT       {"frameId":"page-1","loaderId":"loader-010b239d-4769-4df5-a089-5d312c451b51"}
FRAMETREE_AFTER_NAV   frame.loaderId = "loader-010b239d-4769-4df5-a089-5d312c451b51"
```
So the ref table's document identity is real on obscura and needs no synthetic fallback. **But the CHILD frame's loaderId is derived from its frame id and never changes**: `page-1-frame-1` has `loaderId: "page-1-frame-1-loader"`, before and after. That is a frame id wearing a loader id's name — which is exactly why `RefTable::reset_for_document` keys on the MAIN frame's loader id only (Task 10). Keying on a child's would never reset.

**M-b. `DOM.getDocument{depth:-1, pierce:true}` does NOT descend into iframes.**
```
GETDOCUMENT_HAS_CONTENTDOCUMENT  false
GETDOCUMENT_HAS_FRAMEID          false
IFRAME node: {"nodeName":"IFRAME","childNodeCount":0,"attributes":["src","/child.html", …]}
```
`pierce` is accepted and ignored. The `<iframe>` element is present as an ordinary element with no children. So this fetcher produces **exactly one `RawFrame`**, always, and cross-origin or same-origin iframe *content* is invisible to obscura's snapshot. Not a defect in this code — a stated gap.

**M-c. `DOM.getBoxModel` succeeded for every element on this page and returned a ZERO quad for the inline ones.** The table below is one page, and it is the only page this claim covers — the earlier spike's M11 found five HN elements with real boxes matching `getBoundingClientRect()`, so "obscura has no inline layout" is a hypothesis this data is consistent with and does not establish. **T0's U9 probe settles it.** Nothing downstream depends on the resolution: `rect: None` is never spent as invisibility on obscura either way. Full table from the fixture:

| element | `getBoxModel` | `getBoundingClientRect()` in obscura's own JS |
|---|---|---|
| `HTML` | 1280×208 at (0,0) | 1280×208 at (0,0) |
| `HEAD` / `TITLE` / `STYLE` | 0×0 | 0×0 |
| `BODY` | 1264×179 at (8,21) | 1264×179 at (8,21) |
| `H1` | 1264×37 at (8,21) | 1264×37 at (8,21) |
| `DIV.hid` (`display:none`) | **0×0, success** | 0×0 |
| `DIV.invis` (`visibility:hidden`) | 1264×18 at (8,79) | 1264×18 at (8,79) |
| **`A#lnk`** (inline, plainly visible) | **0×0, success** | **0×0** |
| **`SPAN.zero`** (inline) | **0×0, success** | 0×0 |
| `IFRAME` | 204×84 at (8,115) | 204×84 at (8,115) |

`DOM.getContentQuads` on the `<a>` returns `[[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]]` too. The last two columns agreeing settles WHERE the fault is — in obscura's layout, not in its CDP layer — without settling how far it reaches. It is emphatically not the constant `[8,8,108,8,108,28,8,28]` fallback the source survey warned about (`domains/dom.rs:322-327`): that fallback fires on an unparseable JS round trip, and here the round trip parsed and said zero.

Three consequences, all of them load-bearing:
1. A zero box is mapped to `rect: None`, and **`rect: None` may not be read as "hidden" when `raw.engine == Obscura`.** The spec's `rect=None ⇒ hidden` rule is a Chromium rule; on obscura it hid the only link on the page measured here. The controller has accepted this: **Task 10's visibility rule now consults the computed styles first**, and it holds whichever way U9 comes out — if obscura lays out most inline elements after all, the rule costs nothing; if it lays out none, the rule is the only thing keeping a page describable.
2. The visibility signal on obscura is the computed-flags evaluate (M-d), not the box.
3. A `Coordinates` click cannot reach an element with no box. Task 18's `click` stage therefore aims its coordinate half at a **block-level** `<div onclick>`, which has a box on any reading of U9, and separately asserts the inline link's missing rect as a KNOWN GAP — so if U9 finds the gap is narrower than this page suggests, or if upstream closes it, the fixture says so instead of quietly improving.

**M-d. One `Runtime.evaluate` gives the computed flags, and the cross-check agrees.**
```
ELEMENT_COUNT_FROM_GETDOCUMENT 11
QSA_COUNT                      11
first = HTML, last = IFRAME    (both routes, document order)
rows[6]  DIV.hid   [true,false,false,false,false]   display:none
rows[7]  DIV.invis [false,true,false,false,false]   visibility:hidden
rows[8]  A#lnk     [false,false,false,true,false]   cursor:pointer
rows[9]  SPAN.zero [false,false,true,false,false]   opacity:0
```
The probe above captured FIVE columns; the fifth was `overflow_clip`, which R34
subsequently cut from `Computed`. The rows are quoted as measured — a
measurement is not edited after the fact — but the shipped expression requests
four properties and `parse_computed_rows` enforces four, so **`measured_rows()`
in Step 1 carries four**. These rows are inline in that helper rather than in a
fixture file: they are eleven short arrays, the test is their only reader, and a
JSON file read by nothing would be a fixture in name only (R38). Requesting a
fifth column would put bytes on the wire that nothing reads.
`getComputedStyle` is correct on obscura, the element order from `DOM.getDocument`'s walk matches `document.querySelectorAll('*')`, and the counts match. The cross-check the design calls for is not theatre — it has a real chance of disagreeing (a script that mutates the DOM between the two calls) and a real answer when it does.

**M-e. `Page.getLayoutMetrics` reports the viewport as the content size.**
```
cssContentSize: {"x":0,"y":0,"width":1280,"height":720}   // page is 208 px tall
cssVisualViewport: {"clientWidth":1280,"clientHeight":720,"scale":1,"zoom":1,"pageX":0,"pageY":0}
```
`contentSize` equals the viewport rather than the document. So `Viewport::content_height` from obscura is the viewport height, not the scroll extent, and nothing may compute "how far can I scroll" from it. Recorded in the module doc; the header line prints it as measured rather than pretending.

            [false, false, false, false], // BODY

    fn base_entries(rows: serde_json::Value, n: usize, first: &str, last: &str)
        -> Vec<(&'static str, Responder)>
    {

    /// `(method, Responder)` table cannot express — so the base table is

    async fn server_with(rows: serde_json::Value, n: usize, first: &str, last: &str)
        -> FakeCdpServer
    {
        let boxes = measured_boxes();
        let base = scripted(base_entries(rows, n, first, last));

                    Some(v) => Responder::Reply(v.clone()),
                    None => Responder::Error { code: -32000, message: "Could not compute box model".into() },

            base(req)
        })
        .await
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn fetch_obscura_builds_one_frame_with_measured_rects_and_flags() {
        let server = server_with(measured_rows(), 11, "HTML", "IFRAME").await;
        let (conn, session) = server.connect_and_attach().await;

        let raw = fetch_obscura(&conn, &session, 4).await.expect("fetch must succeed");

        // with an <iframe> still yields exactly one frame.
        assert_eq!(raw.frames.len(), 1, "obscura ignores pierce:true");
        let f = &raw.frames[0];
        assert_eq!(f.frame_id, "page-1");
        assert_eq!(f.loader_id, "loader-010b239d");
        assert_eq!(f.offset, (0, 0));

        assert_eq!(h1.rect, Some(Rect { x: 8, y: 21, w: 1264, h: 37 }));
        assert_eq!(h1.computed.as_ref().unwrap().display_none, false);

        // M-c: a zero box becomes `None`, NOT `Some(0x0)`. A zero-sized rect
        // would be spent downstream as a real position and clicked at (0,0).
        let a = by_id(15);
        assert_eq!(a.tag.as_deref(), Some("a"));
        assert_eq!(a.rect, None, "an inline element has no box on obscura v0.2.2");
        // …and it is emphatically NOT hidden: the flags say so, which is why
        // `rect: None` may not be read as invisibility on this engine.
        let c = a.computed.as_ref().expect("the evaluate covered every element");
        assert!(!c.display_none && !c.visibility_hidden && !c.opacity_zero);
        assert!(c.cursor_pointer, "the measured cursor:pointer must survive");
        assert_eq!(
            a.attrs.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == "href").map(|(_, v)| v.as_str()),
            Some("/second.html"),
            "flat CDP attribute pairs are zipped into (name, value)"
        );

        let hidden = by_id(11);
        assert!(hidden.computed.as_ref().unwrap().display_none);
        assert_eq!(hidden.rect, None);

        // visibility:hidden keeps its layout box — the flag is what hides it.
        let invis = by_id(13);
        assert_eq!(invis.rect, Some(Rect { x: 8, y: 79, w: 1264, h: 18 }));
        assert!(invis.computed.as_ref().unwrap().visibility_hidden);

        // Text nodes come through with their value and their parent.
        let text = f.nodes.iter().find(|n| n.backend_node_id == 10).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(text.kind, RawNodeKind::Text);
        assert_eq!(text.text.as_deref(), Some("VISIBLE-MARK"));
        let parent = text.parent.expect("a text node has a parent");
        assert_eq!(f.nodes[parent].backend_node_id, 9);

        // M-e: contentSize is the VIEWPORT on obscura, recorded as measured.
        assert_eq!(raw.viewport.width, 1280);
        assert_eq!(raw.viewport.height, 720);
        assert_eq!(raw.viewport.content_height, 720);
    }

    /// `backendNodeId: 0` is the document on obscura — a legitimate id, not a
    /// sentinel. Anything that treats 0 as "absent" drops the root.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn backend_node_id_zero_is_the_document_not_a_missing_id() {
        let server = server_with(measured_rows(), 11, "HTML", "IFRAME").await;
        let (conn, session) = server.connect_and_attach().await;
        let raw = fetch_obscura(&conn, &session, 4).await.unwrap();
        let root = &raw.frames[0].nodes[0];
        assert_eq!(root.backend_node_id, 0);
        assert_eq!(root.kind, RawNodeKind::Document);
        assert_eq!(root.parent, None);
    }

    /// The cross-check exists to catch a page that mutated between the two
    /// calls. When it fires twice, every `computed` is `None` — the flags are
    /// not attributed to the wrong nodes, and the loss is stated rather than
    /// silently mis-aligned (判据 §8: an unknown may not be spent as a value).
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_persistent_count_mismatch_drops_every_computed_flag() {
        // 10 rows for 11 elements, twice.
        let short = serde_json::Value::Array(
            measured_rows().as_array().unwrap()[..10].to_vec(),
        );
        let server = server_with(short, 10, "HTML", "IFRAME").await;
        let (conn, session) = server.connect_and_attach().await;
        let raw = fetch_obscura(&conn, &session, 4).await.unwrap();
        assert!(
            raw.frames[0].nodes.iter().all(|n| n.computed.is_none()),
            "a mismatched evaluate must not be zipped onto the wrong nodes"
        );
        // The rects are unaffected: they came from a different call and are
        // still trustworthy.
        let h1 = raw.frames[0].nodes.iter().find(|n| n.backend_node_id == 9).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(h1.rect, Some(Rect { x: 8, y: 21, w: 1264, h: 37 }));
    }

    /// A first/last tag disagreement is the same class of failure as a count
    /// disagreement, and it is the one a count alone cannot see: 11 elements
    /// both times, different 11.
    #[test]
    fn parse_computed_rows_rejects_a_matching_count_with_a_different_first_tag() {
        let value = serde_json::json!({
            "n": 11, "first": "BODY", "last": "IFRAME", "rows": measured_rows(),
        });
        assert!(parse_computed_rows(&value, 11, "HTML", "IFRAME").is_none());
        let value = serde_json::json!({
            "n": 11, "first": "HTML", "last": "SPAN", "rows": measured_rows(),
        });
        assert!(parse_computed_rows(&value, 11, "HTML", "IFRAME").is_none());
        let value = serde_json::json!({
            "n": 11, "first": "HTML", "last": "IFRAME", "rows": measured_rows(),
        });
        let rows = parse_computed_rows(&value, 11, "HTML", "IFRAME").expect("agreeing shapes parse");
        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 11);
        assert!(rows[6].display_none);
        assert!(rows[8].cursor_pointer);
    }

    /// A `getBoxModel` that ERRORS is not a hidden element — it is one whose
    /// geometry we do not know. Same `rect: None`, and (crucially) the fetch
    /// still succeeds: one node's missing box must not lose the whole page.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_box_model_protocol_error_yields_rect_none_and_does_not_fail_the_fetch() {
        let base = scripted(base_entries(measured_rows(), 11, "HTML", "IFRAME"));
        let server = FakeCdpServer::start(move |req| {
            if req["method"] == "DOM.getBoxModel" {
                // Every box model is a PROTOCOL ERROR — a different fact from
                // "no box model", and neither may lose the rest of the page.
                return Responder::Error {
                    code: -32000,
                    message: "Could not compute box model".into(),
                };
            }
            base(req)
        })
        .await;
        let (conn, session) = server.connect_and_attach().await;
        let raw = fetch_obscura(&conn, &session, 4)
            .await
            .expect("one node's missing geometry must not lose the page");
        assert!(raw.frames[0].nodes.iter().all(|n| n.rect.is_none()));
        // The flags are untouched, so the page is still describable.
        assert!(raw.frames[0].nodes.iter().any(|n| n.computed.is_some()));
    }

    /// The bound is real, measured as ELAPSED TIME.
    ///
    /// Part 1's `Responder` has no enter/leave hook, and inventing one here
    /// would be a second design for a type another part owns (判据 §1). A
    /// fixed per-reply delay says the same thing arithmetically: eleven element
    /// nodes at `box_concurrency = 2` is six serialised batches, so the fetch
    /// cannot return in under `6 * delay`; unbounded, it is one batch. The two
    /// are ~6x apart, which is what makes this an effect assertion rather than
    /// a race.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn box_model_concurrency_is_bounded_by_the_parameter() {
        const DELAY: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_millis(20);
        let boxes = measured_boxes();
        let base = scripted_slow(base_entries(measured_rows(), 11, "HTML", "IFRAME"), DELAY);
        let server = FakeCdpServer::start(move |req| {
            if req["method"] == "DOM.getBoxModel" {
                let id = req["params"]["backendNodeId"].as_i64().unwrap_or(-1);
                let reply = boxes.get(&id).cloned().unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({}));
                return Responder::Delay(DELAY, Box::new(Responder::Reply(reply)));
            }
            base(req)
        })
        .await;
        let (conn, session) = server.connect_and_attach().await;

        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        fetch_obscura(&conn, &session, 2).await.unwrap();
        let elapsed = started.elapsed();

        // Floor chosen at 4 batches, not 6: the assertion has to survive a
        // loaded CI box rounding a 20 ms sleep, while still being far above the
        // ~1 batch an unbounded fetch would take.
        assert!(
            elapsed >= DELAY * 4,
            "eleven box models at concurrency 2 finished in {elapsed:?} — that is fewer \
             batches than the bound allows, so the bound is not being applied"
        );
    }

    /// The module is interim, and the sentence that says so is the only thing
    /// that will make someone delete it. Pinned so an edit that removes the
    /// pointer to its own expiry condition goes red.
    #[test]
    fn the_module_doc_states_its_own_deletion_condition() {
        let src = include_str!("fetch_obscura.rs");
        let head: String = src.lines().take_while(|l| l.starts_with("//!")).collect();
        assert!(head.contains("INTERIM"), "{head}");
        assert!(head.contains("DOMSnapshot"), "{head}");
        assert!(
            head.contains("Task 10") || head.contains("census"),
            "it must name what has to change when it goes: {head}"
        );
    }
}

```rust
//! **INTERIM.** obscura's `DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot` fabricates its
//! geometry — `domsnapshot.rs:231-236` is literally
//! `let y = (i as f64) * 18.0; bounds.push(json!([0.0, y, 1280.0, 18.0]))`,
//! with a constant style vector claiming `visibility:visible` for every node
//! and no marker on the wire — so the Chromium fetcher's one-call path cannot
//! be used on this engine. This module is the stand-in: `DOM.getDocument` for
//! the tree, bounded-concurrent `DOM.getBoxModel` for rectangles, and one
//! `Runtime.evaluate` for the computed flags.
//!
//! **DELETE IT** when the obscura ledger tag (`runtimes::specs::OBSCURA_TAG`)
//! reaches the release carrying the upstream `DOMSnapshot` layout fix (the
//! patch is `…-evidence/upstream/domsnapshot-real-layout.patch`). At that
//! point `fetch_chromium` serves both engines, and **Task 10's census —
//! "exactly one `PageState::build` call site, and every fetcher produces a
//! `RawDom`" — must be relaxed to allow a single fetcher**, or it will go red
//! on the deletion and look like a regression.
//!
//! # What this fetcher knows that the Chromium one does not
//!
//! Every item below was measured on the real v0.2.2 binary (2026-09-06), not
//! inferred from the source survey:
//!
//! * **`pierce: true` is accepted and ignored.** `DOM.getDocument` never
//!   returns a `contentDocument` and never returns a `frameId`; an `<iframe>`
//!   arrives as an ordinary element with `childNodeCount: 0`. So this fetcher
//!   always produces **exactly one** `RawFrame`, and iframe *content* is
//!   invisible to an obscura snapshot.
//! * **Inline elements had no box on the page that was measured, and the scope of
//!   that claim is the page.** On the fixture below, `<a>` and `<span>` returned
//!   a zero quad from `DOM.getBoxModel`, from `DOM.getContentQuads`, AND from
//!   `getBoundingClientRect()` in obscura's own JS — the three agreeing places
//!   the fault in the layout engine rather than in the CDP layer. It does
//!   **not** generalise on this evidence: the earlier spike (M11) measured five
//!   HN elements whose boxes were real and matched `getBoundingClientRect()`
//!   byte for byte. Both readings can be true, and **T0's U9 probe is what
//!   settles which elements obscura lays out** — a conclusion's scope is its
//!   method (判据 §18). What this fetcher does either way: a zero box becomes
//!   `rect: None`, and **`rect: None` is never read as hidden on this engine**,
//!   because on at least one real page that would hide the only link.
//!   Visibility comes from [`COMPUTED_FLAGS_JS`].
//! * **`Page.getFrameTree` carries a real, changing `loaderId` for the main
//!   frame** (`loader-blank-page-1` → `loader-010b239d-…` across a navigate),
//!   which is what makes ref generations work here at all. A CHILD frame's
//!   `loaderId` is derived from its frame id and never changes, so it must not
//!   be used as a document identity.
//! * **`Page.getLayoutMetrics.cssContentSize` is the viewport, not the
//!   document** (1280×720 for a 208 px page). Recorded as measured; nothing
//!   may compute a scroll extent from it.
//! * **`backendNodeId: 0` is the document.** It is a real id, not a sentinel.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use aleph_cdp::methods::{dom, page, runtime};
use aleph_cdp::{CdpConnection, SessionId};
use futures::stream::StreamExt;

use super::{Computed, RawDom, RawFrame, RawNode, RawNodeKind, Rect, Viewport};
use crate::browser::engine::Engine;
use crate::browser::error::BrowserError;

/// How many `DOM.getBoxModel` calls may be in flight at once.
///
/// Bounded because obscura serialises every `DOM.*` call behind one
/// per-connection V8 lock (`dispatch.rs:748-754`): unbounded concurrency does
/// not go faster, it just queues N commands against a 60 s per-command
/// watchdog, so one slow page turns into N timeouts instead of one.
pub const DEFAULT_BOX_CONCURRENCY: usize = 16;

/// The single expression that carries every per-element flag plus the
/// cross-check anchors, in `document.querySelectorAll('*')` order.
///
/// One expression rather than one per element: on obscura each `evaluate` is a
/// separate trip through the V8 lock, and the flags are cheap next to the trip.
/// The three anchors (`n`, `first`, `last`) are what make zipping the rows onto
/// the `getDocument` walk falsifiable rather than hopeful — a count alone
/// cannot see "11 elements both times, a different 11".
///
/// `pub` so `qa/browser_dual`'s prober runs the same string the fetcher runs;
/// two copies would let the QA agree with a fetcher that had changed.
pub const COMPUTED_FLAGS_JS: &str = "(() => { \
    const es = [...document.querySelectorAll('*')]; \
    const rows = es.map(e => { const c = getComputedStyle(e); return [ \
        c.display === 'none', \
        c.visibility === 'hidden', \
        parseFloat(c.opacity) === 0, \
        c.cursor === 'pointer' ]; }); \
    return { n: es.length, first: es[0] ? es[0].tagName : '', \
             last: es.length ? es[es.length - 1].tagName : '', rows }; })()";

/// Parse the evaluate payload, refusing anything whose shape disagrees with
/// the tree we walked.
///
/// `None` means "these flags cannot be trusted for THIS tree" and the caller
/// spends it as `computed: None` on every node — never as a partial zip, which
/// would attribute one element's visibility to another (判据 §8).
#[must_use]
pub fn parse_computed_rows(
    value: &serde_json::Value,
    element_count: usize,
    first_tag: &str,
    last_tag: &str,
) -> Option<Vec<Computed>> {
    let n = usize::try_from(value.get("n")?.as_u64()?).ok()?;
    if n != element_count {
        return None;
    }
    if !value.get("first")?.as_str()?.eq_ignore_ascii_case(first_tag) {
        return None;
    }
    if !value.get("last")?.as_str()?.eq_ignore_ascii_case(last_tag) {
        return None;
    }
    let rows = value.get("rows")?.as_array()?;
    if rows.len() != element_count {
        return None;
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(rows.len());
    for row in rows {
        let cols = row.as_array()?;
        // Four, and the number is `Computed`'s field count, not a wire
        // convention: R34 cut `overflow_clip`, and a row that still carried it
        // would be a column nothing reads (判据 §1).
        if cols.len() != 4 {
            return None;
        }
        out.push(Computed {
            display_none: cols[0].as_bool()?,
            visibility_hidden: cols[1].as_bool()?,
            opacity_zero: cols[2].as_bool()?,
            cursor_pointer: cols[3].as_bool()?,
        });
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// A flattened node plus the CDP id its box has to be fetched by.
struct Walked {
    node: RawNode,
    /// `Some` for element nodes: the id to ask `DOM.getBoxModel` about, and
    /// the position of this node in `querySelectorAll('*')` order.
    element_index: Option<usize>,
}

/// Flatten `DOM.getDocument`'s nested tree into document order.
///
/// Order matters twice over: it is the order `render_text` prints, and it is
/// the order the computed rows are zipped in. `querySelectorAll('*')` is
/// document order too, which is why the zip is sound — and the first/last tag
/// anchors are what prove it on each fetch rather than once in a comment.
fn walk(node: &dom::Node, parent: Option<usize>, out: &mut Vec<Walked>, element_seq: &mut usize) {
    let kind = match node.node_type {
        1 => RawNodeKind::Element,
        3 => RawNodeKind::Text,
        9 => RawNodeKind::Document,
        _ => RawNodeKind::Other,
    };
    let element_index = if matches!(kind, RawNodeKind::Element) {
        let i = *element_seq;
        *element_seq += 1;
        Some(i)
    } else {
        None
    };
    // CDP ships attributes as a FLAT [name, value, name, value, …] array.
    let attrs: Vec<(String, String)> = node
        .attributes
        .chunks_exact(2)
        .map(|pair| (pair[0].clone(), pair[1].clone()))
        .collect();
    let text = if matches!(kind, RawNodeKind::Text) && !node.node_value.is_empty() {
        Some(node.node_value.clone())
    } else {
        None
    };
    let me = out.len();
    out.push(Walked {
        node: RawNode {
            // `backendNodeId: 0` is the document on obscura. Cast, never
            // filter: treating 0 as absent drops the root.
            backend_node_id: u64::try_from(node.backend_node_id).unwrap_or(0),
            parent,
            kind,
            tag: matches!(kind, RawNodeKind::Element)
                .then(|| node.node_name.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            attrs,
            text,
            rect: None,
            computed: None,
            clickable_hint: None,
        },
        element_index,
    });
    for child in &node.children {
        walk(child, Some(me), out, element_seq);
    }
    // Shadow roots are walked so their contents are visible — as ORDINARY
    // children. Part 1's `dom::Node` still carries `shadow_roots`, but R34 cut
    // `RawNode::shadow_root`, so nothing downstream distinguishes them and a
    // flag here would have no reader. obscura returns none today, so this is a
    // branch the Chromium-shaped fixtures cover and the obscura ones do not.
    for root in &node.shadow_roots {
        walk(root, Some(me), out, element_seq);
    }
    // Present for symmetry with the CDP type. obscura never populates it
    // (measured: `pierce: true` is ignored), so on this engine the branch is
    // dead — and it is written rather than `unreachable!()` so that the day
    // obscura DOES populate it, the content appears instead of panicking.
    if let Some(doc) = &node.content_document {
        walk(doc, Some(me), out, element_seq);
    }
}

/// A quad's bounding rect, or `None` when the engine reported nothing usable.
///
/// A zero-area box is `None`, not `Some(0x0)`. On obscura every inline element
/// reports exactly that (measured: `<a>`, `<span>`), and a zero rect spent
/// downstream is a click at (0, 0) — a wrong answer that looks like an answer.
fn rect_from(model: &dom::BoxModel) -> Option<Rect> {
    let q = &model.border;
    let xs = [q[0], q[2], q[4], q[6]];
    let ys = [q[1], q[3], q[5], q[7]];
    let (min_x, max_x) = (
        xs.iter().copied().fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min),
        xs.iter().copied().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max),
    );
    let (min_y, max_y) = (
        ys.iter().copied().fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min),
        ys.iter().copied().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max),
    );
    if !min_x.is_finite() || !min_y.is_finite() {
        return None;
    }
    let w = (max_x - min_x).round();
    let h = (max_y - min_y).round();
    if w <= 0.0 || h <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    Some(Rect {
        x: min_x.round() as i32,
        y: min_y.round() as i32,
        w: w as i32,
        h: h as i32,
    })
}

/// The interim obscura fetcher.
pub async fn fetch_obscura(
    conn: &CdpConnection,
    session: &SessionId,
    box_concurrency: usize,
) -> Result<RawDom, BrowserError> {
    let concurrency = box_concurrency.max(1);

    // 1. Viewport. `cssContentSize` is the VIEWPORT on obscura (measured), not
    //    the document; recorded as reported rather than corrected, because a
    //    correction here would be this module inventing a number.
    let metrics = page::get_layout_metrics(conn, Some(session))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| BrowserError::EngineFailure {
            engine: Engine::Obscura,
            reason: format!("Page.getLayoutMetrics: {e}"),
        })?;
    let viewport = Viewport {
        width: metrics.css_visual_viewport.client_width.round().max(0.0) as u32,
        height: metrics.css_visual_viewport.client_height.round().max(0.0) as u32,
        scroll_x: metrics.css_visual_viewport.page_x.round() as i32,
        scroll_y: metrics.css_visual_viewport.page_y.round() as i32,
        content_width: metrics.css_content_size.width.round().max(0.0) as u32,
        content_height: metrics.css_content_size.height.round().max(0.0) as u32,
        dpr: metrics.css_visual_viewport.scale,
    };

    // 2. Document identity. The MAIN frame's loader id only: a child frame's
    //    is derived from its frame id and never changes (measured), so it
    //    would be a document identity that never expires.
    let tree = page::get_frame_tree(conn, Some(session))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| BrowserError::EngineFailure {
            engine: Engine::Obscura,
            reason: format!("Page.getFrameTree: {e}"),
        })?;
    // `tree.frame`, never a child's: a child frame's `loaderId` is derived from
    // its frame id and never changes (measured), so it is a document identity
    // that would never expire.
    let main = tree.frame;

    // 3. The tree.
    let root = dom::get_document(conn, Some(session), -1, true)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| BrowserError::EngineFailure {
            engine: Engine::Obscura,
            reason: format!("DOM.getDocument: {e}"),
        })?;
    let mut walked = Vec::new();
    let mut element_seq = 0usize;
    walk(&root, None, &mut walked, &mut element_seq);
    let element_count = element_seq;

    // 4. Boxes, bounded. `Ok(None)` (no box model) and `Err` (a protocol
    //    failure) both land on `rect: None` — they are different facts, but
    //    neither is a rectangle, and neither may lose the rest of the page.
    let ids: Vec<i64> = walked
        .iter()
        .filter(|w| w.element_index.is_some())
        .map(|w| i64::try_from(w.node.backend_node_id).unwrap_or(0))
        .collect();
    let boxes: HashMap<i64, Rect> = futures::stream::iter(ids.into_iter().map(|id| async move {
        let model = dom::get_box_model(conn, Some(session), id).await;
        (id, model.ok().flatten().as_ref().and_then(rect_from))
    }))
    .buffer_unordered(concurrency)
    .filter_map(|(id, rect)| async move { rect.map(|r| (id, r)) })
    .collect()
    .await;

    // 5. Computed flags, one call, cross-checked against the walk.
    let first_tag = walked
        .iter()
        .find(|w| w.element_index == Some(0))
        .and_then(|w| w.node.tag.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let last_tag = element_count
        .checked_sub(1)
        .and_then(|last| walked.iter().find(|w| w.element_index == Some(last)))
        .and_then(|w| w.node.tag.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();

    let mut rows = fetch_computed(conn, session, element_count, &first_tag, &last_tag).await;
    if rows.is_none() && element_count > 0 {
        // One retry, and one only. A page that mutates between the two calls
        // is the case this cross-check exists for; a page that mutates
        // continuously is one we stop trying to describe geometrically rather
        // than describe wrongly.
        tracing::debug!("obscura computed-flag cross-check disagreed; re-running once");
        rows = fetch_computed(conn, session, element_count, &first_tag, &last_tag).await;
        if rows.is_none() {
            tracing::warn!(
                element_count,
                "obscura computed-flag cross-check disagreed twice; the snapshot will \
                 carry no visibility flags rather than mis-attributed ones"
            );
        }
    }

    // 6. Assemble.
    let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(walked.len());
    for w in walked {
        let mut node = w.node;
        if let Some(i) = w.element_index {
            let id = i64::try_from(node.backend_node_id).unwrap_or(0);
            node.rect = boxes.get(&id).copied();
            node.computed = rows.as_ref().and_then(|r| r.get(i).copied());
            node.clickable_hint = node.computed.map(|c| c.cursor_pointer);
        }
        nodes.push(node);
    }

    Ok(RawDom {
        engine: Engine::Obscura,
        viewport,
        // Exactly one frame, always: obscura ignores `pierce` (measured).
        frames: vec![RawFrame {
            frame_id: main.id,
            loader_id: main.loader_id,
            offset: (0, 0),
            nodes,
        }],
    })
}

async fn fetch_computed(
    conn: &CdpConnection,
    session: &SessionId,
    element_count: usize,
    first_tag: &str,
    last_tag: &str,
) -> Option<Vec<Computed>> {
    let result = runtime::evaluate(conn, Some(session), COMPUTED_FLAGS_JS, false).await;
    let evaluated = match result {
        Ok(r) if r.exception.is_none() => r.value,
        // A JS exception and a transport failure are different, and neither is
        // a set of flags. Both land on `None`, which the caller renders as
        // "unknown visibility" rather than "visible".
        Ok(r) => {
            tracing::warn!(exception = ?r.exception, "obscura computed-flag evaluate threw");
            return None;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "obscura computed-flag evaluate failed");
            return None;
        }
    };
    parse_computed_rows(&evaluated, element_count, first_tag, last_tag)
}
```

**`FakeCdpServer` is `aleph_cdp::testkit::FakeCdpServer`, behind the cargo
feature `testkit`, with PART 1's API** (controller ruling R20 — Part 1 owns the
type; the constructor-shaped `scripted`/`scripted_slow` in this task's first
draft were a second design for the same name, 判据 §1). The surface, used
verbatim above:

```rust
// Free-standing responder BUILDERS, not constructors. They return the closure
// `start` takes, so a test can wrap or compose them.
pub fn scripted(entries: Vec<(&'static str, Responder)>)
    -> impl Fn(&serde_json::Value) -> Responder + Send + Sync + 'static;
pub fn scripted_slow(entries: Vec<(&'static str, Responder)>, delay: std::time::Duration)
    -> impl Fn(&serde_json::Value) -> Responder + Send + Sync + 'static;

impl FakeCdpServer {
    pub async fn start(responder: impl Fn(&serde_json::Value) -> Responder + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Self;
    pub async fn connect_and_attach(&self) -> (aleph_cdp::CdpConnection, aleph_cdp::SessionId);
}
pub enum Responder { Reply(serde_json::Value), Error { code: i64, message: String }, Delay(Duration, Box<Responder>), Drop, Event(serde_json::Value) }
```

Two consequences for this task's tests, both already applied above:

* **A `Responder::Error` is how a `DOM.getBoxModel` failure is expressed**, not
  a `None` return. `Responder::Error { code: -32000, message: "Could not compute box model".into() }`.
* **Concurrency is measured by ELAPSED TIME, not by enter/leave hooks.**
  Part 1's `Responder` cannot express a hook, and asking for one would be a
  second design again. `scripted_slow(entries, 20ms)` with eleven element nodes
  at `box_concurrency = 2` cannot finish in fewer than six serialised batches;
  unbounded finishes in about one. The two are 4x apart, which is what makes
  the assertion an effect rather than a race.

The `testkit` feature is enabled through `alephcore`'s `[dev-dependencies]`
only. The workspace sets `resolver = "2"` (`Cargo.toml:5`), so it is **not**
enabled for a plain `cargo build` of the library: the shipped binary does not
carry the fake server.

<!doctype html>
<html><head><title>stall</title></head>
<body>
  <h1>__MARKER__-stall</h1>
  <!-- Measured on obscura v0.2.2 (2026-09-06): this loop does NOT run for 20 s.
       obscura terminates it at its own autonomous-task budget after ~5 s
       ("autonomous page task failed: autonomous browser task exceeded its task
       budget" in the server log), and document.title stays "stall" rather than
       becoming "done" — i.e. the script is killed, not completed. While it
       spins, EVERY command on the connection blocks, including Target.getTargets
       which the source survey lists as v8-free. So the stage's assertion is
       about the tool reporting EngineBusy under a low cdp_command_timeout_secs,
       not about a 20 s number. The 20 s is kept so the stall outlives the
       budget on a faster machine too. -->
  <script>
    setTimeout(function () {
      var t = Date.now();
      while (Date.now() - t < 20000) {}
      document.title = "done";
    }, 300);
  </script>
</body></html>
