`qa/browser_dual/run.sh`:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Real-machine QA for the dual-engine browser stack (obscura + chromium over
# Aleph's own CDP driver).
#
#   ./qa/browser_dual/run.sh provision  # the ledger installs obscura from a
#                                       # LOCAL fixture release, sha256-checked;
#                                       # a tampered digest refuses and leaves nothing
#   ./qa/browser_dual/run.sh open       # the readiness gate: /json/version AND a
#                                       # navigate; argv and storage-dir as launched
#   ./qa/browser_dual/run.sh snapshot   # engine=obscura header, refs for the
#                                       # elements that have them, none for the ones
#                                       # obscura cannot see
#   ./qa/browser_dual/run.sh click      # by ref AND by coordinates, each changing
#                                       # the URL; a pre-navigation ref goes stale
#   ./qa/browser_dual/run.sh stall      # a spinning page yields EngineBusy and the
#                                       # engine is still alive afterwards
#   ./qa/browser_dual/run.sh reap       # kill -9 the server: the obscura orphan is
#                                       # swept, a live Chromium is NOT
#   ./qa/browser_dual/run.sh caps       # the capability table, probed against the
#                                       # real binary, verb by verb
#
# Same scratch-HOME discipline as qa/browser_managed/run.sh. No mock provider in
# any stage: every claim goes through `tools.invoke`, which runs a tool without
# an agent turn — but the config still carries a FAKE API KEY, because a server
# in `Mode: Simulated` answers `tools.invoke` with a boot-phase placeholder that
# reads exactly like a wiring failure (qa/README.md).
#
# Two real things, named up front rather than discovered at minute three:
#   * an obscura binary to build the fixture release from (ALEPH_QA_OBSCURA);
#   * a Chrome for the `reap` stage's control (ALEPH_QA_CHROME).
set -uo pipefail

STAGE="${1:-open}"
case "$STAGE" in
  provision|open|snapshot|click|stall|reap|caps) ;;
  *) echo "unknown stage: $STAGE" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
SHARED="$HERE/../busy_input"
MANAGED="$HERE/../browser_managed"

# `add_browser_config.py --cli-binary` is `required=True` (`add_browser_config.py:41`)
# and this fixture shares that script, so it must supply one even though it drives
# CDP and never invokes the CLI. Resolved exactly the way `qa/browser_managed/run.sh:93-97`
# does — same env var, same 69 — rather than relaxing a flag another fixture
# depends on being mandatory.
CLI="${PLAYWRIGHT_CLI:-$(command -v playwright-cli 2>/dev/null)}"
if [ -z "$CLI" ]; then
  echo "no playwright-cli on PATH; set PLAYWRIGHT_CLI=/path/to/playwright-cli" >&2
  echo "(this fixture drives CDP and never runs it — it is required only because" >&2
  echo " add_browser_config.py, shared with qa/browser_managed, demands the key)" >&2
  exit 69
fi

OBSCURA_BIN="${ALEPH_QA_OBSCURA:-$(command -v obscura 2>/dev/null)}"
if [ -z "$OBSCURA_BIN" ] || [ ! -x "$OBSCURA_BIN" ]; then
  echo "no obscura binary; set ALEPH_QA_OBSCURA=/path/to/obscura" >&2
  echo "(the fixture release is built FROM it, so this fixture cannot invent one)" >&2
  exit 69
fi
CHROME_BIN="${ALEPH_QA_CHROME:-/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome}"
if [ "$STAGE" = "reap" ] && [ ! -x "$CHROME_BIN" ]; then
  echo "no browser at $CHROME_BIN; set ALEPH_QA_CHROME" >&2
  echo "(the reap stage's whole claim is that a LIVE chromium survives the sweep," >&2
  echo " so without one the stage would pass by having nothing to spare)" >&2
  exit 69
fi

QA_ROOT="${QA_ROOT:-$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/aleph-qa-dual-XXXXXX")}"
KEEP="${KEEP:-0}"
GATEWAY_PORT="${GATEWAY_PORT:-18787}"
PAGE_PORT="${PAGE_PORT:-18888}"
RELEASE_PORT="${RELEASE_PORT:-18889}"
DEAD_MOCK_PORT="${DEAD_MOCK_PORT:-18999}"
MARKER="aleph-qa-dual-${RANDOM}${RANDOM}"
OBSCURA_REPO="h4ckf0r0day/obscura"
OBSCURA_TAG="v0.2.2"
# The stall stage needs the per-command timeout to be shorter than the stall it
# provokes. 3 s: comfortably under the ~5 s autonomous-task budget that ends the
# stall, and comfortably under obscura's own 60 s guillotine, which is the
# constraint the spec pins (`cdp_command_timeout_secs` must be < 60).
STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS=3

SERVER_PID=""
PAGE_PID=""
RELEASE_PID=""

say() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$*"; }

cleanup() {
  [ -n "$SERVER_PID" ] && kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null
  [ -n "$PAGE_PID" ] && kill -9 "$PAGE_PID" 2>/dev/null
  [ -n "$RELEASE_PID" ] && kill -9 "$RELEASE_PID" 2>/dev/null
  sleep 1
  [ -n "$SERVER_PID" ] && kill -9 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null
  # Anything this run launched and the server did not reap. `--` is required:
  # BSD pgrep reads a leading `-` in the pattern as an option, and the run then
  # leaves live browsers behind while reporting nothing.
  pkill -9 -f -- "--storage-dir=$QA_ROOT" 2>/dev/null
  pkill -9 -f -- "--user-data-dir=$QA_ROOT" 2>/dev/null
  if [ "$KEEP" = "1" ]; then echo "artifacts kept in $QA_ROOT"; else rm -rf "$QA_ROOT"; fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

. "$HERE/../lib/scratch_home.sh"
. "$HERE/../lib/build.sh"
qa_redirect_home "$QA_ROOT"
mkdir -p "$ALEPH_HOME"
CONFIG="$ALEPH_HOME/config.toml"
PAGEDIR="$QA_ROOT/page"
RELEASEDIR="$QA_ROOT/release"
CWD="$QA_ROOT/cwd"
CHROMIUM_UDD="$QA_ROOT/chromium-profile"
mkdir -p "$PAGEDIR" "$CWD" "$CHROMIUM_UDD"
export RUST_MIN_STACK="${RUST_MIN_STACK:-268435456}"

TARGET_DIR="$(cd "$REPO" && HOME="$REAL_HOME" cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 2>/dev/null \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["target_directory"])' 2>/dev/null)"
BIN="${TARGET_DIR:-$REPO/target}/debug/aleph-server"

say "build ($STAGE)"
if [ "${SKIP_BUILD:-0}" != "1" ]; then
  qa_build --bin aleph-server || { echo "build failed" >&2; exit 1; }
fi
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "no binary at $BIN" >&2; exit 1; }

say "serve the page fixture on 127.0.0.1:$PAGE_PORT"
for f in index second stall caps; do
  sed -e "s/__MARKER__/$MARKER/g" "$HERE/pages/$f.html" > "$PAGEDIR/$f.html"
done
(cd "$PAGEDIR" && python3 -m http.server "$PAGE_PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1) >"$QA_ROOT/page.log" 2>&1 &
PAGE_PID=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$PAGE_PORT/index.html" && break; sleep 0.3; done

# --- the fixture "GitHub" -----------------------------------------------
# A static tree, not a custom handler: the two routes the installer uses are
# ordinary paths, so `python3 -m http.server` serves them as files. The API
# document is a FILE named `v0.2.2` with no extension; the installer parses the
# body as JSON and never looks at Content-Type.
say "build a fixture release from $OBSCURA_BIN"
case "$(uname -s)" in Darwin) OS_TAG=macos ;; Linux) OS_TAG=linux ;; *) OS_TAG=unknown ;; esac
case "$(uname -m)" in arm64|aarch64) ARCH_TAG=aarch64 ;; x86_64) ARCH_TAG=x86_64 ;; *) ARCH_TAG=unknown ;; esac
ASSET="obscura-${ARCH_TAG}-${OS_TAG}.tar.gz"
STAGEDIR="$QA_ROOT/stage"
mkdir -p "$STAGEDIR" \
         "$RELEASEDIR/repos/$OBSCURA_REPO/releases/tags" \
         "$RELEASEDIR/$OBSCURA_REPO/releases/download/$OBSCURA_TAG"
cp "$OBSCURA_BIN" "$STAGEDIR/obscura"
# A second member, so an extractor that takes the first entry cannot pass by
# accident — the real archive holds `obscura` and `obscura-worker`.
printf 'not the binary\n' > "$STAGEDIR/obscura-worker"
tar -czf "$RELEASEDIR/$OBSCURA_REPO/releases/download/$OBSCURA_TAG/$ASSET" \
    -C "$STAGEDIR" obscura obscura-worker
DIGEST="$(shasum -a 256 "$RELEASEDIR/$OBSCURA_REPO/releases/download/$OBSCURA_TAG/$ASSET" | awk '{print $1}')"
# `provision` runs twice: once with the true digest (must install) and once
# with a tampered one (must refuse). The tampered value is written by drive.py
# between the two halves, so the RED control lives in the fixture rather than
# in a locally-edited file.
python3 - "$RELEASEDIR/repos/$OBSCURA_REPO/releases/tags/$OBSCURA_TAG" "$ASSET" "$DIGEST" <<'PY'
import json, sys
path, asset, digest = sys.argv[1:4]
json.dump({"tag_name": "v0.2.2", "assets": [{"name": asset, "digest": f"sha256:{digest}"}]},
          open(path, "w"))
PY
(cd "$RELEASEDIR" && python3 -m http.server "$RELEASE_PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1) >"$QA_ROOT/release.log" 2>&1 &
RELEASE_PID=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$RELEASE_PORT/repos/$OBSCURA_REPO/releases/tags/$OBSCURA_TAG" && break
  sleep 0.3
done
echo "fixture release: $ASSET sha256=$DIGEST"

say "generate a baseline config"
timeout 25 "$BIN" --port "$GATEWAY_PORT" start >"$QA_ROOT/gen.log" 2>&1 &
GEN_PID=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do [ -f "$CONFIG" ] && break; sleep 0.5; done
kill "$GEN_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$GEN_PID" 2>/dev/null
[ -f "$CONFIG" ] || { echo "no config generated at $CONFIG"; tail -20 "$QA_ROOT/gen.log"; exit 1; }

say "patch config"
python3 "$SHARED/patch_config.py" "$CONFIG" \
  --gateway-port "$GATEWAY_PORT" --mock-port "$DEAD_MOCK_PORT" || exit 1
BROWSER_CFG_ARGS=(
  --cli-binary "$CLI"
  --runtime-download-host "http://127.0.0.1:$RELEASE_PORT"
  --user-data-dir "$CHROMIUM_UDD"
  --headless true
)
# Every stage but `provision` needs an obscura that is already there; pinning
# it is what keeps those stages from depending on a network install. `provision`
# is the one stage that must NOT have the pin, or it would test nothing.
if [ "$STAGE" != "provision" ]; then
  BROWSER_CFG_ARGS+=(--obscura-binary-path "$OBSCURA_BIN")
fi
if [ "$STAGE" = "stall" ]; then
  BROWSER_CFG_ARGS+=(--cdp-command-timeout-secs "$STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS")
fi
if [ "$STAGE" = "reap" ] || [ "$STAGE" = "open" ]; then
  # A second profile on the OTHER engine. `reap` needs it so the sweep has
  # something it must SPARE — without it the stage proves only that the sweep
  # kills things. `open` needs it because spec §7.4 says the readiness gate is
  # proven "对两引擎都成立", and a stage that only ever launches obscura does not
  # say anything about the other engine's gate or about `--use-mock-keychain`,
  # whose absence is round-7's headline defect (a Chrome that answers
  # /json/version while every first navigation silently dies).
  BROWSER_CFG_ARGS+=(
    --profile-engine "escape=chromium"
    --runtime-binary-path "$CHROME_BIN"
    --prefer-system-browser false
  )
fi
if [ "$STAGE" = "open" ] && [ ! -x "$CHROME_BIN" ]; then
  echo "no browser at $CHROME_BIN; set ALEPH_QA_CHROME" >&2
  echo "(the open stage proves the readiness gate on BOTH engines — spec §7.4)" >&2
  exit 69
fi
python3 "$MANAGED/add_browser_config.py" "$CONFIG" "${BROWSER_CFG_ARGS[@]}" || exit 1

# `$ALEPH_HOME`, not `$HOME/.aleph`: `qa_redirect_home` already exported it, and
# spelling the path a second way makes a latent second author out of two strings
# that happen to be equal today.
cat > "$ALEPH_HOME/approval-policy.json" <<'JSON'
{"defaults":{
  "browser_open":"allow","browser_navigate":"allow","browser_click":"allow",
  "browser_type":"allow","browser_evaluate":"allow","browser_session_state":"allow"
},"allowlist":[],"blocklist":[]}
JSON

say "start server (cwd=$CWD)"
(cd "$CWD" && "$BIN" start) >"$QA_ROOT/server.log" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
  curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$GATEWAY_PORT/health" && break
  kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || { echo "server died"; tail -40 "$QA_ROOT/server.log"; exit 1; }
  sleep 1
done
echo "gateway up on $GATEWAY_PORT"

say "drive: $STAGE"
RC=0
if [ "$STAGE" = "caps" ]; then
  python3 "$HERE/caps.py" \
    "ws://127.0.0.1:$GATEWAY_PORT/ws" \
    --page-url "http://127.0.0.1:$PAGE_PORT/caps.html" \
    --aleph-home "$ALEPH_HOME" \
    --chrome "$CHROME_BIN" || RC=$?
else
  python3 "$HERE/drive.py" \
    "ws://127.0.0.1:$GATEWAY_PORT/ws" "$STAGE" \
    --page-url "http://127.0.0.1:$PAGE_PORT/index.html" \
    --stall-url "http://127.0.0.1:$PAGE_PORT/stall.html" \
    --second-url "http://127.0.0.1:$PAGE_PORT/second.html" \
    --marker "$MARKER" \
    --qa-root "$QA_ROOT" \
    --aleph-home "$ALEPH_HOME" \
    --release-dir "$RELEASEDIR" \
    --release-repo "$OBSCURA_REPO" \
    --release-tag "$OBSCURA_TAG" \
    --asset "$ASSET" \
    --digest "$DIGEST" \
    --server-bin "$BIN" \
    --server-cwd "$CWD" \
    --gateway-port "$GATEWAY_PORT" \
    --server-pid "$SERVER_PID" \
    --stall-timeout "$STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS" \
    --chromium-udd "$CHROMIUM_UDD" || RC=$?
  # `reap` restarts the server itself, so it owns the pid from that point on.
  # Cleared ONLY on a clean exit: clearing it unconditionally orphans the
  # server (and every browser it launched) whenever the driver dies before the
  # restart — the bug qa/browser_managed/run.sh:419-427 records.
  if [ "$STAGE" = "reap" ] && [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
    SERVER_PID=""
  fi
fi

say "server log tail"
LOGDIR="$ALEPH_HOME/logs"
if [ -d "$LOGDIR" ]; then
  grep -iE "obscura|engine|browser|reap" "$LOGDIR"/aleph-server.log* 2>/dev/null | tail -25
else
  tail -25 "$QA_ROOT/server.log"
fi

say "verdict: rc=$RC"
exit "$RC"
```

`qa/browser_dual/drive.py` — the six non-`caps` stages. Every claim asserts an EFFECT.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage drivers for qa/browser_dual. One websocket, `tools.invoke`, and
out-of-band oracles (`ps`, the sidecar JSON, the installed file) for everything
the code under test would otherwise be asked to confirm about itself."""
import argparse, asyncio, glob, json, os, subprocess, sys, time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "browser_managed"))
from qa_rpc import Ledger, Rpc, ws_connect, http_json  # noqa: E402


def ps_lines(pattern):
    """Full command lines of live processes matching `pattern`.

    `pgrep -f -- "<pat>"`: the `--` is required, because BSD pgrep reads a
    leading `-` in the pattern as one of its own options and then matches
    nothing — which reads exactly like "the process is gone" and would make
    every death assertion below pass for free."""
    out = subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-f", "--", pattern], capture_output=True, text=True)
    pids = [p for p in out.stdout.split() if p.strip()]
    lines = []
    for pid in pids:
        ps = subprocess.run(["ps", "-p", pid, "-o", "command="], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if ps.returncode == 0 and ps.stdout.strip():
            lines.append((int(pid), ps.stdout.strip()))
    return lines


def sidecars(aleph_home):
    """Every engine sidecar record, whatever leaf directory holds them.

    Globbed rather than hard-coded: the registry leaf is `engine/process.rs`'s
    business and this fixture must not be a second place that decides it. An
    empty result is reported as a FAILED claim, never skipped — "I looked
    nowhere" and "there is nothing" are different answers."""
    out = {}
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(aleph_home, "data", "browser", "*", "*.json")):
        try:
            with open(path) as fh:
                out[path] = json.load(fh)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            out[path] = None
    return out


async def stage_provision(rpc, led, a):
    installed = os.path.join(a.aleph_home, "runtimes", "obscura", a.release_tag, "obscura")
    led.check("no obscura is installed before the stage starts", not os.path.exists(installed), installed)

    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("runtime_manage", {"action": "install", "capability": "obscura"})
    led.check("runtime_manage accepts capability=obscura", ok, json.dumps(body)[:200])
    job = (body or {}).get("process_id") or (body or {}).get("job_id")
    if job:
        await rpc.invoke("bash", {"process_action": "wait", "process_id": job})
    else:
        # No job id means the tool ran the install inline; either way the
        # assertion below is about the file, not about the mechanism.
        led.check("the install reported a pollable job", False, json.dumps(body)[:300])

    for _ in range(120):
        if os.path.exists(installed):
            break
        time.sleep(1)
    led.check("the binary landed at the ledger's tag-named path", os.path.exists(installed), installed)
    led.check("it is executable", os.access(installed, os.X_OK))
    ver = subprocess.run([installed, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    led.check("`--version` reports the pinned tag", "0.2.2" in ver.stdout, ver.stdout.strip())
    led.check(
        "obscura-worker was NOT installed",
        not os.path.exists(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(installed), "obscura-worker")),
    )
    rows = [r for r in (await rpc.invoke("runtime_manage", {"action": "list"}))[1].get("runtimes", [])
            if r["name"] == "obscura"]
    led.check("runtime_manage{list} shows exactly one obscura row", len(rows) == 1, str(rows))
    led.check("and it reports Ready", rows and rows[0]["status"].startswith("Ready"), str(rows))

    # --- the RED half, in the fixture rather than in a local edit -----------
    api = os.path.join(a.release_dir, "repos", a.release_repo, "releases", "tags", a.release_tag)
    with open(api) as fh:
        doc = json.load(fh)
    doc["assets"][0]["digest"] = "sha256:" + ("0" * 64)
    with open(api, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(doc, fh)
    import shutil
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.dirname(installed), ignore_errors=True)

    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("runtime_manage", {"action": "install", "capability": "obscura"})
    job = (body or {}).get("process_id") or (body or {}).get("job_id")
    if job:
        await rpc.invoke("bash", {"process_action": "wait", "process_id": job})
    time.sleep(3)
    led.check("a tampered digest installs NOTHING", not os.path.exists(installed), installed)
    part = glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(installed), "*.part"))
    led.check("and leaves no partial download behind", not part, str(part))
    log = open(os.path.join(a.qa_root, "server.log")).read() + "".join(
        open(p).read() for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(a.aleph_home, "logs", "aleph-server.log*")))
    led.check("and the refusal names both hashes", a.digest in log and "0" * 64 in log)


async def stage_open(rpc, led, a):
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "default", "url": a.page_url})
    led.check("browser_open on the default profile succeeds", ok, json.dumps(body)[:300])

    procs = ps_lines("obscura serve")
    led.check("an `obscura serve` process is running", len(procs) >= 1, str(procs))
    argv = procs[0][1] if procs else ""
    led.check("its storage-dir is under the scratch root, as ONE argv token",
              f"--storage-dir={a.qa_root}" in argv or f"--storage-dir={a.aleph_home}" in argv, argv)
    led.check("it binds loopback explicitly", "--host=127.0.0.1" in argv, argv)
    led.check("it was NOT given --allow-file-access", "--allow-file-access" not in argv, argv)

    cars = sidecars(a.aleph_home)
    led.check("a sidecar record exists", bool(cars), str(list(cars)))
    ours = [r for r in cars.values() if r and r.get("engine") == "obscura"]
    led.check("and it records engine=obscura", len(ours) == 1, json.dumps(list(cars.values()))[:300])
    http = ours[0].get("http_url") if ours else None
    led.check("with an endpoint (the second write happened)", bool(http), str(http))

    port = int(http.rsplit(":", 1)[1])
    status, ver = http_json(port, "/json/version")
    led.check("/json/version answers on that endpoint", status == 200, str(status))
    # The readiness gate's OTHER half: the engine navigated. `/json/version`
    # alone is the sentinel plan 1 recorded as insufficient — Chrome answered
    # it while every first navigation silently died.
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_evaluate",
                                {"profile": "default", "script": "document.title"})
    led.check("and the page really navigated", ok and "QA" in json.dumps(body), json.dumps(body)[:200])

    owner = subprocess.run(
        ["lsof", "-a", "-nP", f"-iTCP:{port}", "-sTCP:LISTEN", "-Fp"],
        capture_output=True, text=True)
    owner_pid = next((int(l[1:]) for l in owner.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("p")), None)
    led.check("the obscura we launched owns the port", owner_pid == procs[0][0],
              f"listener pid {owner_pid}, obscura pid {procs[0][0] if procs else None}")

    # --- the OTHER engine's gate (spec §7.4: 就绪门对两引擎都成立) ------------
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "escape", "url": a.page_url})
    led.check("browser_open on the chromium profile succeeds", ok, json.dumps(body)[:300])
    chrome = ps_lines(f"--user-data-dir={a.chromium_udd}")
    led.check("a chromium is running", bool(chrome), str(chrome))
    chrome_argv = chrome[0][1] if chrome else ""
    # Round-7's headline defect: without this switch Chrome answers
    # /json/version and looks healthy while every first navigation per page
    # silently dies. The spec names it explicitly for this stage.
    led.check("its argv still carries --use-mock-keychain",
              "--use-mock-keychain" in chrome_argv, chrome_argv)
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_evaluate",
                                {"profile": "escape", "script": "document.title"})
    led.check("and the chromium profile really navigated",
              ok and "QA" in json.dumps(body), json.dumps(body)[:200])
    cars = sidecars(a.aleph_home)
    led.check("its sidecar records engine=chromium",
              any(r and r.get("engine") == "chromium" for r in cars.values()),
              json.dumps(list(cars.values()))[:300])


async def stage_snapshot(rpc, led, a):
    await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "default", "url": a.page_url})
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_snapshot", {"profile": "default"})
    led.check("browser_snapshot succeeds", ok, json.dumps(body)[:200])
    text = (body or {}).get("snapshot_text", "")
    head = text.splitlines()[0] if text else ""
    led.check("the header names the engine", "engine=obscura" in head, head)
    led.check("the header names the url", a.page_url in head or "index.html" in head, head)
    led.check("the header reports the no-box count", "no_box=" in head, head)
    led.check("the link has a ref", "[ref=" in text and "go by ref" in text, text[:600])
    led.check("the block clickable has a ref", "go by coordinates" in text, text[:600])
    # The two elements obscura CAN see as hidden, via the computed flags rather
    # than via a box (measured: an inline element's box is zero either way).
    led.check("a display:none element is not offered", f"{a.marker}-hidden" not in text, text[:600])
    led.check("an opacity:0 element is not offered", f"{a.marker}-ghost" not in text, text[:600])
    led.check("ref_count agrees with the rendered refs",
              (body or {}).get("ref_count", 0) == text.count("[ref="),
              f"{(body or {}).get('ref_count')} vs {text.count('[ref=')}")


async def stage_click(rpc, led, a):
    await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "default", "url": a.page_url})
    _, snap = await rpc.invoke("browser_snapshot", {"profile": "default"})
    text = snap.get("snapshot_text", "")
    ref = next((ln.split("[ref=")[1].split("]")[0] for ln in text.splitlines()
                if "[ref=" in ln and "go by ref" in ln), None)
    led.check("the link's ref is in the snapshot", ref is not None, text[:600])

    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_click", {"profile": "default", "ref": ref})
    led.check("click by ref succeeds", ok, json.dumps(body)[:200])
    _, ev = await rpc.invoke("browser_evaluate", {"profile": "default", "script": "location.pathname"})
    led.check("…and the URL changed", "second" in json.dumps(ev), json.dumps(ev)[:200])

    # The stale half: that ref was minted against the previous document.
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_click", {"profile": "default", "ref": ref})
    # `(not ok) and "stale" in …`, never `not ok or …`. The disjunction passes
    # whenever the click fails for ANY reason — a dead engine, a refused
    # connection, a denied approval — so 判据 §2's question ("when does this go
    # red?") had only one answer left: the click succeeded AND said nothing
    # about staleness. A dead engine read as a correct stale-ref refusal.
    led.check("the pre-navigation ref is now stale",
              (not ok) and "stale" in json.dumps(body).lower(),
              json.dumps(body)[:300])
    led.check("and the refusal names the way out", "browser_snapshot" in json.dumps(body),
              json.dumps(body)[:300])

    # Coordinates, on the BLOCK element. Not on the link: measured on obscura
    # v0.2.2, an inline element reports a zero box from every route, so a
    # coordinate click on it would be a click at (0, 0) — and a stage that
    # aimed there would be testing the wrong thing whichever way it came out.
    await rpc.invoke("browser_navigate", {"profile": "default", "url": a.page_url})
    _, snap = await rpc.invoke("browser_snapshot", {"profile": "default"})
    state = snap.get("state_json") or {}
    blk = next((n for n in state.get("nodes", []) if "coordinates" in (n.get("name") or "")), None)
    led.check("the block clickable has a rect", blk and blk.get("rect"), json.dumps(blk)[:300])
    rect = blk["rect"]
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_click", {
        "profile": "default",
        "x": rect["x"] + rect["w"] // 2,
        "y": rect["y"] + rect["h"] // 2,
    })
    led.check("click by coordinates succeeds", ok, json.dumps(body)[:200])
    _, ev = await rpc.invoke("browser_evaluate", {"profile": "default", "script": "location.pathname"})
    led.check("…and the URL changed", "second" in json.dumps(ev), json.dumps(ev)[:200])

    # The measured gap, asserted so it cannot improve silently: the day obscura
    # grows inline layout, this claim flips and someone reads the note.
    await rpc.invoke("browser_navigate", {"profile": "default", "url": a.page_url})
    _, snap = await rpc.invoke("browser_snapshot", {"profile": "default"})
    state = snap.get("state_json") or {}
    lnk = next((n for n in state.get("nodes", []) if "by ref" in (n.get("name") or "")), None)
    # Scoped to THIS page on purpose: T0's U9 probe is what says how far the
    # gap reaches, and the spike's M11 measured HN elements that did have real
    # boxes. If this claim starts failing, obscura laid out an inline element
    # and someone should read U9 again — which is the whole point of asserting
    # a gap you expect rather than leaving it in a comment.
    led.check("KNOWN GAP (see T0 U9): this inline link has no rect on obscura v0.2.2",
              lnk is not None and lnk.get("rect") is None, json.dumps(lnk)[:300])


async def stage_stall(rpc, led, a):
    await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "default", "url": a.stall_url})
    before = ps_lines("obscura serve")
    led.check("obscura is running before the stall", bool(before), str(before))
    time.sleep(1.5)  # the page arms its loop 300 ms after load
    t0 = time.time()
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_snapshot", {"profile": "default"})
    waited = time.time() - t0
    blob = json.dumps(body)
    led.check("the stalled call was refused, not hung forever", waited < 60, f"{waited:.1f}s")
    led.check("the refusal is EngineBusy", "EngineBusy" in blob or "engine_busy" in blob, blob[:300])
    led.check("and it says how long it waited", "waited" in blob.lower(), blob[:300])
    led.check("and it names the way across", "switch_engine" in blob, blob[:300])
    led.check("the wait was about the configured timeout, not instant",
              waited >= a.stall_timeout * 0.5, f"{waited:.1f}s vs {a.stall_timeout}s")

    after = ps_lines("obscura serve")
    led.check("the engine is STILL ALIVE afterwards", {p for p, _ in after} == {p for p, _ in before},
              f"{before} -> {after}")
    # Measured: obscura ends the page's own task at its autonomous budget, so
    # the engine recovers by itself. A stage that stopped at EngineBusy would
    # not notice a driver that had left the connection wedged.
    time.sleep(8)
    ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_evaluate", {"profile": "default", "script": "1+1"})
    led.check("the engine answers again once the page stops spinning", ok, json.dumps(body)[:200])
    led.check("and the page's own script was terminated, not completed",
              "done" not in json.dumps(
                  (await rpc.invoke("browser_evaluate",
                                    {"profile": "default", "script": "document.title"}))[1]),
              "document.title")


async def stage_reap(rpc, led, a):
    await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "default", "url": a.page_url})
    await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "escape", "url": a.page_url})
    obs = ps_lines(f"--storage-dir={a.aleph_home}")
    chrome = ps_lines(f"--user-data-dir={a.chromium_udd}")
    led.check("an obscura is running", bool(obs), str(obs))
    led.check("a chromium is running too", bool(chrome), str(chrome))

    os.kill(int(a.server_pid), 9)
    time.sleep(2)
    led.check("both engines survived the server's death (they are orphans now)",
              bool(ps_lines(f"--storage-dir={a.aleph_home}")) and bool(ps_lines(f"--user-data-dir={a.chromium_udd}")))

    proc = subprocess.Popen([a.server_bin, "start"], cwd=a.server_cwd,
                            stdout=open(os.path.join(a.qa_root, "server2.log"), "w"),
                            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    for _ in range(90):
        try:
            http_json(int(a.gateway_port), "/health")
            break
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(1)
    time.sleep(5)

    led.check("the obscura orphan was swept", not ps_lines(f"--storage-dir={a.aleph_home}"),
              str(ps_lines(f"--storage-dir={a.aleph_home}")))
    # The half that makes the other half mean something: a sweep that killed
    # everything would pass the first claim on its own.
    led.check("the LIVE chromium was NOT killed", bool(ps_lines(f"--user-data-dir={a.chromium_udd}")),
              str(ps_lines(f"--user-data-dir={a.chromium_udd}")))
    print(f"restarted server pid {proc.pid}", flush=True)


STAGES = {"provision": stage_provision, "open": stage_open, "snapshot": stage_snapshot,
          "click": stage_click, "stall": stage_stall, "reap": stage_reap}


async def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("ws"); p.add_argument("stage")
    for flag in ("page-url", "stall-url", "second-url", "marker", "qa-root", "aleph-home",
                 "release-dir", "release-repo", "release-tag", "asset", "digest",
                 "server-bin", "server-cwd", "gateway-port", "server-pid", "chromium-udd"):
        p.add_argument f"--{flag}"  # noqa  (written out per-flag in the real file)
    p.add_argument("--stall-timeout", type=float, default=3.0)
    a = p.parse_args()
    led = Ledger()
    async with ws_connect(a.ws) as ws:
        rpc = Rpc(ws)
        await rpc.connect("qa-browser-dual")
        await STAGES[a.stage](rpc, led, a)
    return led.verdict()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
```
(The `add_argument` loop above is shorthand for the reader; in the real file
write the sixteen `p.add_argument("--page-url")` lines out, because argparse's
`dest` mangling is exactly the kind of cleverness a fixture should not have.)

`qa/browser_dual/caps.py` — the capability table, falsified verb by verb.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Probe the REAL obscura for each row of the capability table and diff against
`browser_session{action:"capabilities"}`.

A name list only covers the world as it was on the day it was written (判据 §5).
This is that list's expiry check, and it is deliberately built out of EFFECTS:
`Input.dispatchTouchEvent` is ROUTED on obscura — to `Ok(json!({}))` — so a
probe that only checked for a protocol error would report touch as supported.
The probe fires a touch at a listener and reads the flag it should have set."""
import argparse, asyncio, base64, json, os, subprocess, sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "browser_managed"))
from qa_rpc import Ledger, Rpc, ws_connect  # noqa: E402
import websockets  # noqa: E402


class Raw:
    """A raw CDP connection, so the probes reach verbs Aleph's tools do not."""

    def __init__(self, ws):
        self.ws, self._id = ws, 0

    async def call(self, method, params=None, session=None):
        self._id += 1
        msg = {"id": self._id, "method": method, "params": params or {}}
        if session:
            msg["sessionId"] = session
        await self.ws.send(json.dumps(msg))
        while True:
            m = json.loads(await asyncio.wait_for(self.ws.recv(), timeout=90))
            if m.get("id") == self._id:
                return m


async def probe_obscura(ws_url, page_url, led):
    async with websockets.connect(ws_url, max_size=None, ping_interval=None) as ws:
        cdp = Raw(ws)
        made = await cdp.call("Target.createTarget", {"url": "about:blank"})
        tid = made["result"]["targetId"]
        att = await cdp.call("Target.attachToTarget", {"targetId": tid, "flatten": True})
        s = att["result"]["sessionId"]
        await cdp.call("Page.enable", {}, s)
        await cdp.call("Runtime.enable", {}, s)
        await cdp.call("Page.navigate", {"url": page_url}, s)
        await asyncio.sleep(2.5)

        async def ev(expr):
            r = await cdp.call("Runtime.evaluate",
                               {"expression": expr, "returnByValue": True}, s)
            return r.get("result", {}).get("result", {}).get("value")

        found = {}

        r = await cdp.call("Page.handleJavaScriptDialog", {"accept": True}, s)
        found["js_dialogs"] = "supported" if "error" not in r else "unsupported"

        r = await cdp.call("Input.dispatchDragEvent",
                           {"type": "dragOver", "x": 10, "y": 10, "data": {"items": []}}, s)
        found["drag"] = "supported" if "error" not in r else "unsupported"

        # `touch`, `screencast`, `network_interception` and `multi_connection`
        # are NOT probed here, and their absence is the point: R39 cut them
        # from the capability table because no `browser_*` verb dispatches
        # them. A QA stage that kept probing them would be measuring something
        # the table no longer claims — and the diff below would fail on the
        # prober's surplus rather than on a wrong claim.
        doc = await cdp.call("DOM.getDocument", {"depth": -1}, s)

        def find(node, tag, ident):
            if node.get("nodeName", "").lower() == tag:
                attrs = node.get("attributes", [])
                pairs = dict(zip(attrs[::2], attrs[1::2]))
                if pairs.get("id") == ident:
                    return node["backendNodeId"]
            for c in node.get("children", []):
                got = find(c, tag, ident)
                if got is not None:
                    return got
            return None

        file_id = find(doc["result"]["root"], "input", "file")
        tmp = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".caps-upload.txt")
        with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
            fh.write("caps")
        await cdp.call("DOM.setFileInputFiles", {"backendNodeId": file_id, "files": [tmp]}, s)
        found["file_upload"] = "supported" if await ev(
            "document.getElementById('file').files.length === 1") else "unsupported"
        os.remove(tmp)

        r = await cdp.call("Page.printToPDF", {}, s)
        data = r.get("result", {}).get("data", "")
        found["pdf"] = "supported" if data and base64.b64decode(data)[:4] == b"%PDF" else "unsupported"

        txt_id = find(doc["result"]["root"], "input", "txt")
        await cdp.call("DOM.focus", {"backendNodeId": txt_id}, s)
        await cdp.call("Input.insertText", {"text": "caps-probe"}, s)
        found["insert_text"] = "supported" if await ev(
            "document.getElementById('txt').value === 'caps-probe'") else "unsupported"

        return found


async def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("ws")
    p.add_argument("--page-url", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--aleph-home", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--chrome", required=True)
    a = p.parse_args()
    led = Ledger()

    async with ws_connect(a.ws) as gw:
        rpc = Rpc(gw)
        await rpc.connect("qa-browser-dual-caps")
        await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"profile": "default", "url": a.page_url})
        ok, body = await rpc.invoke("browser_session", {"action": "capabilities"})
        led.check("browser_session{capabilities} answers", ok, json.dumps(body)[:200])
        table = (body or {}).get("capabilities", {})
        led.check("it carries both engines", set(table) >= {"obscura", "chromium"}, str(list(table)))

        import glob
        http = None
        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(a.aleph_home, "data", "browser", "*", "*.json")):
            rec = json.load(open(path))
            if rec.get("engine") == "obscura":
                http = rec.get("http_url")
        led.check("the obscura endpoint is known from its sidecar", bool(http), str(http))
        port = int(http.rsplit(":", 1)[1])

        measured = await probe_obscura(f"ws://127.0.0.1:{port}/devtools/browser", a.page_url, led)

    claimed = table.get("obscura", {})
    for name, got in sorted(measured.items()):
        led.check(f"obscura.{name}: the table says what the binary does",
                  claimed.get(name) == got, f"table={claimed.get(name)} measured={got}")
    led.check("every claimed row was probed",
              set(claimed) - {"measured_on"} == set(measured),
              f"claimed={sorted(set(claimed) - {'measured_on'})} probed={sorted(measured)}")
    led.check("the obscura row says what it was measured on",
              claimed.get("measured_on") == "v0.2.2", str(claimed.get("measured_on")))
    # Chromium's row is UNRUN here, and says so rather than passing: probing it
    # needs a second launch, and an unrun claim reported as a pass is the
    # failure mode qa/README.md records for spend_budget on Windows.
    print("  [UNRUN] chromium.* — not probed by this stage; the chromium row is "
          "asserted in src/browser/engine/capability.rs and exercised by "
          "qa/browser_managed under ALEPH_QA_DRIVER=cdp", flush=True)
    return led.verdict()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
```

```
                                   # release; a tampered sha256 refuses and leaves nothing

                                   # get refs, display:none and opacity:0 do not

                                   # a pre-navigation ref reports StaleRef
./qa/browser_dual/run.sh stall     # a spinning page yields EngineBusy under a 3 s
                                   # cdp_command_timeout_secs, and the engine survives
./qa/browser_dual/run.sh reap      # kill -9 the server: the obscura orphan is swept and
                                   # a LIVE chromium is not (needs ALEPH_QA_CHROME)
./qa/browser_dual/run.sh caps      # the capability table, probed against the real binary
```
and a prose entry beside the `browser_managed` one:
```
`browser_dual` needs two real binaries and says so at second zero: an obscura
(`ALEPH_QA_OBSCURA`, or one on PATH) and — for `reap` only — a Chrome
(`ALEPH_QA_CHROME`). A missing one exits 69, not 0.

It exists because the three things this round can get wrong are all invisible
to a fake engine. **`provision`** is the only place the sha256 gate is ever
exercised against bytes that came off a socket; it runs the install twice, the
second time with a digest the fixture itself tampers with, so the RED control is
in the repository rather than in someone's working copy. **`stall`** is the only
place `EngineBusy` is produced by an engine that is genuinely wedged — measured
on v0.2.2, a page busy-loop blocks *every* command on the connection, including
`Target.getTargets`, which the source survey lists as lock-free; obscura then
ends the page's own task at its autonomous budget after ~5 s and recovers, so
the stage also asserts that the engine answers again and that the page's script
was *terminated* (`document.title` never becomes `done`) rather than finishing.
**`reap`** is the only place the sweep's negative half is checked: a sweep that
killed everything would pass "the orphan is gone" on its own, so the stage keeps
a live Chromium beside the obscura and requires it to survive.

Two measured facts shape the fixtures rather than being asserted in prose.
On the page this fixture serves, obscura v0.2.2 gives **no box to the inline
elements** — `<a>` and `<span>` report a zero quad from `DOM.getBoxModel`,
`DOM.getContentQuads` and `getBoundingClientRect()` alike. How far that
generalises is T0's U9 question (an earlier spike measured HN elements that did
have real boxes), so `click`'s coordinate half aims at a block-level
`<div onclick>` — which has a box on any answer — and the inline link's missing
rect is asserted as a KNOWN GAP that flips if U9 or upstream narrows it. And obscura ignores
`pierce: true`, so an `<iframe>`'s contents never appear in a snapshot; the
fixture page carries no iframe rather than asserting a hole.
```

## Part 6 — Stage S5 + S6 — engine switch with migration, docs, upstream, verification (Tasks 19–20)

### Part 6 deviations (skeleton → HEAD)

Each line is `skeleton says X → Y because <file:line>`. Y is used consistently below.

1. **`describe_for_tool() -> String` is not the tool's `DESCRIPTION`, and does not try to be.**
   `AlephTool::DESCRIPTION` is `const DESCRIPTION: &'static str` (`src/tools/traits.rs:69`), and
   `BuiltinToolDefinition.description` is `&'static str` inside the `const BUILTIN_TOOL_DEFINITIONS`
   array (`src/executor/builtin_registry/definitions.rs:73`, `:81`), whose module doc forbids a
   literal that is not the tool's own const (`definitions.rs:20-42`, guard
   `no_catalog_entry_inlines_its_description` at `:1664`).
   → **Y** (controller ruling; Task 16 implements it at `part-5-obscura.md:3745-3776`): the
   capability table reaches the model as a **tool result** — `browser_session{action:"capabilities"}`
   — and the const carries one static pointer sentence. Nothing in this plan generates description
   text at runtime.
   **Consequence for Task 19**: the "what migrates / what does not" list is static prose about a
   design decision, not a rendering of a runtime table, so it is a plain literal appended to that
   const — no `MIGRATION_ROWS`, no `describe_migration()`, no guard test. The cost is stated in
   Step 4's review obligation instead of hidden.

2. **`BrowserSessionArgs.name` is already `Option<String>` — Task 16 did it.**
   `part-5-obscura.md:3717-3729` ships `#[serde(default)] pub name: Option<String>` together with
   its own refusal message, because `capabilities` has no session to name. Task 19 therefore adds
   **only** `engine` and `migrate`, and **does not** touch the name check or its message. (An
   earlier draft of this part re-decided this; it is settled in Part 5.)

3. **`EngineProcess::kill` takes the `Launched`, not a pid** (Task 9 deviation 11,
   `part-3-handle-pagestate.md:11`): `async fn kill(&self, launched: &Launched, grace: Duration)`,
   with `Launched.child: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::process::Child>>>`. Task 19 never calls
   it — every teardown goes through `EngineHandle::shutdown()` — so only the test fake must match.

4. **Two new `EngineRegistry` primitives, and the reason they had to exist** (controller ruling,
   landing in Task 9). `EngineRegistry::handle` is keyed by `req.profile` and refuses with
   `EngineMismatch` when the parked handle's engine differs (`part-3-handle-pagestate.md:1436-1445`).
   So the switch **cannot** be written as "launch the target, then kill the source": while the
   source is parked under the profile, launching the target through `handle` is exactly the case
   that arm rejects. Nor may the source be removed first — that would leave the profile with no
   engine across a launch that might fail, which is the failure mode the whole ordering exists to
   prevent. Task 9 therefore adds:
   - `pub async fn launch_detached(&self, engine: Engine, req: &LaunchRequest) -> Result<Arc<EngineHandle>, BrowserError>`
     — the launch body of `handle` with the map lookup and the map insert removed. The handle it
     returns belongs to the caller and is in no map, so a failure costs only that handle.
   - `pub async fn replace(&self, profile: &str, new: Arc<EngineHandle>) -> Option<Arc<EngineHandle>>`
     — one locked swap returning the displaced handle. Atomic on purpose: `remove` + `insert` leaves
     a window in which the profile has no engine and a concurrent `browser_open` would launch a
     third one.

5. **One new `BrowserError` variant, not two.** `EngineMismatch` is Task 9's
   (`part-3-handle-pagestate.md:41,200`). Task 19 adds only `AlreadyOnEngine { profile, engine }`,
   for a switch to the engine already running — which `EngineMismatch` cannot express, because it
   is the *opposite* mismatch.

6. **Approval default: the same curated decision as `browser_open`** (ruling **R6**).
   `ActionType::BrowserSwitchEngine` gets `DefaultDecision::Ask` — `BrowserOpen`'s value
   (`src/approval/config.rs:328`) — plus `inherited_from() -> Some(BrowserOpen)`
   (`src/approval/types.rs:124-131`), so an operator whose policy file already names `"browser_open"`
   covers the switch without a second key, which is what 「别造第二道没有把手的门」 asks for. The verb
   does *more* than opening a tab (it starts a second browser process and copies every cookie into
   it), so a looser default than `browser_open` was never available.
   ⚠️ An earlier spec draft wrote this row as 「默认放行」 immediately followed by 「它不比
   `browser_open` 更危险」 — two clauses of one sentence contradicting each other, the second being
   what it meant. **The spec has since been corrected itself**, so this is a deviation from a draft,
   not from the spec as it stands. Do not re-narrate it as "the spec says X" (判据 §1: once a
   quotation is written down, every revision on the quoted side turns the quoting side into the
   lying half).

7. **`SnapshotOutput.page_url` / `page_title` are `Option<String>`** after Task 12
   (`part-4-cdp-backend.md:47`), not the `String` they are at HEAD. `SwitchReport.snapshot` carries
   whatever Task 12 shipped and Task 19 reads only `snapshot_text`.

Create `src/browser/cdp_backend/migration.rs` containing ONLY `use super::*;` and the test module
below. It will not compile (nothing it names exists); that is the RED.

Two things about these tests are load-bearing and must not be "simplified" later:

1. **`Target.getTargets` answers `[]` in every fake here.** That is what real obscura answers even
   on its own connection (ruling R13; Part 4 makes it that module's most important mutation,
   `part-4-cdp-backend.md:2312`). A fake that answered truthfully would let an implementation
   resolve tab URLs through target enumeration, stay green, and carry **zero tabs** on a real
   obscura → Chromium switch. The URL comes from `TabEntry.url`, which Part 4 keeps true from
   main-frame `Page.frameNavigated`.
2. The assertions read **the bytes the fake received, in order**. "Cookies were installed before the
   first tab was opened" is a sequence claim, and a membership check cannot express it.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use aleph_cdp::testkit::{FakeCdpServer, Responder};
    use serde_json::json;

    /// Every method name the fake saw, in order.
    fn methods(server: &FakeCdpServer) -> Vec<String> {
        server
            .received()
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|m| m.get("method")?.as_str().map(str::to_string))
            .collect()
    }

    /// A source engine with one tab on https://example.com/a, one cookie, one
    /// localStorage pair, scrolled to y=480.
    ///
    /// `Target.getTargets` answers `[]` on purpose — see the note above the
    /// module. Any implementation that reads tab URLs from the enumeration
    /// fails here, which is the whole reason the fake is written this way.
    async fn source_server() -> FakeCdpServer {
        FakeCdpServer::start(|req| {
            let method = req.get("method").and_then(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
            let expr = req
                .get("params")
                .and_then(|p| p.get("expression"))
                .and_then(|e| e.as_str())
                .unwrap_or("");
            match method {
                "Target.getTargets" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "targetInfos": [] })),
                "Network.getAllCookies" => Responder::Reply(json!({
                    "cookies": [{
                        "name": "sid", "value": "abc123", "domain": "example.com",
                        "path": "/", "expires": -1.0, "httpOnly": true,
                        "secure": false, "sameSite": "Lax"
                    }]
                })),
                "Runtime.evaluate" if expr.contains("scrollX") => Responder::Reply(json!({
                    "result": { "type": "object", "value": [0, 480] }
                })),
                "Runtime.evaluate" if expr.contains("localStorage") => Responder::Reply(json!({
                    "result": { "type": "string", "value": "[[\"theme\",\"dark\"]]" }
                })),
                _ => Responder::Reply(json!({})),
            }
        })
        .await
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn export_reads_cookies_tabs_and_local_storage_from_the_source() {
        let server = source_server().await;
        let handle = crate::browser::testkit::fake_engine_handle(
            Engine::Obscura,
            &server,
            &[("T-A", "https://example.com/a", true)],
        )
        .await;

        let state = export_state(&handle).await.expect("export");

        assert_eq!(state.cookies.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(state.cookies[0].name, "sid");
        assert_eq!(state.cookies[0].value, "abc123");
        assert_eq!(state.tabs.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(state.tabs[0].url, "https://example.com/a");
        assert_eq!(state.tabs[0].scroll_y, 480);
        assert!(state.tabs[0].active);
        assert_eq!(
            state.local_storage,
            vec![(
                "https://example.com".to_string(),
                vec![("theme".to_string(), "dark".to_string())]
            )]
        );
        // The URL did NOT come from target enumeration — the fake answered [].
        assert!(
            !methods(&server).iter().any(|m| m == "Target.getTargets"),
            "tab URLs must come from TabEntry.url, not from an enumeration \
             obscura answers falsely (R13); saw {:?}",
            methods(&server)
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn import_sets_the_same_cookies_and_reopens_every_tab_on_the_target() {
        let src = source_server().await;
        let source = crate::browser::testkit::fake_engine_handle(
            Engine::Obscura,
            &src,
            &[("T-A", "https://example.com/a", true)],
        )
        .await;
        let state = export_state(&source).await.expect("export");

        let dst = FakeCdpServer::start(|req| {
            let method = req.get("method").and_then(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
            match method {
                "Target.createTarget" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "targetId": "T-B" })),
                "Target.attachToTarget" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "sessionId": "S-B" })),
                "Target.getTargets" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "targetInfos": [] })),
                "Page.navigate" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "frameId": "F-B" })),
                "Runtime.evaluate" => {
                    Responder::Reply(json!({ "result": { "type": "string", "value": "ok" } }))
                }
                _ => Responder::Reply(json!({})),
            }
        })
        .await;
        // The target starts with its launch tab, as a real one does
        // (`EngineHandle::new` takes a `first_tab`).
        let target = crate::browser::testkit::fake_engine_handle(
            Engine::Chromium,
            &dst,
            &[("T-BOOT", "about:blank", true)],
        )
        .await;

        let report = import_state(&target, &state).await.expect("import");

        assert_eq!(report.cookies_moved, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.tabs_reopened, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.local_storage_origins, 1);

        // The cookies that arrive are the ones that left — read off the params
        // the fake received, not off a value this test also wrote.
        let set = dst
            .received()
            .into_iter()
            .find(|m| m.get("method").and_then(|x| x.as_str()) == Some("Network.setCookies"))
            .expect("Network.setCookies must be sent");
        let cookies = set["params"]["cookies"].as_array().expect("cookies array");
        assert_eq!(cookies.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(cookies[0]["name"], "sid");
        assert_eq!(cookies[0]["value"], "abc123");
        assert_eq!(cookies[0]["domain"], "example.com");
        // The exported cookie carries its own domain, so nothing on the wire
        // may attribute it to a page URL: a `url` here would let the engine
        // re-derive a narrower origin than the one the cookie already names.
        // Read Part 1 Task 4's wrapper doc for exactly how `page_url` is
        // rendered before asserting the key name — the RULE is that a cookie
        // with a domain gets no url, whatever the field ends up being called.
        assert!(
            cookies[0].get("url").is_none(),
            "a domain-carrying cookie must not be given a url, got {:?}",
            cookies[0]
        );

        let created = dst
            .received()
            .into_iter()
            .find(|m| m.get("method").and_then(|x| x.as_str()) == Some("Target.createTarget"))
            .expect("Target.createTarget must be sent");
        assert_eq!(created["params"]["url"], "https://example.com/a");

        // Cookies before tabs: a tab that loads before its cookie is an
        // unauthenticated page, and the model would read the login screen as
        // the site.
        let seen = methods(&dst);
        let cookies_at = seen.iter().position(|m| m == "Network.setCookies").unwrap();
        let target_at = seen.iter().position(|m| m == "Target.createTarget").unwrap();
        assert!(
            cookies_at < target_at,
            "cookies must be installed before any tab is opened, saw {seen:?}"
        );

        let tabs = target.tabs.lock().await;
        assert!(tabs.entries.contains_key("T-B"));
        assert_eq!(tabs.entries["T-B"].url, "https://example.com/a");
        assert_eq!(tabs.active.as_deref(), Some("T-B"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_cookie_export_failure_is_an_error_and_touches_no_target() {
        let src = FakeCdpServer::start(|req| {
            let method = req.get("method").and_then(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
            if method == "Network.getAllCookies" {
                return Responder::Error {
                    code: -32000,
                    message: "cookie store unavailable".into(),
                };
            }
            Responder::Reply(json!({}))
        })
        .await;
        let source = crate::browser::testkit::fake_engine_handle(
            Engine::Obscura,
            &src,
            &[("T-A", "https://example.com/a", true)],
        )
        .await;

        let err = export_state(&source).await.expect_err("must fail closed");
        // `map_cdp_err` turns a protocol error into `BrowserError::Cdp`, which
        // carries the method — so the error says WHICH call failed, and a
        // timeout on the same call would have become `EngineBusy` instead.
        assert!(
            matches!(&err, BrowserError::Cdp { method, .. } if method == "Network.getAllCookies"),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn an_engine_barrier_during_export_is_engine_busy_not_engine_failure() {
        // obscura's global command barrier arrives as a per-command timeout.
        // Reporting it as `EngineFailure` would tell the model the engine is
        // broken when it is merely wedged, and lose the verb it should use.
        let src = FakeCdpServer::start(|req| {
            let method = req.get("method").and_then(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
            if method == "Network.getAllCookies" {
                return Responder::Delay(
                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
                    Box::new(Responder::Reply(json!({ "cookies": [] }))),
                );
            }
            Responder::Reply(json!({}))
        })
        .await;
        let source = crate::browser::testkit::fake_engine_handle(
            Engine::Obscura,
            &src,
            &[("T-A", "https://example.com/a", true)],
        )
        .await;

        let err = export_state(&source).await.expect_err("the barrier must surface");
        assert!(
            matches!(&err, BrowserError::EngineBusy { engine, method, .. }
                     if *engine == Engine::Obscura && method == "Network.getAllCookies"),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_local_storage_failure_is_a_warning_not_an_abort() {
        let src = FakeCdpServer::start(|req| {
            let method = req.get("method").and_then(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
            let expr = req
                .get("params")
                .and_then(|p| p.get("expression"))
                .and_then(|e| e.as_str())
                .unwrap_or("");
            match method {
                "Network.getAllCookies" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "cookies": [] })),
                "Runtime.evaluate" if expr.contains("scrollX") => Responder::Reply(json!({
                    "result": { "type": "object", "value": [0, 0] }
                })),
                "Runtime.evaluate" => Responder::Error {
                    code: -32000,
                    message: "SecurityError: localStorage is not available".into(),
                },
                _ => Responder::Reply(json!({})),
            }
        })
        .await;
        let source = crate::browser::testkit::fake_engine_handle(
            Engine::Obscura,
            &src,
            &[("T-A", "https://example.com/a", true)],
        )
        .await;

        let state = export_state(&source).await.expect("localStorage is best effort");
        assert!(state.local_storage.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(state.tabs.len(), 1, "the tab still migrates");
        assert!(
            state.warnings.iter().any(|w| w.contains("localStorage")),
            "the loss must be stated, got {:?}",
            state.warnings
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// The one ordering claim that matters: a failed migration must never cost
    /// the user the browser they already had.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_failed_import_leaves_the_source_engine_running_and_selected() {
        use crate::browser::engine::Engine;
        use crate::browser::engine::EngineLaunch;
        use crate::browser::testkit::{switch_fixture, SwitchFixture};

        let SwitchFixture {
            manager,
            source_killed,
            ..
        } = switch_fixture(Engine::Obscura, Engine::Chromium, /* target_rejects_cookies */ true)
            .await;

        let err = manager
            .switch_engine("default", Engine::Chromium, true)
            .await
            .expect_err("a target that refuses the cookies must fail the switch");
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("chromium"),
            "the error must name the engine that failed, got: {err}"
        );
        assert!(
            !source_killed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),
            "the source engine must still be alive after a failed import"
        );
        // And the profile still routes to the engine it had. `Refuse` proves
        // the handle was found rather than launched.
        let handle = manager
            .engine_handle_for("default", Engine::Obscura, EngineLaunch::Refuse)
            .await
            .expect("the source handle is still the profile's handle");
        assert_eq!(handle.engine, Engine::Obscura);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn switching_to_the_engine_already_running_is_refused_by_name() {
        use crate::browser::engine::Engine;
        use crate::browser::testkit::{switch_fixture, SwitchFixture};

        let SwitchFixture { manager, .. } =
            switch_fixture(Engine::Obscura, Engine::Chromium, false).await;
        let err = manager
            .switch_engine("default", Engine::Obscura, true)
            .await
            .expect_err("a no-op switch must be refused, not reported as success");
        assert!(matches!(err, BrowserError::AlreadyOnEngine { .. }), "got {err:?}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_successful_switch_kills_the_source_and_replaces_the_handle() {
        use crate::browser::engine::Engine;
        use crate::browser::engine::EngineLaunch;
        use crate::browser::testkit::{switch_fixture, SwitchFixture};

        let SwitchFixture {
            manager,
            source_killed,
            ..
        } = switch_fixture(Engine::Obscura, Engine::Chromium, false).await;

        let report = manager
            .switch_engine("default", Engine::Chromium, true)
            .await
            .expect("switch");
        assert_eq!(report.from, Engine::Obscura);
        assert_eq!(report.to, Engine::Chromium);
        assert_eq!(report.cookies_moved, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.tabs_reopened, 1);
        assert!(
            source_killed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),
            "the source process must be killed once the target holds the state"
        );
        let handle = manager
            .engine_handle_for("default", Engine::Chromium, EngineLaunch::Refuse)
            .await
            .expect("the target is now the profile's handle");
        assert_eq!(handle.engine, Engine::Chromium);
    }
```

Extract the launch body of `handle` (`part-3-handle-pagestate.md:1450-1512`) into a private
`async fn launch_one(&self, engine, req) -> Result<Arc<EngineHandle>, BrowserError>` and have BOTH
`handle` and `launch_detached` call it, so "how an engine comes into existence" keeps exactly one

```rust
    /// Launch an engine that goes into **no map**.
    ///
    /// [`Self::handle`] is keyed by `req.profile` and refuses with
    /// `EngineMismatch` when a different engine is already parked there — which
    /// is correct for every caller except the one that is deliberately standing
    /// up the *other* engine for that same profile. `switch_engine` needs the
    /// target running and the source still parked at the same moment: the
    /// source is what it falls back to if the migration fails, so removing it
    /// first would leave the profile with no engine across a launch that can
    /// fail, and asking `handle` for it would hit the mismatch arm.
    ///
    /// The returned handle belongs to the caller. Nothing else can reach it, so
    /// a failure downstream costs exactly this handle and the caller must
    /// `shutdown()` it — there is no map entry to clean up and no other owner.
    pub async fn launch_detached(
        &self,
        engine: Engine,
        req: &LaunchRequest,
    ) -> Result<Arc<EngineHandle>, BrowserError> {
        self.launch_one(engine, req).await
    }

    /// Swap the handle parked under `profile`, returning the displaced one.
    ///
    /// One locked operation, not `remove` + `insert`: between those two a
    /// concurrent `browser_open` would find no handle, launch a third engine,
    /// and then be overwritten. The caller owns whatever comes back and is the
    /// one that shuts it down — this method never kills anything, because the
    /// order "swap, then stop the old one" is the caller's contract to state
    /// and the registry has no way to know whether the displaced handle is
    /// finished being read.
    pub async fn replace(
        &self,
        profile: &str,
        new: Arc<EngineHandle>,
    ) -> Option<Arc<EngineHandle>> {
        let mut map = self.handles.lock().await;
        map.insert(profile.to_string(), new)
    }
```
