**3d. `src/browser/cdp_backend/migration.rs`** (above the test module from Step 1):

```rust
//! Carrying a profile's identity from one engine's process to the other's.
//!
//! `--user-data-dir` (Chromium) and `--storage-dir` (obscura) persist different
//! formats and neither reads the other's, so a switch cannot hand over a
//! directory — it has to re-state the state over CDP. The honest definition of
//! "seamless" is spec §5.5's: **the login survives, the page progress does
//! not.** That sentence is written out for the model as a literal in
//! `BrowserSessionTool::DESCRIPTION`; it is prose about a design decision, not a
//! rendering of anything here, so there is deliberately no table for it to
//! drift from. The per-engine facts that ARE table-shaped reach the model the
//! other way — as the result of `browser_session{action:"capabilities"}`.
//!
//! Failure policy, and the reason for it: cookies and tabs are **errors**
//! (a switch that silently drops the session is exactly the "报成功的 no-op"
//! shape, 判据 §11); localStorage and scroll are **warnings** (per-origin, best
//! effort — a `SecurityError` on a sandboxed frame is not a reason to strand
//! the user on a browser they asked to leave). Warnings travel in the return
//! value, never a log line.
//!
//! Every CDP error goes through [`super::map_cdp_err`]. That is not tidiness:
//! it is the only thing that turns obscura's global command barrier into
//! `EngineBusy{engine, method, waited_secs}` instead of a generic failure, and
//! `EngineBusy` is the error whose text names the verb that gets out of it.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use aleph_cdp::methods::{network, page, runtime, target};
use aleph_cdp::SessionId;

use super::navigate::{apply_document_boundary, wait_for_load};
use super::{as_call_expression, map_cdp_err};
use crate::browser::engine::{Engine, EngineHandle, TabEntry};
use crate::browser::error::BrowserError;

/// One tab, as it must be re-created on the other engine.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct TabMigration {
    pub url: String,
    pub scroll_x: i32,
    pub scroll_y: i32,
    pub active: bool,
}

/// Everything read off the source engine, before anything is written anywhere.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct MigrationState {
    pub cookies: Vec<network::Cookie>,
    pub tabs: Vec<TabMigration>,
    /// `(origin, [(key, value)])`, one entry per distinct origin among the open
    /// tabs. Two tabs on one origin share one entry — a second read of the same
    /// store would answer the same thing.
    pub local_storage: Vec<(String, Vec<(String, String)>)>,
    /// What did not come across. Never empty for a lossy export.
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
}

/// What actually landed on the target.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct ImportReport {
    pub cookies_moved: usize,
    pub tabs_reopened: usize,
    pub local_storage_origins: usize,
    /// The target-side tab id carrying the source's active tab, if any.
    pub active_tab: Option<String>,
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
}

/// `scheme://host[:port]` for a page URL, or `None` for anything that is not a
/// tuple origin (`about:blank`, `data:`). A non-tuple origin has no
/// localStorage to move, so `None` is a fact and not a failure.
fn origin_of(url: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let parsed = url::Url::parse(url).ok()?;
    let origin = parsed.origin();
    origin.is_tuple().then(|| origin.ascii_serialization())
}

const READ_SCROLL: &str = "[window.scrollX, window.scrollY]";
const READ_LOCAL_STORAGE: &str = "JSON.stringify(Object.entries(localStorage))";

/// Read every migratable fact off `handle`. Nothing is written anywhere and the
/// source engine is untouched, so a failure here costs the caller nothing.
pub(crate) async fn export_state(
    handle: &EngineHandle,
) -> Result<MigrationState, BrowserError> {
    let engine = handle.engine;
    let conn = &handle.conn;

    // (tab_id, session, url, active), taken under the lock and then released,
    // so no CDP round trip happens while holding it.
    //
    // The URL comes from `TabEntry.url` — the tab table, which Task 12 keeps
    // true from main-frame `Page.frameNavigated`. It deliberately does NOT come
    // from `Target.getTargets`: obscura answers that with an empty list even on
    // its own connection (R13), so an enumeration-based export would carry no
    // tabs at all in the default direction while every unit test stayed green.
    let open: Vec<(String, SessionId, String, bool)> = {
        let tabs = handle.tabs.lock().await;
        tabs.entries
            .iter()
            .map(|(id, e)| {
                (
                    id.clone(),
                    e.session.clone(),
                    e.url.clone(),
                    tabs.active.as_deref() == Some(id),
                )
            })
            .collect()
    };

    let mut state = MigrationState::default();
    let Some((_, first_session, _, _)) = open.first().cloned() else {
        // A handle with no tab has no page session, and every cookie method is
        // session-scoped. Say what did not happen instead of returning an empty
        // success that reads like "there was nothing to move".
        state.warnings.push(format!(
            "{engine} had no open tab: no cookies, tabs or localStorage were exported"
        ));
        return Ok(state);
    };

    // Cookies first: the whole browser context in one call, and the one thing
    // whose loss makes the switch pointless.
    state.cookies = network::get_all_cookies(conn, Some(&first_session))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| map_cdp_err(engine, "Network.getAllCookies", e))?;

    let mut seen_origins: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (tab_id, session, url, active) in &open {
        // Scroll via the page, not `Page.getLayoutMetrics`: the two engines
        // disagree about what that method reports for a scrolled document, and
        // `window.scrollX/Y` is the value the restore side writes back with
        // `window.scrollTo`. One derivation for read and write.
        let (scroll_x, scroll_y) =
            match runtime::evaluate(conn, Some(session), READ_SCROLL, false).await {
                Ok(res) if res.exception.is_none() => decode_scroll(&res.value).unwrap_or((0, 0)),
                Ok(res) => {
                    state.warnings.push(format!(
                        "scroll position of {url} was not readable ({}); it will open at the top",
                        res.exception.unwrap_or_default()
                    ));
                    (0, 0)
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    state.warnings.push(format!(
                        "scroll position of {url} was not readable ({}); it will open at the top",
                        map_cdp_err(engine, "Runtime.evaluate", e)
                    ));
                    (0, 0)
                }
            };
        state.tabs.push(TabMigration {
            url: url.clone(),
            scroll_x,
            scroll_y,
            active: *active,
        });
        let _ = tab_id;

        let Some(origin) = origin_of(url) else { continue };
        if seen_origins.contains(&origin) {
            continue;
        }
        seen_origins.push(origin.clone());
        match runtime::evaluate(conn, Some(session), READ_LOCAL_STORAGE, false).await {
            Ok(res) if res.exception.is_none() => match decode_local_storage(&res.value) {
                Some(pairs) if !pairs.is_empty() => state.local_storage.push((origin, pairs)),
                Some(_) => {}
                None => state.warnings.push(format!(
                    "localStorage for {origin} was not in the expected shape and was not migrated"
                )),
            },
            Ok(res) => state.warnings.push(format!(
                "localStorage for {origin} was not migrated: {}",
                res.exception.unwrap_or_default()
            )),
            Err(e) => state.warnings.push(format!(
                "localStorage for {origin} was not migrated: {}",
                map_cdp_err(engine, "Runtime.evaluate", e)
            )),
        }
    }

    Ok(state)
}

/// `[x, y]` → ints. `None` means "not that shape", which the caller reports.
fn decode_scroll(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<(i32, i32)> {
    let arr = value.as_array()?;
    let x = arr.first()?.as_f64()?.round() as i32;
    let y = arr.get(1)?.as_f64()?.round() as i32;
    Some((x, y))
}

/// `[["k","v"],…]` (JSON, possibly nested in a string) → pairs.
fn decode_local_storage(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<Vec<(String, String)>> {
    let parsed = match value {
        serde_json::Value::String(s) => serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(s).ok()?,
        other => other.clone(),
    };
    let rows = parsed.as_array()?;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(rows.len());
    for row in rows {
        let pair = row.as_array()?;
        out.push((
            pair.first()?.as_str()?.to_string(),
            pair.get(1)?.as_str()?.to_string(),
        ));
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// JS that installs a whole localStorage payload.
///
/// The payload is built with `serde_json` so a key or value containing a quote
/// cannot end the expression — these are page-authored bytes, which is the one
/// place a hand-built string is a bug. The wrapper is
/// [`super::as_call_expression`], not a second locally-written IIFE: Task 12
/// owns "how a script becomes a call" and names this call site as its reuser
/// (`part-4-cdp-backend.md:76`).
fn import_local_storage_js(pairs: &[(String, String)]) -> String {
    let payload = serde_json::Value::Array(
        pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| serde_json::json!([k, v])).collect(),
    );
    as_call_expression(&format!(
        "() => {{ for (const [k, v] of {payload}) localStorage.setItem(k, v); return 'ok'; }}"
    ))
}

/// Write `state` into `handle`'s engine and re-open its tabs.
///
/// Order is load-bearing: cookies are installed **before** the first tab is
/// created, because a tab that loads before its cookie is an unauthenticated
/// page and the model would read the login screen as the site.
///
/// **This deliberately does not re-run the SSRF pre-check** that
/// `cdp_backend::navigate::navigate` runs. These URLs are not model input: they
/// came off tabs the guard already admitted, on this same profile, moments ago,
/// and `apply_document_boundary` + the caller's post-switch snapshot still see
/// wherever they actually land. Re-vetting them would also mean a policy edited
/// between the two engines could strand a switch half-done — the worst state
/// this module can be in. If that trade is ever reversed, the change is to
/// route this through `CdpBackend` rather than to add a second guard call here.
pub(crate) async fn import_state(
    handle: &EngineHandle,
    state: &MigrationState,
) -> Result<ImportReport, BrowserError> {
    let engine = handle.engine;
    let conn = &handle.conn;
    let budget = conn.command_timeout();
    let mut report = ImportReport {
        warnings: state.warnings.clone(),
        ..ImportReport::default()
    };

    if !state.cookies.is_empty() {
        let boot = boot_session(handle).await?;
        // `set_cookies`' fourth argument attributes cookies that carry no
        // domain of their own. Everything `Network.getAllCookies` returns is a
        // cookie already IN a store, so it has one, and `None` is the right
        // answer for the whole batch — passing a URL there would attach an
        // origin to cookies that already name their own and could silently
        // narrow them. The `else` arm exists for a `MigrationState` that did
        // not come from `export_state`; it attributes them to the first tab,
        // which is the only origin this function knows.
        let page_url = if state.cookies.iter().all(|c| !c.domain.is_empty()) {
            None
        } else {
            state.tabs.first().map(|t| t.url.as_str())
        };
        network::set_cookies(conn, Some(&boot), &state.cookies, page_url)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| map_cdp_err(engine, "Network.setCookies", e))?;
        report.cookies_moved = state.cookies.len();
    }

    let by_origin: HashMap<&str, &Vec<(String, String)>> = state
        .local_storage
        .iter()
        .map(|(o, p)| (o.as_str(), p))
        .collect();
    let mut imported_origins: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    for tab in &state.tabs {
        let target_id = target::create_target(conn, &tab.url)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| map_cdp_err(engine, "Target.createTarget", e))?;
        let tab_id = target_id.0.clone();
        // `ensure_tab` is the one place a tab is attached and its domains
        // enabled (Task 9); calling it here means the target's tab table is
        // populated by the same code path every other verb uses.
        let session = handle.ensure_tab(&tab_id).await?;

        settle(handle, conn, &session, &tab_id, &tab.url, budget, engine).await?;

        // localStorage is origin-scoped and only reachable from a document on
        // that origin, so it is written after the first load and the page is
        // navigated once more (a fresh navigation, not a reload — reloading a
        // POSTed page prompts). A site that reads localStorage at startup
        // therefore sees it; the cost is one extra load per origin.
        if let Some(origin) = origin_of(&tab.url) {
            if let Some(pairs) = by_origin.get(origin.as_str()) {
                if !imported_origins.contains(&origin) {
                    match runtime::evaluate(
                        conn,
                        Some(&session),
                        &import_local_storage_js(pairs),
                        false,
                    )
                    .await
                    {
                        Ok(res) if res.exception.is_none() => {
                            imported_origins.push(origin.clone());
                            if let Err(e) =
                                settle(handle, conn, &session, &tab_id, &tab.url, budget, engine)
                                    .await
                            {
                                report.warnings.push(format!(
                                    "localStorage for {origin} was written but the reload failed \
                                     ({e}); the page may not have read it"
                                ));
                            }
                        }
                        Ok(res) => report.warnings.push(format!(
                            "localStorage for {origin} could not be restored: {}",
                            res.exception.unwrap_or_default()
                        )),
                        Err(e) => report.warnings.push(format!(
                            "localStorage for {origin} could not be restored: {}",
                            map_cdp_err(engine, "Runtime.evaluate", e)
                        )),
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if tab.scroll_x != 0 || tab.scroll_y != 0 {
            let js = as_call_expression(&format!(
                "() => {{ window.scrollTo({}, {}); return 'ok'; }}",
                tab.scroll_x, tab.scroll_y
            ));
            if let Err(e) = runtime::evaluate(conn, Some(&session), &js, false).await {
                report.warnings.push(format!(
                    "scroll position of {} was not restored: {}",
                    tab.url,
                    map_cdp_err(engine, "Runtime.evaluate", e)
                ));
            }
        }

        if tab.active {
            let mut tabs = handle.tabs.lock().await;
            tabs.active = Some(tab_id.clone());
            report.active_tab = Some(tab_id.clone());
        }
        report.tabs_reopened += 1;
    }

    Ok(report)
}

/// Navigate one tab and wait for it, reusing Task 12's barrier and boundary.
///
/// `events` is opened BEFORE the command, because a cached page's load event
/// otherwise arrives while nobody is listening and the barrier waits out the
/// whole budget (Task 12 states this rule on `wait_for_load` itself).
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
async fn settle(
    handle: &EngineHandle,
    conn: &aleph_cdp::CdpConnection,
    session: &SessionId,
    tab_id: &str,
    url: &str,
    budget: std::time::Duration,
    engine: Engine,
) -> Result<(), BrowserError> {
    let mut events = conn.events();
    let result = page::navigate(conn, Some(session), url)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| map_cdp_err(engine, "Page.navigate", e))?;
    if let Some(text) = result.error_text {
        return Err(BrowserError::EngineFailure {
            engine,
            reason: format!("the new engine refused to load {url}: {text}"),
        });
    }
    let outcome = wait_for_load(&mut events, session, &result.frame_id, budget).await;
    let loader = result.loader_id.or(outcome.loader_id);
    let landed = outcome.url.unwrap_or_else(|| url.to_string());
    apply_document_boundary(handle, tab_id, loader.as_deref(), Some(&landed)).await;
    // A tab that did not finish loading is NOT an error here: the switch has
    // already moved the cookies, and the model's next `browser_snapshot` sees
    // whatever is actually there. Reporting a failure would throw away a
    // migration that mostly worked.
    Ok(())
}

/// A page session on `handle` for the browser-context-wide cookie write.
///
/// Task 9's `EngineHandle::new` takes a `first_tab`, so a freshly launched
/// handle always has one and this always finds it. There is deliberately **no**
/// `create_target("about:blank")` fallback: an arm that can only run when an
/// invariant is already broken is a safety net nobody has ever tested, and it
/// would hide the breakage rather than report it (判据 §17).
async fn boot_session(handle: &EngineHandle) -> Result<SessionId, BrowserError> {
    let tabs = handle.tabs.lock().await;
    tabs.active
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|id| tabs.entries.get(id))
        .or_else(|| tabs.entries.values().next())
        .map(|e| e.session.clone())
        .ok_or_else(|| BrowserError::EngineFailure {
            engine: handle.engine,
            reason: "the newly launched engine reported no page to install cookies into; \
                     re-run browser_open"
                .to_string(),
        })
}
```

```rust
/// What a completed [`ProfileManager::switch_engine`] actually moved.
///
/// Counts, not booleans: "the switch succeeded" and "the switch carried your
/// login" are different facts, and only the numbers tell them apart.
pub struct SwitchReport {
    pub from: Engine,
    pub to: Engine,
    pub cookies_moved: usize,
    pub tabs_reopened: usize,
    pub local_storage_origins: usize,
    /// Everything the migration could not carry. Rendered to the model
    /// verbatim; empty means nothing was lost, not "nothing was checked".
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
    pub snapshot: SnapshotOutput,
}
```

and two methods in `impl ProfileManager`:

```rust
    /// What `browser_open` should run on, given an optional one-shot override.
    ///
    /// Deliberately thin: "is a different engine already running for this
    /// profile" is a question `EngineRegistry::handle` already answers under its
    /// own lock, by returning `EngineMismatch`
    /// (`engine/registry.rs`, the `existing.engine != engine` arm). Re-deriving
    /// it here from a second read of the map would be the same fact with two
    /// answers, and the registry's is the one that cannot race.
    pub(crate) async fn prepare_engine(
        &self,
        profile: &str,
        requested: Option<Engine>,
    ) -> Result<Engine, BrowserError> {
        let cfg = self
            .get_config(profile)
            .ok_or_else(|| BrowserError::ProfileNotFound(profile.into()))?;
        if requested.is_some() && cfg.driver != BrowserDriver::Cdp {
            return Err(BrowserError::ActionFailed(format!(
                "profile '{profile}' uses driver '{:?}', which has no engine to choose; \
                 set driver = \"cdp\" on it with `browser_profile` first",
                cfg.driver
            )));
        }
        let (default_engine, _) = self.launch_request_for(profile)?;
        let target = requested.unwrap_or(default_engine);
        // `EngineLaunch` is payload-free: `launch_request_for` already derived
        // everything a launch needs, so a second `SessionLaunch` here would be
        // that derivation's second author (判据 §1).
        self.engine_handle_for(profile, target, EngineLaunch::Allow)
            .await?;
        Ok(target)
    }

    /// Move `profile` onto `to`, carrying the state spec §5.5 names: every
    /// cookie, each open tab's URL and scroll, and per-origin localStorage.
    /// Everything else — the JS heap, in-flight form input, the history stack,
    /// sessionStorage — is gone, and `BrowserSessionTool::DESCRIPTION` is where
    /// that is stated for the model.
    ///
    /// **Human control lease (plan 2's hook point, deliberately absent today).**
    /// When a person holds the control lease on this profile's browser, this
    /// method must refuse rather than pull the browser out from under them —
    /// the check belongs immediately after the `AlreadyOnEngine` guard below,
    /// before anything is exported. There is no lease to check in this round:
    /// the live view that mints one is plan 2, and a `false`-returning stub
    /// here would be a gate that has never once been closed (判据 §2). This
    /// comment is the hook point, placed where the edit will be made.
    ///
    /// The order is the contract, chosen so **every failure before the last
    /// step leaves the user on the browser they already had**:
    ///
    /// 1. find the source (still parked, still serving)
    /// 2. read it (nothing written anywhere)
    /// 3. `launch_detached` the target — deliberately NOT `engine_handle_for`:
    ///    the source is still parked under this profile, which is exactly the
    ///    case `EngineRegistry::handle` refuses with `EngineMismatch`
    /// 4. write the target (a failure here kills the *target*; the source is
    ///    untouched and still the profile's handle)
    /// 5. `replace` — one locked swap, so no window exists in which the profile
    ///    has no engine
    /// 6. stop the displaced source
    ///
    /// Step 4-before-6 is the one an implementation naturally gets wrong: it
    /// reads more cleanly to shut the old engine first, and it is wrong for the
    /// same reason `reap_idle` stopping at `close` was wrong — the observable
    /// state afterwards is "reported success, browser gone".
    pub async fn switch_engine(
        &self,
        profile: &str,
        to: Engine,
        migrate: bool,
    ) -> Result<SwitchReport, BrowserError> {
        self.record_activity(profile);
        let source = self
            .engines()
            .get(profile)
            .await
            .ok_or_else(|| BrowserError::NoSession(profile.into()))?;
        let from = source.engine;
        if from == to {
            return Err(BrowserError::AlreadyOnEngine {
                profile: profile.into(),
                engine: to,
            });
        }

        let state = if migrate {
            migration::export_state(&source).await?
        } else {
            MigrationState {
                warnings: vec![
                    "migrate=false: no cookies, tabs or localStorage were carried across".into(),
                ],
                ..MigrationState::default()
            }
        };

        let (_, mut req) = self.launch_request_for(profile)?;
        req.data_dir = engine_data_dir(profile, to)?;
        let target = self.engines().launch_detached(to, &req).await?;

        let report = match migration::import_state(&target, &state).await {
            Ok(r) => r,
            Err(e) => {
                target.shutdown().await;
                return Err(e);
            }
        };

        let displaced = self.engines().replace(profile, Arc::clone(&target)).await;
        if let Some(old) = displaced {
            old.shutdown().await;
        }

        // The model's old refs all died with the old process, so the new tree
        // travels back in the return value rather than being something it must
        // remember to ask for.
        let backend = self.get_backend(profile)?;
        let tab_id = match report.active_tab.clone() {
            Some(id) => id,
            // No active tab is a fact, not an empty string. Ask the backend the
            // same question every other verb asks (`browser_tools/mod.rs:204`)
            // rather than handing `snapshot` a `""` it will fail on obscurely.
            None => crate::builtin_tools::browser_tools::active_tab_of(backend.as_ref()).await?,
        };
        let snapshot = backend.snapshot(&tab_id).await?;

        Ok(SwitchReport {
            from,
            to,
            cookies_moved: report.cookies_moved,
```

**3g. `src/browser/testkit.rs`** (Task 9's file) — both fixtures, written out.

```rust
/// An [`EngineHandle`] wired to a running [`FakeCdpServer`], with `tabs`
/// pre-populated from `(target_id, url, active)` triples.
///
/// The process side is a [`FakeEngineProcess`] so nothing is spawned; the CDP
/// side is real transport against a fake peer, which is what makes the
/// migration tests assert bytes on the wire rather than that a function ran.
///
/// The first triple becomes `EngineHandle::new`'s `first_tab`, matching a real
/// launch (Task 9 creates one tab before the ready gate).
pub(crate) async fn fake_engine_handle(
    engine: Engine,
    server: &aleph_cdp::testkit::FakeCdpServer,
    tabs: &[(&str, &str, bool)],
) -> Arc<EngineHandle> {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("sidecar dir");
    let process: Arc<dyn EngineProcess> =
        Arc::new(FakeEngineProcess::new(engine, server, dir.path()));
    let launched = process
        .launch(LaunchRequest {
            profile: "default".into(),
            session_key: "default".into(),
            data_dir: dir.path().to_path_buf(),
            headless: true,
            proxy: None,
            allow_private_network: false,
            stealth: false,
            extra_args: vec![],
        })
        .await
        .expect("fake launch");
    let conn = aleph_cdp::CdpConnection::connect(
        &launched.endpoint.ws_url,
        aleph_cdp::ConnectOptions {
            // Short: one migration test asserts the timeout arm, and the 30 s
            // production default would make it take 30 s.
            command_timeout: std::time::Duration::from_millis(400),
        },
    )
    .await
    .expect("connect to fake");

    let (first_id, first_url, _) = tabs.first().copied().unwrap_or(("T-0", "about:blank", true));
    let first_session = aleph_cdp::SessionId(format!("S-{first_id}"));
    let handle = Arc::new(EngineHandle::new(
        engine,
        "default".into(),
        launched,
        conn,
        process,
        (first_id.to_string(), first_session.clone()),
    ));
    {
        let mut table = handle.tabs.lock().await;
        for (id, url, active) in tabs {
            let mut entry = TabEntry::new(aleph_cdp::SessionId(format!("S-{id}")));
            entry.url = (*url).to_string();
            table.entries.insert((*id).to_string(), entry);
            if *active {
                table.active = Some((*id).to_string());
            }
        }
    }
    // The tempdir must outlive the handle; leak it, because a test fixture that
    // deletes the sidecar under a live handle produces a failure that looks
    // like the code under test.
    std::mem::forget(dir);
    handle
}

/// A [`ProfileManager`] whose `default` profile is already running `from`, with
/// a launcher for `to` registered so the switch can stand one up.
pub(crate) struct SwitchFixture {
    pub manager: Arc<ProfileManager>,
    /// Flipped inside the source [`FakeEngineProcess`]'s
    /// `kill(&self, launched: &Launched, grace: Duration)` arm — the same
    /// signature the real launchers implement, so the fake cannot pass a test
    /// the production trait would not compile against.
    ///
    /// Set it in `kill`, **never** in `EngineHandle::shutdown`: shutdown is the
    /// caller under test, and a flag flipped there would go green for a
    /// shutdown that reached no process (判据 §4 — assert the effect arrived,
    /// not that the call was made).
    pub source_killed: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>,
    pub source: aleph_cdp::testkit::FakeCdpServer,
    pub target: aleph_cdp::testkit::FakeCdpServer,
}

/// `target_rejects_cookies` makes the target's fake answer `Network.setCookies`
/// with an error — the failure the ordering claim is about.
pub(crate) async fn switch_fixture(
    from: Engine,
    to: Engine,
    target_rejects_cookies: bool,
) -> SwitchFixture {
    use serde_json::json;
    let source = aleph_cdp::testkit::FakeCdpServer::start(|req| {
        let method = req.get("method").and_then(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
        let expr = req
            .get("params")
            .and_then(|p| p.get("expression"))
            .and_then(|e| e.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("");
        match method {
            "Target.getTargets" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "targetInfos": [] })),
            "Network.getAllCookies" => Responder::Reply(json!({
                "cookies": [{
                    "name": "sid", "value": "abc123", "domain": "example.com",
                    "path": "/", "expires": -1.0, "httpOnly": true,
                    "secure": false, "sameSite": "Lax"
                }]
            })),
            "Runtime.evaluate" if expr.contains("scrollX") => {
                Responder::Reply(json!({ "result": { "type": "object", "value": [0, 0] } }))
            }
            _ => Responder::Reply(json!({ "result": { "type": "string", "value": "[]" } })),
        }
    })
    .await;
    let target = aleph_cdp::testkit::FakeCdpServer::start(move |req| {
        let method = req.get("method").and_then(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
        match method {
            "Network.setCookies" if target_rejects_cookies => Responder::Error {
                code: -32000,
                message: "cookie store is read-only".into(),
            },
            "Target.createTarget" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "targetId": "T-NEW" })),
            "Target.attachToTarget" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "sessionId": "S-NEW" })),
            "Page.navigate" => Responder::Reply(json!({ "frameId": "F-NEW" })),
            _ => Responder::Reply(json!({ "result": { "type": "string", "value": "ok" } })),
        }
    })
    .await;

    let source_killed = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
    let src_dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("dir");
    let dst_dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("dir");
    let src_proc = Arc::new(
        FakeEngineProcess::new(from, &source, src_dir.path())
            .with_kill_flag(Arc::clone(&source_killed)),
    );
    let dst_proc = Arc::new(FakeEngineProcess::new(to, &target, dst_dir.path()));

    let mut processes: std::collections::HashMap<Engine, Arc<dyn EngineProcess>> =
        std::collections::HashMap::new();
    processes.insert(from, src_proc.clone() as Arc<dyn EngineProcess>);
    processes.insert(to, dst_proc as Arc<dyn EngineProcess>);
    let registry = Arc::new(EngineRegistry::new(
        processes,
        std::time::Duration::from_millis(400),
        std::time::Duration::from_secs(2),
    ));

    // The source handle is PARKED under "default" — which is precisely the
    // state that makes `EngineRegistry::handle` refuse the target with
    // `EngineMismatch`, and therefore why `switch_engine` uses
    // `launch_detached` (deviation 4).
    let src_handle = fake_engine_handle(from, &source, &[("T-A", "https://example.com/a", true)]).await;
    registry.insert_for_test("default", Arc::clone(&src_handle)).await;

    let mut config = BrowserSystemConfig::default();
    config.default_engine = from;
    let manager = Arc::new(ProfileManager::with_engine_registry(config, registry));
    std::mem::forget(src_dir);
    std::mem::forget(dst_dir);
    SwitchFixture {
        manager,
        source_killed,
        source,
        target,
    }
}
```

The new method on `BrowserSessionTool`:

```rust
    /// The `switch_engine` arm.
    ///
    /// Gated the same way `save`/`load` are, and one level up for the same
    /// reason: this moves every cookie into a new process. Argument validation
    /// runs BEFORE the gate so a malformed call cannot consume a user approval
    /// — the rule `validate_session_name` already follows (`session.rs:88-95`).
    async fn switch_engine(&self, args: BrowserSessionArgs) -> Result<BrowserSessionOutput> {
        if args.name.is_some() {
            return Ok(BrowserSessionOutput::failed(
                "browser_session switch_engine takes no `name` — it moves the live \
                 session, it does not read a saved one",
            ));
        }
        let Some(engine) = args.engine else {
            return Ok(BrowserSessionOutput::failed(
                "browser_session switch_engine requires `engine`: \"obscura\" or \"chromium\"",
            ));
        };

        if let Some(message) = super::check_browser_approval(
            self.approval_policy.as_ref(),
            ActionType::BrowserSwitchEngine,
            "switch_engine",
            &format!("switch profile '{}' to {engine}", args.profile),
        )
        .await
        {
            return Ok(BrowserSessionOutput::failed(message));
        }

        let migrate = args.migrate.unwrap_or(true);
        match self
            .manager
            .switch_engine(&args.profile, engine, migrate)
            .await
        {
            Ok(report) => {
                let mut message = format!(
                    "Switched profile '{}' from {} to {}: {} cookie(s), {} tab(s), \
                     {} localStorage origin(s) carried across. Every earlier ref is dead; \
                     the new page tree is in snapshot_text.",
                    args.profile,
                    report.from,
                    report.to,
                    report.cookies_moved,
                    report.tabs_reopened,
                    report.local_storage_origins,
                );
                for w in &report.warnings {
                    message.push_str("\nNot carried: ");
                    message.push_str(w);
                }
                Ok(BrowserSessionOutput {
                    success: true,
                    path: None,
                    message: Some(message),
                    capabilities: None,
                    switched_to: Some(report.to.as_str().to_string()),
                    cookies_moved: Some(report.cookies_moved),
                    tabs_reopened: Some(report.tabs_reopened),
                    // Page text is page-derived bytes: through the same egress
                    // chokepoint every other page read uses, never raw.
                    snapshot_text: Some(super::redact_and_wrap(
                        &self.manager,
                        &report.snapshot.snapshot_text,
                    )),
                })
            }
            Err(e) => Ok(BrowserSessionOutput::failed(format!(
                "Switch to {engine} failed: {}",
                super::backend_error_text(&self.manager, &e)
            ))),
        }
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Pay the catalog-description ratchet — and only that one**

Task 19 adds ~600 bytes to `BrowserSessionTool::DESCRIPTION`, one `SessionAction` variant, two
`BrowserSessionArgs` fields and one `BrowserOpenArgs` field. **Exactly one measured ratchet prices
any of that**: `CATALOG_DESCRIPTION_CEILING_BYTES = 114_393` (`definitions.rs:2652`), and its raise
protocol is written at `definitions.rs:1891-1899`.

⚠️ **`REGISTRY_SCHEMA_CEILING_BYTES` (`definitions.rs:3069`) must NOT be raised.** Its test,
`registry_schema_bytes_ratchet`, measures `unconditional_registry_map()` (`definitions.rs:3184`) —
and browser tools are **conditionally** registered, so the baseline table has no `browser_*` row at
all. Raising it would not account for anything this task adds; it would break the sum-equality guard
that makes the table and the total one fact. If that test goes red, something other than this task
moved, and the answer is to find that, not to raise the number.

⚠️ **Task 16 raises the same scalar first.** So Task 19 **re-measures from HEAD** — it never adds its
own delta to a number it read in a plan file or in Task 16's commit. Two tasks each adding a
computed delta to the same running scalar is how a ratchet ends up above the thing it measures, and
the slack it opens is credit already extended (判据 §13).

The protocol, in the order `definitions.rs:1891-1899` states it:

```bash
export CTD=/Volumes/TBU4/Workspace/aleph-target-dual-engine
# 1. BEFORE this task's append, on this branch's HEAD:
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$CTD cargo test -p alephcore --lib catalog_description_bytes_ratchet -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee /tmp/ratchet-before.log
# 2. make the append, then again:
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$CTD cargo test -p alephcore --lib catalog_description_bytes_ratchet -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee /tmp/ratchet-after.log
```

The test prints the measured total. Then:

1. **Record both totals and the delta**, each with the command and the commit it was measured on.
   The "before" number is HEAD's, not the constant's — the constant may already sit above the
   measurement, in which case part of this task's growth is free and the raise is smaller than the
   delta (or zero).
2. **Prune if the delta exceeds 400 B** — that threshold is the protocol's, not this plan's; read
   the doc comment for the exact figure and follow whatever it says. The first candidate to cut is
   "use it when a page renders wrong": a capable model does not need told when a page looks wrong,
   which is R9's first ruler. What must survive the pruning is the what-carries/what-does-not list,
   because it is the model's only statement of what a switch costs and nothing else in the tree
   says it.
3. **Add a dated three-question doc entry** beside the constant — what the bytes buy, why they
   cannot be pruned instead, who consumes them — and **name the platform** the measurement was taken
   on. That last part is not ceremony: `bash_exec`'s `DESCRIPTION` is `#[cfg]`-selected, so this
   scalar is one number guarding two sums and `cargo test` only ever measures the half the compiler
   built (recorded at FL §3.7's 打磨话术).
4. **Raise by the measured delta**, to the measured value, never to a rounded one:
   ```rust
   const CATALOG_DESCRIPTION_CEILING_BYTES: usize = <measured after-total>;
   ```
   If the after-total is **below** the current constant, do not raise it — the ratchet only goes
   down. Record that too.

**7d.** `qa/browser_dual/drive_switch.py`, mirroring Task 18's `drive.py` (its `sys.path` insert,
its `ps_lines` helper, and `qa_rpc`'s `Ledger`/`Rpc`):

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prove spec §5.3/§5.5 on two real engines: the login survives the switch.

Every claim here is one a fake engine cannot make. The load-bearing one is the
LAST: the source engine's process is gone. A switch that leaves the old browser
running looks identical to a correct one from every RPC angle.
"""
import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "browser_managed"))
from qa_rpc import Ledger, Rpc, ws_connect  # noqa: E402

# `ps_lines` carries the `--` reasoning (BSD pgrep reads a leading `-` in the
# pattern as its own option and then matches nothing, which reads exactly like
# "the process is gone"). Import it rather than writing a second wrapper.
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
from drive import ps_lines  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("ws")
ap.add_argument("--page-url", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--aleph-home", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--chromium-udd", required=True)
args = ap.parse_args()

led = Ledger()
log, check = Ledger.log, led.check
COOKIE = "aleph-qa-switch"
VALUE = "carried-%d" % os.getpid()
OBSCURA_PAT = f"--storage-dir={args.aleph_home}"


async def main():
    async with ws_connect(args.ws) as ws:
        rpc = Rpc(ws)
        await rpc.connect("qa-browser-dual-switch")

        ok, res = await rpc.invoke("browser_open", {"url": args.page_url, "profile": "default"})
        check("browser_open on the default profile succeeds",
              ok and res.get("success") is True, json.dumps(res)[:200])
        check("browser_open reports obscura", res.get("engine") == "obscura", str(res.get("engine")))

        before = ps_lines(OBSCURA_PAT)
        check("an obscura owns our storage dir before the switch", bool(before), str(before))

        ok, res = await rpc.invoke("browser_cookies", {
            "profile": "default", "action": "set",
            "name": COOKIE, "value": VALUE, "domain": "127.0.0.1", "path": "/",
        })
        check("a cookie is set on obscura", ok and res.get("success") is True, json.dumps(res)[:200])

        ok, res = await rpc.invoke("browser_tabs", {"profile": "default", "action": "list"})
        check("the tab list shows the page before the switch",
              args.page_url in json.dumps(res), json.dumps(res)[:200])

        ok, res = await rpc.invoke("browser_session", {
            "profile": "default", "action": "switch_engine",
            "engine": "chromium", "migrate": True,
        })
        # `ok` alone is not the claim: every arm of this tool returns
        # `success: false` inside an `ok` envelope for a refusal, so reading
        # only `ok` would call a refused switch a success and blame the wrong
        # step three claims later.
        check("switch_engine succeeds", ok and res.get("success") is True, json.dumps(res)[:300])
        check("it reports the engine it landed on",
              res.get("switched_to") == "chromium", str(res.get("switched_to")))
        check("it reports at least one cookie carried",
              (res.get("cookies_moved") or 0) >= 1, str(res.get("cookies_moved")))
        check("it returns the new page tree in the same call",
              bool(res.get("snapshot_text")), str(res.get("snapshot_text"))[:120])

        ok, res = await rpc.invoke("browser_cookies", {"profile": "default", "action": "list"})
        listed = json.dumps(res)
        check("the cookie set on obscura is readable on chromium",
              COOKIE in listed and VALUE in listed, listed[:300])

        ok, res = await rpc.invoke("browser_tabs", {"profile": "default", "action": "list"})
        check("the tab is on the same URL it was on before the switch",
              args.page_url in json.dumps(res), json.dumps(res)[:200])

        chrome = ps_lines(f"--user-data-dir={args.chromium_udd}")
        check("a chromium is now running", bool(chrome), str(chrome))

        # The load-bearing claim, and the only one invisible from the RPC face.
        after = ps_lines(OBSCURA_PAT)
        check("no obscura with our storage dir survives the switch",
              not after, f"before={before} after={after}")

        ok, res = await rpc.invoke("browser_session", {
            "profile": "default", "action": "switch_engine",
            "engine": "chromium", "migrate": True,
        })
        check("switching to the engine already running is refused, not reported as success",
              res.get("success") is False, json.dumps(res)[:200])

    return led.verdict()


sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
```

⚠️ The `--chromium-udd` claim assumes Task 18's config gives the `default` profile a Chromium
user-data-dir it can be switched to. Task 18 sets `CHROMIUM_UDD` for the `escape` profile
(`part-5-obscura.md:5030-5035`); if the switch's target dir differs, read the sidecar registry
(`$ALEPH_HOME/data/browser/chromium/default.json`) for the real one rather than guessing a path —
the same oracle `qa/browser_managed/drive_attach.py` already uses.

**QA mutations, each shown red once on the real machine:**

- Comment out `old.shutdown().await` → `no obscura with our storage dir survives the switch` reddens.
  This claim has no unit-test twin on real binaries.
- Make `import_state` skip `set_cookies` when `cookies.len() == 1` →
  `the cookie set on obscura is readable on chromium` reddens.
- Remove `--` from `ps_lines`' `pgrep` call and re-run on macOS → the survival claim must **not**
  silently pass. Task 18's helper already carries the `--`; this mutation confirms the import
  brought it rather than a local copy without it.

````markdown
- **第八轮（2026-09-06）——引擎决定反过来：obscura 成为默认内核、Chromium 降为逃生舱，两者藏在同一个 Aleph 自有的 CDP 客户端后面**。承接 spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-design.md`（D6 的落地），evidence 在同名 `-evidence/` 目录（`aleph-browser-map.md` 子系统地图 · `obscura-spike-v022.md` 实测 · `obscura-source-survey.md` 源码勘察）。**这一轮的头条不是「换了个浏览器」，是本仓第一次自己拥有页面表示**：模型看到的不再是某个外部 CLI 转述的 YAML/缩进树，而是 `src/browser/page_state/` 从 DOM ＋几何**一条推导**生成的空间状态树（文本渲染 + JSON + 带世代的 ref 表），两个引擎共用同一个 builder。下面 **①–④** 是本轮的四条裁定，**⑤–⑫** 是设计本身，**⑬–⑯** 是实测把设计推翻或收窄的地方，**⑰–⑱** 是装置，**⑲** 是交出去的上游工作，**⑳** 是**记录在案没做**的清单。
  - **① [裁定] 一个 CDP 客户端，不是两个。** `crates/aleph-cdp` 是零 Aleph 依赖的传输层（一条 websocket、多 session、逐命令超时、断连时把全部 pending 一次性失败）。**不引 `chromiumoxide`**（违 R3：为一个能力引一个重库，而我们要的只是「发一个 JSON 收一个 JSON」），**也不在 `src/browser/` 里再手写一份**。CLAUDE.md 的禁用清单因此多一行。判据 §1：两份 wire 客户端会各自实现一半的 session 路由，然后在第三个引擎出现时互相抵消。
  - **② [裁定] 不栅格化。** D6 附的那个悬而未决的问题——「是否干脆跳过栅格化，改用 DOM+布局 → 给模型的空间状态 JSON 树」——本轮答**是**。截图仍然可用（`browser_screenshot` 两个引擎都发 `Page.captureScreenshot`），但**模型的默认观测是 `PageState`**，不是像素。理由不是省 token（虽然确实省），是 `page_state/` 拿得到的东西比像素多：`rect=None` 是「这个元素不生成盒子」的**诚实答案**，而在一张图里它和「在视口外」长得一模一样。
  - **③ [裁定] `browser_session{switch_engine}` 是模型的动词，不是 harness 的启发式。** 没有任何确定性代码判断「这页渲染坏了」（违 R7），没有自动升级（违 R10 第 5 不）。硬件层只做三件事：把事实摆出来（能力表 + `EngineBusy` / `UnsupportedByEngine` / `EngineFailure` 三类错误各有**一个**拥有者）、提供动词、搬状态。ChatGPT 那套 `BrowserRequirement` 静态路由与「Browser Intelligence」**整类不做**，理由在 spec §5.7。
  - **③b [裁定] 能力表是**工具结果**，`DESCRIPTION` 里只有一句指路。** 「把事实摆出来」有两种做法，本轮选了后一种：把能力散文**渲染进** `DESCRIPTION`，还是让模型**问一次**。前者要求描述在运行时被生成，而 `AlephTool::DESCRIPTION` 是 `const`（`src/tools/traits.rs:69`）、`BUILTIN_TOOL_DEFINITIONS` 是 `const` 数组（`definitions.rs:73,81`），于是只剩「散文写成字面量 + 一条把它和表比对的守卫」——一套只为一句英文服务的机件，而且**每次会话都付一遍那些字节的钱**。落地是 `browser_session{action:"capabilities"}` 返回 `describe_for_tool()` 的文本外加一份 JSON，`DESCRIPTION` 里只留一句「要看每个引擎支持什么就问这个 action」。**全仓没有任何运行时生成的描述文本。** 这正是 R9 第二把尺问的那一句——「有没有一个工具拥有这句话」：有，而且它现在真的拥有它，不是抄了一份。⚠️ 代价写下来：能力事实从此**只对问过的模型可见**，一个不问就切引擎的模型拿不到它；换来的是那张表可以随引擎版本变化而不必每次都过一遍描述棘轮。
  - **③c [同一裁定的另一半] 「切换带走什么」不走那条路，它是散文。** `switch_engine` 的「带 / 不带」清单**是** `DESCRIPTION` 里的字面量，没有表也没有守卫——它描述的是一个设计决定（登录态活着、页面进度死了），不是某个运行时值的渲染，给三句话配一张常量表加一个渲染器加一条 `contains` 断言就是判据 §1 反过来用。**代价同样写下来**：`export_state`/`import_state` 以后若增删一个**类别**（sessionStorage、IndexedDB、历史栈），那句话就假了而**没有任何东西会红**。所以复核问句是固定的：**`MigrationState` 的字段数（今天三个）与那句话里「带」的分句数（今天三条）还相等吗**——判据 §6，数它，别记它。
  - **④ [裁定 R6] `switch_engine` 的审批默认与 `browser_open` 相同，并继承它。** `ActionType::BrowserSwitchEngine` 落在 curated 表里的值是 `DefaultDecision::Ask`——`BrowserOpen` 的那一个（`approval/config.rs:328`）——外加 `inherited_from() -> Some(BrowserOpen)`：**写过 `"browser_open"` 的策略文件不需要第二个键**，这正是「别造第二道没有把手的门」要的东西（判据 §14）。理由是这个动词做的事**多于**开一个标签页：它启动第二个浏览器进程，并把每一条 cookie 搬进去；给它比 `browser_open` 更松的默认不成立。⚠️ 一个更早的 spec 草稿曾把这一行写成「**默认放行**」，紧接着又写「它不比 `browser_open` 更危险」——同一句话里两个互相矛盾的分句，而后半句才是它真正的意思。**spec 自己已经改过来了**，所以这里记的是裁定，不是一次对现行 spec 的反驳；写下「spec 第 N 行说 X」这种叙述之前先去读那一行，判据 §1：引用一旦写下，被引用方的每一次修订都会让引用这一侧变成说谎的那一份。
  - **⑤ 两根正交的轴，不是一个枚举。** `driver`（谁驱动：`managed_cli` / `chrome_mcp` / **`cdp`**）与 `engine`（跑哪个进程：`obscura` / `chromium`）分开。旧配置的 `driver=managed_cli|chrome_mcp` **隐含** `engine=chromium`；`BrowserType` **不**长 `Obscura` 变体（它回答的是「Chrome 还是 Edge 还是 Brave」，obscura 不在那个族里）；`engine=obscura` × `driver≠cdp` 是一条**带修法文本的配置错误**，不是静默回落。自动注入的 `"default"` profile 改为 `engine=obscura, driver=cdp`；`"user"` 逐字不动（仍是 Chrome `ExistingSession`）。
  - **⑥ 引擎切换不持久化，而这是一个决定不是省事。** 运行中的进程本身就是状态，进程退出即回到配置默认。想改默认走既有的 `browser_profile` 工具（R8）。**不新增会话旋钮**——`SESSION_KNOBS.md` 那张表一行不加。
  - **⑦ 一个 `BrowserBackend` 实现服务两个引擎，分支只在三处。** `src/browser/cdp_backend/` 对两个引擎发同一批 CDP 命令；按引擎分叉的只有**几何抓取**（Chromium 走 `DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot`，obscura 走 `DOM.getDocument` + 批量 `DOM.getBoxModel`，理由见 ⑬）、**JS 对话框**（obscura 无）与**遮挡命中测试**。其余每一个动词两个引擎逐字节同路。
  - **⑧ `page_state/` 只有一个 builder。** 两个 fetcher（`fetch_chromium` / `fetch_obscura`）产出同一个 `RawDom`，`PageState::build` 是**唯一**把它变成模型看得见的东西的地方，由一条源码普查钉住（`page_state/` 之外恰好零个 `PageState::build(` 调用点）。可访问名（accname-lite）、role 推断、可交互性的多信号判定、文本渲染与 JSON 序列化全在这一条推导上，所以「两个引擎看到的页面不一样」在结构上说不出口。
  - **⑨ ref 带世代，失效有原因。** `RefTable` 按 `(frame_id, loader_id, backend_node_id)` 铸 ref，主框架的 `loaderId` 一变就整表重置；`resolve` 失败返回 `StaleReason::{Navigated, NodeGone, Unknown}` 而不是一个笼统的 false。`BrowserError::StaleRef` 的文本点名恢复动词（"re-run browser_snapshot"）。
  - **⑩ 两个引擎都是安装期外部运行时，走同一个台账。** `src/runtimes/specs.rs` 多一种安装策略 **`InstallStrategy::GithubRelease{repo, tag, asset, binary_in_archive}`**——用 `Shell` 拼 `curl | tar` 是第二个答案（判据 §1），所以它是一个类型。按 `os×arch` 选资产、对 GitHub API 的 `digest` 做 sha256 校验、校验不过就**拒绝并删除**、落到 `~/.aleph/runtimes/obscura/<tag>/`。`download_host` 与 Chromium 那条同名同义（本机需要它——release-assets 主机被 DNS 挡）。obscura 的 tag 钉在 spec 里（`v0.2.2`），上游 PR 合入后升 tag 就是台账的一次 `install`。
  - **⑪ `ChromiumLocator::locate()` 的签名变更，不是重命名。** 上一轮 ㉑ 把它单独标出来说「第二个引擎需要的是一次 SIGNATURE 变更」，本轮兑现：`EngineLocator::locate_all(&self) -> Vec<RuntimeRow>`，`runtime_manage{list}` 因此一次报出两个引擎，`runtime_manage{install, capability:"obscura"}` 走 ⑩ 那条策略。doctor 侧 `browser/chromium-missing` **保留原 id**（用户面 wire 值），旁边新增 `browser/obscura-missing`；`chromium_missing.rs` 改名 `engine_missing.rs` 后同时产出两条。
  - **⑫ 生命周期与孤儿回收从「Chromium 的」泛化成「引擎的」。** `ChromiumSidecar` → `EngineSidecar`（多一个 `engine` 字段，`#[serde(default)]` 让上一轮写下的、没有这个字段的记录仍读作 Chromium）；孤儿清扫按引擎选它要匹配的那个 flag（Chromium 是 `--user-data-dir=`，obscura 是 `--storage-dir=`），而**读 argv 的方式一个字不改**——上一轮 ⑰ 已经把它从「空格拼好的命令行 + `contains`」修成「`sysinfo::Process::cmd()` 的向量 + 整 token 相等」，这一轮只是给它第二种 flag。两个 daemon 退出点的回收覆盖面同样从「Chromium」扩到「每一个引擎句柄」，源码普查随之改名。
  - **⑫b 两个产物都跑两个引擎，而这句话是由一条普查背书的、不是由一段散文。** spec §6.5 承诺独立的 `aleph-server` 二进制与桌面 App 内置的那个 server 都能无头跑两个引擎（Panel 纯壳无关）。它今天成立的**唯一**理由是：`src/browser/engine/`、`src/browser/cdp_backend/`、`src/browser/page_state/`、`crates/aleph-cdp/src/` 这四处**没有任何 shell 相关的代码**——没有 `tauri`、没有 `aleph_desktop`、没有按产物分叉的 `cfg`。所以本轮**不写一句「两个产物都支持」的散文**（那种句子没有任何东西会让它变红，判据 §2），改成 Task 20 验收表里的一条 `rg` 普查：`rg -n "cfg\(target_os|cfg\(feature|tauri|aleph_desktop|desktop::" src/browser/engine/ src/browser/cdp_backend/ src/browser/page_state/ crates/aleph-cdp/src/` 期望 **0 行**（若 obscura 定位器真的需要一个 `cfg(windows)` 补 `.exe`，那条就是**唯一**被点名的命中，期望值改成 1，而这个数**从跑出来的结果里抄**）。⚠️ 这条普查的作用域是**方法**不是目录（判据 §18）：它证的是「这四处没有按产物分叉」，**不是**「两个产物都被真机跑过」——后者本轮**没有**做，`qa/browser_dual` 只在独立二进制上跑过，桌面 App 内置 server 零真机。
  - **⑬ [实测推翻设计] obscura 的 `DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot` 返回的是编造的几何，而它报成功。** 模块 doc 自己写着「Obscura has no layout/paint engine, so there is no real geometry to report. We synthesize it」，代码是 `let y = (i as f64) * 18.0; bounds.push(json!([0.0, y, 1280.0, 18.0]))`（`crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/domsnapshot.rs:231-236`），外加一份对**每一个**节点都声称 `visibility:visible, opacity:1, position:static` 的常量样式向量（`:200-214`）。`DOM.getBoxModel` 同族：JS 往返解析不出来时返回常量 quad `[8,8,108,8,108,28,8,28]`、`width:100,height:20`，**作为一次成功的应答**（`domains/dom.rs:322-327`, `:352-357`）。所以本轮的 `fetch_obscura` 是一条**写明有效期的临时路径**：`DOM.getDocument` + 逐节点 `DOM.getBoxModel`（有界并发）+ 一次 `Runtime.evaluate` 拿计算样式，两者**交叉核对**，不一致就把 `computed` 置 `None`（判据 §8：不一致只有资格说「我不知道」）。模块 doc 逐字写着「interim; delete when the ledger tag ≥ the release carrying the upstream DOMSnapshot fix」。上游那笔工作见 ⑲。
  - **⑭ [实测收窄设计] obscura 上有一道全局命令屏障，所以「换条路绕开卡顿」不是一个可用的动作。** 80 tick × 5 方法 = 400 个样本、0 错误：**全部**在三个时刻完成（`t≈25.75 s` 上 260 个、`t≈49.4 s` 上 4 个、`t≈70.5 s` 上 135 个），`Runtime.evaluate` / `DOM.getDocument` / `DOM.getBoxModel` / `Page.getLayoutMetrics` / `Target.getTargets` 每个方法在每个屏障上完成的条数**几乎逐一相等**。这不是逐调用成本，是**一个全局屏障一次性放行所有人**。设计里两条「哪条几何路更快」的推理因此全部作废，剩下的唯一动作是**把它说出来**：`cdp_command_timeout_secs` 默认 **30**（必须 `< 60`，因为 obscura 自己的 `OBSCURA_CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` 到 60 s 会**终结 isolate**——我们要在它开铡刀之前先自己回答），超时抬成 `BrowserError::EngineBusy{engine, method, waited_secs}`，文本点名 `browser_session{switch_engine}`，驱动**不重发**（重发只是再排一次同一个屏障的队）。
  - **⑮ [实测收窄设计] 一条连接看得见的 target，是它自己创建的那些。** obscura 每条 CDP 连接跑在自己的 OS 线程上、各持一份 `CdpContext`（`server.rs:824-829`），这是它避开 V8 跨线程 abort 的**机制**，不是疏忽。所以 `EngineHandle` **一个引擎一条连接**，所有 session 复用它；「另开一条连接看同一批 tab」在 obscura 上结构性不成立，能力表里 `multi_connection` 因此是 `Unsupported`，而不是留白。
  - **⑯ [实测] `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` 在 obscura 上不做 name-from-content。** `compute_name` 的顺序是 `aria-label` → `aria-labelledby` → `alt` → `title` → `placeholder` → （仅文本节点）自身文本（`domains/accessibility.rs:273-345`），没有「role 支持 name-from-content 时拼接后代文本」那一步，于是 `<a href=…>Foo</a>` 没有 name。这是 `page_state/accname.rs` 自己算可访问名、而不是问引擎要 AX 树的直接原因——顺带它也让两个引擎的名字由**同一段代码**产生（判据 §1）。
  - **⑰ [装置] `qa/browser_dual/run.sh` 八个阶段，两个真二进制。** `{provision,open,snapshot,click,stall,reap,caps,switch}`：台账真的装得下 obscura（含 digest 不符时**拒绝并删除**）· 冷启动到可导航 · `PageState` 在真页面上有 ref 有几何 · 按 ref 点击真的改变页面 · **`stall`** 把 ⑭ 那道屏障做成一条断言（一个页面脚本占住引擎，`EngineBusy` 必须在 `cdp_command_timeout_secs` 内说话且文本里有 `switch_engine`——**该阶段把这个旋钮配成 3 s**，不是产品默认的 30 s：实测 obscura 在自己的自主任务预算 ~5 s 就结束了那个忙循环，所以一道 30 s 的闸根本等不到它自己关上，那条断言会变成判据 §2 的恒绿）· `reap` 证明退出时两个引擎都被杀 · **`caps`** 对真二进制逐项探测能力表里的每一条声明（判据 §5：一张名单只覆盖立法当天的世界，这个阶段就是它的**到期检查**）· `switch` 见下。每一条守卫在提交前**变异过一次**并记下红的名字。
  - **⑱ [装置] `switch` 阶段的承重断言是「源引擎的进程没了」。** 在 obscura 上 set 一个 cookie、切到 chromium、断言 `browser_cookies{list}` 读得到它、断言当前 URL 与切换前一致、断言**没有任何带我们 `--storage-dir` 的 obscura 进程存活**。前三条从 RPC 面看得见，最后一条看不见——一个把旧引擎留着不关的切换，从每一个 RPC 角度看都和正确的那次一模一样（判据 §11）。`pgrep -f` 的模式以 `--` 开头，所以命令里**必须**有 `--` 分隔符，且 `pgrep` 返回 `0/1` 之外的码要当**探针自己坏了**处理而不是「没有进程」（判据 §8；上一轮 ⑲① 正是被 BSD pgrep 的这一点静默 no-op 掉的）。
````

```markdown
- **顺序地量一个会阻塞的东西，量到的是你自己的等待，不是它的行为** —— obscura 的 CDP 卡顿最初被量成「每次调用 19–26 s」，因为探针每 tick **await** 完上一批才发下一批：一个卡住的 tick 吃掉 40 s 窗口里的 25 s，两个 run 各只剩两行数据。改成**固定 500 ms、不等上一 tick** 的密集采样（80 tick × 5 方法 = 400 样本、0 错误）之后，真相立刻换了形状：400 个调用只在**三个时刻**完成——`t≈25.75 s` 上 260 个、`t≈70.5 s` 上 135 个——而五个方法在每个时刻完成的条数几乎逐一相等。那不是逐调用成本，是**一道全局屏障一次性放行所有人**，于是「换一条 CDP 路绕开卡顿」这个动作根本不存在。判据：**要区分「每次都慢」和「大家一起等」，就必须并发地量**；串行探针对后者结构性失明，而它给出的每一个数字看起来都像一个 RTT。配套两条：采样前先断言**页面身份**（早先一次 run 静默没导航成功，量到的是 `about:blank` 的 1–3 ms）；结论写「**完成时刻**」而不是「RTT」，因为 RTT 那一列在屏障下是线性倒数、读起来像别的东西 → §3.12 第八轮 ⑭
```

```markdown
### Web & Search
```

```markdown
### Browser — 26 tools, two engines, one driver

Every browser tool routes through `ProfileManager::get_backend` (`src/browser/manager.rs`), which
maps a profile's `driver` to a `BrowserBackend`. Since 2026-09-06 the default driver is `cdp`
(`src/browser/cdp_backend/`), which speaks CDP directly through the Aleph-owned client in
`crates/aleph-cdp` and serves **both** engines:

| axis | values | what it decides |
|---|---|---|
| `driver` | `cdp` (default) · `managed_cli` · `chrome_mcp` | who drives the browser |
| `engine` | `obscura` (default) · `chromium` | which process runs |

The two axes are orthogonal. A legacy `driver = "managed_cli"` or `"chrome_mcp"` implies
`engine = "chromium"`; `engine = "obscura"` with any driver other than `cdp` is a configuration
error carrying its own fix, not a silent fallback.

**The model's default observation is not a screenshot.** `browser_snapshot` returns a page-state
tree built by `src/browser/page_state/` from the DOM plus geometry — one builder, both engines —
carrying role, accessible name, states, rect and a generation-stamped `ref` per node. A `ref` dies
when the main frame's `loaderId` changes, and says why (`StaleRef{reason}`).

**Three tool faces carry the engine:**

| Tool | Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `browser_open` | `engine?` | one-shot: which engine to *start* for a cold profile. Refused, by name, if that profile already runs the other one — its cookies live in that process. |
| `browser_session` | `action:"capabilities"` | the per-engine support table, as a tool result: rendered text plus a JSON form, each row stamped with the engine version it was measured on. |
| `browser_session` | `action:"switch_engine", engine, migrate?` | move a live profile to the other engine, carrying cookies, tab URLs + scroll, and per-origin localStorage. Returns the new page tree; every earlier `ref` is dead. |

Engine capabilities are a constant table (`src/browser/engine/capability.rs`). It reaches the model
**as a tool result, not as description bytes** — `browser_session`'s `DESCRIPTION` carries one
sentence pointing at `action:"capabilities"`, and nothing in this tree generates description text
at runtime (`AlephTool::DESCRIPTION` is a `const`). The same table raises
`UnsupportedByEngine{engine, verb}` — the verb is named, so the model knows what it would be
switching for. `qa/browser_dual/run.sh caps` probes every row against the real binaries, which is
that table's expiry check.

### Generation
```

(end of the stale-lock paragraph) and line 23 (`## 日志轮转 (Log Rotation)`):

```markdown
## 浏览器引擎子进程 (Browser engine children)

Aleph 自己 spawn 浏览器（2026-09-05 起 Chromium，2026-09-06 起还有 obscura），而 `std::process::Child`
**不在 drop 时 kill**，驱动它的外部 CLI 又从来不是它的父进程。所以「谁负责关掉它」必须写下来：

- **sidecar 记录**：每一个被起起来的引擎在 `~/.aleph/data/browser/<engine>/<session-key>.json` 留一条
  `EngineSidecar{engine, pid, http_url, data_dir, build}`。它放在**一个注册表目录**而不是各自的 profile
  目录里——一个 profile 可以把 `user_data_dir` / `storage_dir` 指到任何地方，记录跟着走的话开机清扫就只
  扫得到「派生出来的那个根」，配过目录的 profile（本仓 QA 自己就配）永远扫不到（判据 §12：「有哪些浏览器
  要收」只能有一个推导点）。`engine` 字段带 `#[serde(default)]`，所以 2026-09-05 那一轮写下的、没有这个
  字段的记录仍读作 Chromium。
- **孤儿回收**：开机时按记录里的 pid 读 argv 并**整 token 相等**地比对我们自己那个 flag——Chromium 是
  `--user-data-dir=<path>`，obscura 是 `--storage-dir=<path>`。读的是 `sysinfo::Process::cmd()` 那个
  **argv 向量**，不是拼好的命令行：拼好的串上只表达得出 `contains`，而 `--user-data-dir=<root>/default`
  是活着的 `--user-data-dir=<root>/default-2` 的子串，于是这条检查会杀掉**邻居 profile** 的浏览器。探测
  结果是三态 `ArgvProbe{Absent, Unreadable, Argv}`，四条臂：匹配 → 杀并删记录；`Argv` 但不匹配（pid 被
  回收）→ 不杀、删记录；`Absent` → 删记录；**`Unreadable` → 什么都不做、记录留着**（Windows 上读不到
  argv 是常态，而「读不出来」不是「不在了」）。
- **退出时杀**：挂在**两个** daemon 退出点——有序停机（`start/mod.rs` 的 `run_until_shutdown` 返回处）与
  卡死兜底（`start/helpers.rs` 的 `std::process::exit(0)` 之前）。只挂前者的话，负载中的 `aleph-server stop`
  照样漏浏览器，而 `SHUTDOWN_FAILSAFE = 5 s` 正是为那种停机设的。规则不是预算：**SIGKILL + 有界回收，绝不
  做优雅握手**——不 SIGTERM-然后-等，不发 CDP `Browser.close`，不向一个可能正是停机卡死原因的进程发起往返。
- **代价，写下来而不是留给人发现**：被 SIGKILL 的 Chromium 一定在 profile 目录里留下 `SingletonLock` /
  `SingletonSocket` 与一个「did not shut down correctly」标记，下次启动可能弹恢复提示。本仓**没有**做宽限
  期，也**没有**清理陈旧 singleton 锁。

详见 [FEATURE_LOCATOR §3.12](FEATURE_LOCATOR.md) 第七轮 ⑯⑰ 与第八轮 ⑫。

```

Controller ruling, binding. The spec is this plan's **authority document**: the parts defer to it
wherever they disagree. So a ruling that overturned a spec sentence and left the sentence standing
makes the spec the stale half of a pair, and the stale half is the one a later reader believes
(判据 §1). Ten passages are in that state; this step is where the branch pays them. **The list grew twice while this step was open** (6i and 6j arrived after 6a-6h were written), which is itself the reason the verification below counts rather than asserts: a list of amendments is exactly the kind of thing that is one short (判据 §6).

**The house style for all eight** (the same one Step 3 uses on the ㉑ inventory): quote the current
sentence verbatim, **strike** the overturned clause, write the replacement beside it, and attach a
「由 plan ruling R*n* 更正」 note naming the ruling. **Never delete the struck text.** A spec that
silently reads as though it always said the right thing cannot be used to audit a plan against its
own reasoning — and the struck clause is what tells the next reader that a measurement, not a
preference, changed the answer.

Replace with (the second clause is carried through **unchanged** — it is still true and still the


**6i. `:251` (§5.6) — the `caps` stage probes five rows, and two it names no longer exist.**
Ruling **R39**.

R39: a capability-table row exists only if a `browser_*` verb dispatches the CDP method it
describes, **and the row's doc names that verb**. The table is published to the model, so a
verb-less row tells it Aleph can do something no tool can reach (判据 §9). Part 5 cut four rows on
that rule — `touch`, `screencast`, `network_interception`, `multi_connection` — and kept five.

Current:

```markdown
`qa/browser_dual/run.sh caps` 对真二进制逐项探测表里的每个声明（JS 对话框事件、拖拽事件、`Input.insertText`、screencast、第二连接、文件选择器…），任何一项与表不符即红。名单只覆盖立法当天的世界（判据 §5），这条守卫就是它的到期检查。表的每一行带「测于哪个版本」。
```

**7a. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-evidence/upstream/domsnapshot-real-layout.md`:**

````markdown
# Upstream deliverable 1 — `DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot` should report the real layout

> **This file is for a human to submit.** It is a PR description plus a patch *sketch* against the
> obscura clone at `/Volumes/TBU4/Github/obscura`, commit
> `72c84adcc6ec3ea4a7144adb4e45d4d3038ebcda` (2026-09-04, "Merge pull request #840 from
> h4ckf0r0day/fix/main-build-and-cdp-gaps"). It was written from a read-only survey and **has not
> been compiled** — this branch does not build obscura. Treat the code below as the shape of the
> change, not as a diff to apply blind. That clone had never been fetched since it was made, so
> re-read `domsnapshot.rs` before submitting.

## Title

`cdp: DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot should report real layout in render builds`

## Problem

`DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot` returns synthesized geometry, and says so itself
(`crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/domsnapshot.rs:1-16`):

> "Obscura has no layout/paint engine, so there is no real geometry to report. We synthesize it:
> every node gets a distinct, on-screen, non-icon-sized box (a simple vertical stack) … the
> coordinates are not real."

The implementation (`domsnapshot.rs:231-236`) is a vertical stack:

```rust
let y = (i as f64) * 18.0;
bounds.push(json!([0.0, y, 1280.0, 18.0]));
```

plus a constant style vector claiming `visibility:visible`, `opacity:1`, `position:static`,
`background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)` for **every** node (`domsnapshot.rs:200-214`).

That premise is no longer true for a build with the `render` feature. `obscura-render` computes a
real `DomLayout`, and the screenshot path already paints from it. But
`rg 'render|layout_dom|DomLayout' crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/domsnapshot.rs` finds nothing —
the CDP domain does not consult the render layer even when one exists.

The consequence for a CDP client is worse than a missing feature: the response is
**indistinguishable from a measurement**. Every consumer that reads `layout.bounds` (browser-use
does; so does anything that ports Chrome's snapshot path) receives a stack of 1280×18 rectangles
with correct-looking shape and no error to notice. A client cannot tell "this build has no layout
engine" from "this page really is a vertical stack of 18px rows".

The same shape exists in `DOM.getBoxModel` / `DOM.getContentQuads`
(`crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/dom.rs:322-327` and `:352-357`), which return the constant quad
`[8,8,108,8,108,28,8,28]`, `width:100, height:20` **as a successful response** whenever the JS
round trip returns something unparseable.

## Proposed change

In a `render` build, source `captureSnapshot`'s bounds and computed styles from the retained
`PreparedRender` the screenshot path already holds, so the snapshot and the pixels agree by
construction. In a non-render build, keep today's behaviour but make it legible — see "Smaller
alternative".

The accessors needed are already `pub` on `PreparedRender`: `crates/obscura-render/src/paint.rs:986`
`pub fn layout(&self) -> &crate::DomLayout`, `:991` `content_size`, `:995` `viewport_fixed_nodes`,
`:999` `sticky_layout`. `DomLayout` carries `rects: HashMap<NodeId, Rect>`,
`styles: HashMap<NodeId, LayoutStyle>` and `text_runs: HashMap<NodeId, Vec<(Rect, String)>>`, all
`pub`.

**The one missing piece is a way out of `obscura-js`.** `PreparedRender` lives in
`SharedState.prepared_render`, and `rg 'pub fn .*prepared' crates/obscura-js/src/runtime.rs` yields
only derived scalars (`prepared_content_size()`, `prepared_has_active_css_animations()`,
`screenshot_prepared*()`). `Page` mirrors exactly those
(`crates/obscura-browser/src/page.rs:3885-3931`).

### Sketch

1. `crates/obscura-js/src/runtime.rs` — hand the retained render out, the same way `with_dom`
   already hands out the DOM (`runtime.rs:3311`, which takes a `RefCell` borrow and no V8 scope):

   ```rust
   pub fn with_prepared_render<R>(
       &self,
       f: impl FnOnce(&crate::PreparedRender) -> R,
   ) -> Option<R> {
       let state = self.state.borrow();
       state.prepared_render.as_ref().map(f)
   }
   ```

2. `crates/obscura-browser/src/page.rs` — forward it, mirroring `Page::with_dom` (`page.rs:3566`):

   ```rust
   pub fn with_prepared_render<R>(
       &self,
       f: impl FnOnce(&obscura_render::PreparedRender) -> R,
   ) -> Option<R> {
       self.js.as_ref()?.with_prepared_render(f)
   }
   ```

3. `crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/domsnapshot.rs` — replace the synthetic stack with a lookup, and
   fall back to today's behaviour only when there is no retained render:

   ```rust
   // Before: bounds.push(json!([0.0, (i as f64) * 18.0, 1280.0, 18.0]));
   // After:
   let real = page.with_prepared_render(|pr| {
       let layout = pr.layout();
       node_ids
           .iter()
           .map(|nid| layout.rects.get(nid).map(|r| json!([r.x, r.y, r.width, r.height])))
           .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   });
   match real {
       Some(rects) => {
           for r in rects {
               // `None` == this node generates no box (display:none, detached).
               // Emit an EMPTY rect, which is what Chrome emits, rather than a
               // plausible one — being able to tell is the whole point.
               bounds.push(r.unwrap_or_else(|| json!([])));
           }
       }
       None => { /* today's synthetic stack, behind the module doc's caveat */ }
   }
   ```

   and source computed styles from `layout.styles` (`LayoutStyle` already carries display,
   visibility, opacity, position and transforms) instead of the constant vector at `:200-214`.

### Smaller alternative, if that is too large for one PR

Make the fabrication **legible on the wire** instead of removing it: add a non-standard
`"obscuraSynthesizedGeometry": true` to the `captureSnapshot` result whenever the layout is
synthesized, and to `getBoxModel`/`getContentQuads` when the constant quad is returned. That fixes
nothing, but it turns a silent fabrication into a fact a client can branch on — which is the
difference between "we cannot measure this" and "we measured this".

## What this is worth downstream

Aleph currently ships an interim fetcher (`src/browser/page_state/fetch_obscura.rs`) that walks
`DOM.getDocument` and issues one `DOM.getBoxModel` per node with bounded concurrency, then
cross-checks against a `Runtime.evaluate` of the computed style and drops the geometry when the two
disagree. That is slower than one `captureSnapshot`, and it is written to be deleted: its module
doc says "interim; delete when the ledger tag ≥ the release carrying the upstream DOMSnapshot fix."

## Evidence

Every line reference above comes from the read-only survey in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-evidence/obscura-source-survey.md`, §3
("Two geometry landmines over CDP") and §4 ("Direct Rust access to DOM + layout"), taken at
`72c84ad`.
````

**7b. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-evidence/upstream/barrier-issue.md`:**

````markdown
# Upstream deliverable 2 — issue: every CDP method stalls together behind one global barrier

> **This file is for a human to submit** as an issue on the obscura repository. Measured against
> **obscura 0.2.2** (the released binary, not a source build) on 2026-09-05/06. Raw data:
> `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-evidence/obscura-spike-v022.md` §M12/M12b;
> probe scripts in that directory's `probes/`.

## Title

`cdp: all methods stall together for 25-44s on a busy page, including Target.getTargets`

## Summary

On a large page, every CDP method this probe touched — `Runtime.evaluate`, `DOM.getDocument`,
`DOM.getBoxModel`, `Page.getLayoutMetrics`, `Target.getTargets` — stops answering at the same moment
and resumes at the same moment. It is not per-call cost and it is not serial queueing: 400 calls
issued on a fixed 500 ms schedule completed at **three instants**, and the number of calls each
method completed at each instant is essentially identical.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Start obscura (0.2.2 release build, render feature)
obscura serve --port=9444 --allow-private-network

# 2. Dense sampler: 80 ticks x 5 methods on a fixed 500 ms schedule, NOT awaiting the
#    previous tick. That last part is the whole measurement — see "Why the first
#    measurement was wrong".
node docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-browser-dual-engine-evidence/probes/m12e-dense.mjs \
  ws://127.0.0.1:9444/devtools/browser
```

The probe navigates to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)`, asserts page
identity (`location.href` contains `wikipedia.org`) before sampling — an earlier run silently
navigated nowhere and measured `about:blank` at 1-3 ms — resolves `<body>` after `loadEventFired`,
then samples.

## Result

400 samples, 0 errors, 0 unfinished. Completion instants, not round trips:

| completion instant (ms since load) | calls finishing there |
|---|---|
| 25,727 – 25,807 | 260 |
| 49,420 | 4 |
| 70,481 – 70,500 | 135 |

Per method, at each instant:

| method | @25.7–25.8 s | @49.4 s | @70.5 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Runtime.evaluate` | 51 (+1 at 26,015) | 0 | 27 |
| `DOM.getDocument` | 52 | 1 | 27 |
| `DOM.getBoxModel` | 52 | 1 | 27 |
| `Page.getLayoutMetrics` | 52 | 1 | 27 |
| `Target.getTargets` | 52 | 1 | 27 |

Every call issued between t=0 and t=25,500 completed at t≈25,750 **regardless of when it was
issued**, which is why the RTT column counts down linearly (25,727 / 25,248 / 24,749 / … / 306).
There are two barriers on this page: ~25.8 s starting at load, and a second ~44 s one starting at
t≈26.5 s. The only sample that escaped is one `Runtime.evaluate` issued at t=26,000 — in the 250 ms
gap between the two barriers — which returned in **15 ms** while its four tick-mates were caught by
the second barrier and waited 23.4 s.

A separate run also showed the stall is not one bounded window after load: a connection that sat
**idle for 45 s** paid 19.4 s on its first touch afterwards.

## Why the first measurement was wrong, in case it matters for triage

The first version of this probe awaited each tick's five calls before issuing the next, so a stalled
tick ate 25 s of a 40 s window and each run produced two usable rows. That version reported "19-26 s
per call", which reads like per-call cost and points at the wrong mechanism entirely. The barrier
only becomes visible with **concurrent** sampling. Any triage that reproduces this serially will be
measuring its own waiting.

## What is NOT measured

The binary was not instrumented, so this issue **cannot say which lock it is**. The source survey
notes `ctx.v8_lock` (`crates/obscura-cdp/src/dispatch.rs:125`), taken by every method outside the
`is_v8_free_method` allowlist (`dispatch.rs:653-717`), and observes that `Target.getTargets` and
`Page.getLayoutMetrics` appear to be *on* that allowlist yet stall anyway — so either the allowlist
is not protecting them in practice at 0.2.2, or the shared resource is something else. The 15 ms
`Runtime.evaluate` sitting beside a 23 s `DOM.getDocument` in the same tick is evidence against both
a pure single-V8-lock story and pure head-of-line blocking on the socket.

## Why it matters downstream

The per-command watchdog (`OBSCURA_CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 60,000 ms,
`dispatch.rs:766-780`) bounds the stall by **terminating the isolate**. A client that wants to
survive the barrier must therefore answer before 60 s and treat the wait as a fact about the engine
rather than an error — which is what we do (30 s per-command timeout, surfaced as a typed "engine
busy" the model can act on). But the barrier also means "issue the geometry call on a different CDP
path to dodge the stall" is not an available move for any client, which is worth knowing before
someone designs around it.
````

```markdown
## Handoff (Task 20)

3. **`fetch_obscura.rs` is written to be deleted.** Its module doc names the condition: the ledger
   tag reaching the release that carries the upstream `DOMSnapshot` fix. The PR text for that fix is
   in `-evidence/upstream/domsnapshot-real-layout.md` and **the user submits it** — this repo does
   not open PRs elsewhere. The barrier issue in the same directory is the same kind of hand-off.
4. **`cdp_command_timeout_secs` must stay under 60.** obscura's own
   `OBSCURA_CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` terminates the isolate at 60 s; our 30 s default exists so we
   answer before it does. Raising ours past that trades a typed `EngineBusy` for a killed page.
5. **The `caps` QA stage is the capability table's expiry check, not a duplicate of it.** If it goes
   red, the table is stale — the upstream engine moved. Update the table and its "measured on"
   stamp; do not relax the stage.
6. **`switch_engine`'s approval default is `Ask` and inherits `browser_open`** (ruling R6). An
   early spec draft said 默认放行; the spec itself was corrected before this plan was assembled, so
   there is nothing left to reconcile — but the reasoning is worth reading before touching the value,
   in FL §3.12 第八轮 ④.
7. **UNRUN stages on this machine**: 〈list, with the reason for each〉. They are not passes.
```
